\section{n9. Full smooth BFJ specialization on all semivaluations}
\textit{Earlier local supports: n1, n3, n8.}

Use n1, n3 and n8. The published BFJ application in this note is ONLY at the closed point of a smooth affine variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Dimension at least two is treated by BFJ; dimensions one and zero are treated directly below. No characteristic-free singular resolution is inferred.

The complete used units of Boucksom--Favre--Jonsson, Valuations and plurisubharmonic singularities, were checked from the bound publication: the setting; semivaluations and primary profiles; simple modifications, simplices, and retractions in Sections 1.2--1.7; Definitions 2.1 and 2.5, Proposition 2.2, and 2.7--2.8; 3.6--3.14; and the complete proofs of 3.9--3.10 through 3.18 and 3.22--3.25. The historical smooth resolution, usual multiplier ideal subadditivity, and smooth Izumi inputs remain disclosed published background. BFJ's nef Weil cone is its weak closed cone generated by formal-ideal divisors; its formal psh functions are finite and strongly continuous on quasi-monomials and have that nef coefficient divisor. They extend to ALL semivaluations by
\[
H_W(v)=\inf_\pi H_W(r_\pi v).
\]
Proposition 2.7 says H\_W<=H\_W composed with r\_pi; the composed functions decrease under refinement. The projective-limit statement 1.13 applies to the all-support compact semivaluation space, not just fraction-field valuations.

Proposition 3.11 proves substantive continuity on each CLOSED simplex. Its proof uses multiplier profiles h\_k=(1/k)log|L\textasciicircum{}2(kW)| and the estimate |h\_k-H\_W|<=A/k on divisorial points. Thinness A is bounded on each closed simplex. The continuous multiplier profiles are consequently uniformly Cauchy there, and their limit supplies the continuous extension, including its faces. One must not substitute the false assertion that a finite convex function is automatically continuous at the boundary of a closed simplex.

Correct 3.13 as follows. For a nonzero formal psh g, define, for integers j>=1,
\[
B_j=L^2(2^j g)+\widehat{\mathfrak m}^{\,4^j},\qquad
g_j=2^{-j}\log|B_j|=\max\{2^{-j}\log|L^2(2^jg)|,-2^j\}.
\]
The exponents were checked visually in the actual PDF on printed page 475. Subadditivity 3.10 gives the decreasing first term, and 3.9 gives convergence to g at every quasi-monomial. The truncation also decreases. The ideals contain a boundary power but early terms can be the unit ideal. Nonzero g has g(ord\_m)<0 by 3.14, and 3.9 at ord\_m makes the multiplier profile strictly negative there for all large j. Thus B\_j is EVENTUALLY proper primary; discard a finite prefix. For g=0 use the UNIT ideal, not a sequence of proper primary ideals decreasing to zero. The identically bottom function is not a finite formal psh function on quasi-monomials; add it separately by -N=-v(m\textasciicircum{}N).

The approximants decrease to g on ALL semivaluations. Given finite t>g(v), choose a retraction with g(r\_pi v)<t by the definition of the all-retraction infimum, even when g(v) is bottom. Then choose j with g\_j(r\_pi v)<t. The formal-psh inequalities give
\[
g(v)\le g_j(v)\le g_j(r_\pi v)<t.
\]
This proves full convergence; it is not merely divisorial or quasi-monomial convergence. N1 contracts each completed primary B\_j exactly to R, preserving the profile. The completed unit also contracts to the unit. Thus every BFJ function, with bottom adjoined, belongs to D\_R, and every finite continuous BFJ function belongs to C\_R by the compact decreasing-continuous uniform-convergence argument (Dini's open-cover proof).

Conversely any finite real primary profile is BFJ formal psh, since its coefficient divisor is nef and its evaluation is continuous on simplices; principalization and the published retractions give its canonical all-semivaluation extension. Let g be a uniform limit of such profiles. Its divisorial coefficients give a finite weak limit W in BFJ's closed nef cone. Proposition 3.11 gives H\_W. Uniform convergence on quasi-monomials shows g=H\_W there: they agree on dense divisorial points of each simplex and both are continuous there. Moreover the same uniform error estimate survives taking the infimum over ALL retractions. Thus g(v)=inf\_pi H\_W(r\_pi v) at every semivaluation. This proves C\_R is EXACTLY the finite continuous BFJ subclass.

Now let g=inf\_i g\_i be a decreasing C\_R-net. BFJ 3.14 gives g\_i(v)<=g\_i(ord\_m) at every v (first on quasi-monomials, then by retractions). If g(ord\_m) is bottom, g is bottom everywhere. Otherwise 3.14 also gives C(v)g\_i(ord\_m)<=g\_i(v) at every quasi-monomial v, so g is finite there. Its divisorial coefficients give a finite weak-nef W. On a simplex the decreasing limit g is finite convex. For any point x take its MINIMAL face; x lies in that face's relative interior, where finite convex functions are continuous. H\_W is continuous on the whole face by the actual 3.11 theorem. Their equality on the dense rational divisorial points of that relative interior proves equality at x. Vertices are already divisorial. This handles every face without asserting closed-simplex continuity from convexity alone.

Finally, extended infima commute over the Cartesian product of the net and ALL models:
\[
g(v)=\inf_i\inf_\pi g_i(r_\pi v)
=\inf_\pi\inf_i g_i(r_\pi v)
=\inf_\pi H_W(r_\pi v).
\]
No arbitrary decreasing-net flattening principle is used. Hence D\_R minus the identically bottom function is exactly the full BFJ formal psh class with its canonical extension to all semivaluations. D\_R is that class with bottom adjoined, and n8 gives the same statements for D\_geom and C\_geom.

For a smooth DVR every nonempty normalized boundary is a singleton. Primary ideals are powers of the parameter, so C is all finite nonpositive constants and D all extended nonpositive constants. The closed point itself is an effective Cartier divisor, and degree conditions on contracted curves are empty, giving the same independent geometric core. In dimension zero the centred boundary is empty and all statements mean its unique empty function. General primary gauges in the BFJ range follow n1's exact homogeneous cocycle, with bounded positive denominators preserving uniform and decreasing convergence. Completion homeomorphism and primary contraction apply without claiming equivalent model categories.

\section{n10. Nonisolated cusp: separation from the entire finite-real raw cone}
\textit{Earlier local supports: n1, n3, n4, n8.}

Use n1, n3, n4 and n8. Work in characteristic zero, with
\[
R=k[t^2,t^3,z]_{(t^2,t^3,z)},\quad S=k[t,z]_{(t,z)},\quad
\mathfrak a=(t^2,t^3,z),\quad \mathfrak c=t^2S.
\]
Indeed S is finite via t, is normal, and has the same fraction field. R consists of polynomials with no term of t-degree one, localized at the stated maximal ideal; multiplying by t shows its conductor is exactly t\textasciicircum{}2S. The quotient R/c is k[z] localized, and S/c is its square-zero t-thickening. Their all-semivaluation boundaries are the same singleton when nonempty. N1 therefore makes restriction V\_\{aS\}(S) to V\_a(R) a continuous bijection and hence a homeomorphism, including the support (t) upstairs. This is a two-dimensional nonisolated cusp, not just a finite curve link.

Write s=w(t), u=w(z), b=z+t and B=w(b); min(2s,u)=1. Allow s,u,B to be infinite whenever the normalization permits. The bounded continuous positive profile
\[
A(w)=w((b,t^2))=\min\{B,2s\}
\]
descends topologically. For k>=1 define actual downstairs ideals
\[
K_k=(b^k(z-kt),\ t^2b^k,\ t^{2k+2})\subset R.
\]
The first generator has zero t-linear coefficient: the two contributions k z\textasciicircum{}k and -k z\textasciicircum{}k cancel. The other two have t-degree at least two. Localizations do not change membership. The ideals are proper primary: the last generator puts t\textasciicircum{}2 and t\textasciicircum{}3 in the radical, and the first then puts z in it.

For EVERY normalized semivaluation, every generator has value at least kA. For the first this is kB+w(z-kt)>=kA, and the other two are immediate. The upper bound is a complete case analysis. If A=2s<=B, cancellation forces s=u=1 (different values would give B=min(s,u)<2s), and the last generator has value kA+2. If A=B<2s and s<=u, normalization gives s<=1, and the second generator has value kA+2s<=kA+2. If s>u, including s infinite, then u=1 and B=w(z-kt)=1; the first generator has value kA+1. The case u infinite belongs to the second case. Thus on ALL supports, including cancellation and infinite coordinates,
\[
0\le v(K_k)/k-A\le2/k.
\]
Hence -A lies in C\_R, and is a normalization-raw profile in N\_R. This analytic bound is a proof; a finite sample check is only a diagnostic.

We separate A from the ENTIRE finite REAL positive raw cone P\_R, not merely rational single-ideal profiles. Let w\_infty kill t and give z value one. Let w\_star be the monomial valuation in coordinates (t,b) with weights (1,2); then z=b-t has value one, so both valuations are in the same primary section. They give A(w\_infty)=1 and A(w\_star)=2.

For ANY proper primary downstairs ideal I, put d=w\_infty(I), a positive integer. Choose f in I attaining d; its local denominator is a unit at both valuations. Expand in k[[t,z]]: no coefficient of t-degree one occurs. Its degree-d homogeneous part has nonzero z\textasciicircum{}d coefficient and zero t z\textasciicircum{}\{d-1\} coefficient. In characteristic zero it cannot be a scalar multiple of b\textasciicircum{}d=(z+t)\textasciicircum{}d. After substituting z=b-t, it therefore contains a nonzero term t\textasciicircum{}\{d-j\}b\textasciicircum{}j with j<d. That monomial has w\_star-value d+j<=2d-1. Terms of other total degrees cannot cancel it, since the linear substitution preserves total degree. If other terms have still smaller value they only strengthen the bound. Consequently
\[
w_\star(I)<2w_\infty(I).
\]
Every nonzero finite real positive combination of proper primary gauges retains this strict inequality; unit terms are zero. But A has equality. Thus A is outside P\_R, and -A is outside Q\_R. We have proved N\_R is not Q\_R and C\_R is not Q\_R in this example. Their uniform closures still agree by n4. This does not assert raw geometric and ideal equality.

\section{n11. Rejected shortcuts and the radial scope constraint}
\textit{Earlier local supports: n1, n2, n3, n4, n8, n10.}

Use n1--n4, n8 and n10. These are diagnostics, not extra hypotheses.

An incompatible-contraction shortcut is false even over a smooth normal surface. Inject A=k[x,y]\_(x,y) diagonally into A times A and take J=((x,y\textasciicircum{}2),(x\textasciicircum{}2,y)). Then I\_N=J\textasciicircum{}N intersect A=(x,y\textasciicircum{}2)\textasciicircum{}N intersect (x\textasciicircum{}2,y)\textasciicircum{}N. The m-order of both fibre ideals is one. A monomial x\textasciicircum{}a y\textasciicircum{}b belongs to I\_N exactly when 2a+b>=2N and a+2b>=2N. Summing gives a+b>=ceil(4N/3); balanced nonnegative exponents with that sum achieve both inequalities. Therefore
\[
\operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak m}(I_N)=\lceil4N/3\rceil,
\]
whose normalized limit is 4/3, not one. The two ideal profiles were not fibre constant. No general contraction-as-fibre-minimum formula is used in n4--n6.

The literal positive-gauge inequality in BdFFU Proposition 2.4(b) has the wrong sign. At a smooth surface take parameters x and b=x+y, and the monomial valuation v(x)=1, v(b)=2. On the first-blowup dual complex its retraction is ord\_m. For I=(x+y,x\textasciicircum{}3), v(I)=2 whereas r(v)(I)=1. Hence the printed inequality r(v)(I)>=v(I) fails. The negative function -v(I) has the expected opposite inequality. Complete Definition 2.1--2.2 and Proposition 2.4 with proof were read from the bound BdFFU paper, solely for this diagnostic. Its own normal complex-variety hypotheses do not repair the sign. It supplies no premise of the construction.

The geometric boundary cone is not asserted to be the cone of literal CLD or classical logarithmic radial extensions. On a nodal curve R=k[x,y]\_(x,y)/(xy), its finite normalization has two DVR centres. The tuple (-1,0) is in C\_S and is fibre compatible: the conductor has finite positive value on both boundary points, so its restriction has no identified pair. N4 therefore puts (-1,0) in C\_R, and n8 puts it in C\_geom. For a classical analytic node with two normalized discs, a literal zero logarithmic slope on one disc forces the nodal value to be at least zero by upper semicontinuity. The other literal negative slope tends to minus infinity at its origin. If its nodal value is at least zero, the subharmonic maximum principle on that disc (the outer-circle value is zero and interior values are negative) forbids the resulting interior maximum. Thus this mixed-zero profile cannot be a literal classical psh radial extension. The original dossier's corresponding CLD closed-disc obstruction is kept as a scope constraint, not silently overridden or used as a theorem premise. We make no CLD comparison theorem for other singular germs. A boundary trace of a different kind is a separate question.

# Exact scope

The construction is for every excellent local germ, after reduction, with a nonempty intrinsic centred ray boundary when the local reduction has positive dimension. Sections use arbitrary proper primary ideals. Nonminimal prime supports and infinite function values are retained. Zero-dimensional local reduction gives the empty boundary. For nonreduced germs this is a semivaluation theory of the reduction; nilpotent intersection multiplicities are not supplied.

The independent geometric core uses actual primary blowups of the reduced germ, actual negative effective finite real Cartier presentations, and degree >=0 on every contracted proper integral curve. Common product-ideal blowups identify presentations. There is no assertion that this system is cofinal in all proper birational models, no nonnormal Weil-coefficient substitute for Cartier effectivity, and no arbitrary-characteristic resolution assertion. The uniform and actual decreasing completions are justified by the proved comparison C_geom=C_ideal and D_geom=D_ideal; core positivity is geometric before that comparison.

P is the finite REAL positive ideal cone; Q=-P; C is its finite continuous uniform closure; D consists of actual decreasing C-nets with bottom allowed. N is the normalization-RAW compatible cone. Q subset N subset C, and both uniform closures equal C. The nonisolated cusp separates N and C from Q. No raw equality is asserted.

Primary-gauge changes are the exact homogeneous cocycle u_b(v/v(b))=u_a(v)/v(b), with bounded positive denominator. Completion is an all-semivaluation homeomorphism with exact primary contraction. \section{n3. New exact separable coefficient-field descent gives all continuous envelopes on finite smooth quotients over any characteristic-zero field.}
\textit{Supports: G331, n1, n2.}

NEW algebraic-field descent, proved independently. Let k be any field, let (R,m) be a positive-dimensional normal domain essentially of finite type over k with residue field EXACTLY k, and assume geometric integrality and geometric normality. Fix primary a. Let k\textasciicircum{}s be a separable closure and put R\_s=R tensor\_k k\textasciicircum{}s. It is the local ring at the corresponding rational point: for every finite Galois E/k, R\_E=R tensor\_k E is finite free and has a unique maximal ideal, since R\_E/mR\_E=E and every maximal ideal in a finite integral algebra lies over m. The directed union is local, and is the corresponding finite-type localized k\textasciicircum{}s algebra, hence Noetherian excellent normal. Geometric hypotheses are explicit; no assertion about arbitrary excellent germs or completions is made. All semivaluation supports are retained.

Write X\_E=V\_(aR\_E)(R\_E), X\_s=V\_(aR\_s)(R\_s), and Gamma=Gal(k\textasciicircum{}s/k). G331 supplies surjective restriction at every finite stage. There is an actual homeomorphism X\_s=lim\_E X\_E: a compatible tuple defines a semivaluation on the union, satisfies the axioms and a-normalization there, and conversely every semivaluation restricts. Coordinates belong to a finite stage, so the topology is exactly the inverse-limit topology. Compactness and finite-stage surjectivity prove rho:X\_s-\textgreater{}X=V\_a(R) is continuous surjective, also at nonminimal supports. One can see surjectivity by the finite-intersection property for the nonempty compact finite-stage fibres.

Every rho-fibre is a FULL Gamma orbit. Indeed R\_E\textasciicircum{}Gal(E/k)=R: expand in a k-basis of E and impose invariance, or use the trace-dual coefficient argument below. Its generic extension is Galois of degree [E:k] by geometric integrality and n2's fixed-field proof. Thus G331's full-support normal-target coefficient trace identifies each finite-stage fibre with a full Gal(E/k) orbit. Given w,w' in the same infinite fibre, let C\_E be the set of gamma in Gamma for which their E-restrictions agree after gamma. Each C\_E is nonempty clopen, because finite-field automorphisms extend to k\textasciicircum{}s and the fibre is an orbit. Finite intersections contain C\_F for a common finite Galois F. The profinite compactness of Gamma gives a common gamma. This proves full transitivity, not merely transitivity on original-field valuations. Gamma is the inverse limit of the finite Galois groups; its compactness and restriction surjectivity are ordinary separable field theory, and the finite-intersection argument is supplied here.

Here is COMPLETE ideal descent, avoiding an infinite average. For finite Galois E/k choose a k-basis e\_j and trace-dual c\_i with Tr(c\_i e\_j)=delta\_ij. Nondegeneracy can be proved without an extra theorem: n2's evaluation-matrix fixed-field proof gives a basis whose matrix M=(sigma(e\_j)) is invertible. The trace Gram matrix is M\textasciicircum{}t M, with determinant (det M)\textasciicircum{}2 nonzero; its entries lie in k. Thus a trace-dual basis exists, also when the characteristic divides the group order. If an ideal I\_E in R\_E is Galois-stable and s=sum\_j r\_j e\_j belongs to it, then sum\_sigma sigma(c\_i s)=r\_i belongs to I\_E intersect R. Hence I\_E=(I\_E intersect R)R\_E.

If an ideal I\_s in R\_s is Gamma-stable, choose a finite Galois E containing its finite set of generators and let I\_E be the generated ideal. R\_s is faithfully flat over R\_E (field extension), so I\_s intersect R\_E=I\_E. Every automorphism of E extends to Gamma, and stability of I\_s forces stability of I\_E. Finite descent therefore gives I\_s=(I\_s intersect R)R\_s. This proves the assertion on the entire Noetherian algebra, not just on a generic field. Primary and unit ideals retain their type: proper primary ideals contain a power of m\_s=mR\_s, and faithful contraction contains a power of m and remains proper.

For any finite continuous signed f on X, put F=f composed with rho. The source canonical B\_m=A\_m\textasciicircum{}(R\_s)(F) is Gamma-stable by its all-support definition. Restriction surjectivity proves B\_m intersect R=A\_m\textasciicircum{}R(f). Ideal descent now gives the exact EVERY-degree identity

 B\_m=A\_m\textasciicircum{}R(f)R\_s,  h\_m\textasciicircum{}(R\_s)=rho\textasciicircum{}*h\_m\textasciicircum{}R,
 direct-sum B\_m t\textasciicircum{}m=(direct-sum A\_m\textasciicircum{}R t\textasciicircum{}m) tensor\_k k\textasciicircum{}s.

Taking the raw supremum identity of n1 proves rho\textasciicircum{}*p\_R(f)=p\_(R\_s)(F), WITHOUT first assuming either envelope continuous. Continuity of either raw envelope is equivalent to continuity of the other: pullback preserves continuity, and continuous fibre-constant functions descend through the compact quotient rho. The uniform criterion of n1 then proves positivity in C whenever continuous. Sup norms and all uniform canonical error bounds are preserved exactly, without a field-degree loss. Finite generation of the two canonical algebras is also equivalent: if the source is generated in degrees \textless{}=D, the multiplication maps from base degrees \textless{}=D become surjective after faithfully flat extension, hence were already surjective; finitely many generators of those Noetherian ideals suffice. The reverse is base extension. This is an equivalence, not general finite generation.

For completeness the positive continuous cone itself descends: rho\textasciicircum{}*C\_R is precisely the Gamma-invariant subclass of C\_(R\_s). Pullback is an isometry and preserves C,D by primary ideal extension and actual limits. If H in source C is invariant, approximate it uniformly within epsilon by -w(I)/r. Descend its generators and primary-power containment to finite Galois E. Replace I\_E by I'\_E=sum\_sigma sigma(I\_E), whose profile is the maximum of its translates and is within epsilon of H on every source point, by Gamma invariance. I'\_E is stable, unit or proper primary. The trace-dual proof descends it to J in R, giving the approximant -v(J)/r downstairs. Compact quotient descent and these uniform approximants put H in C\_R. No assertion that arbitrary invariant D nets automatically descend through an infinite extension is needed or made.

Actual NEW CE application: in characteristic zero k\textasciicircum{}s is an algebraic closure. Let a finite group G act faithfully by k-linear transformations on k[x\_1,...,x\_n], preserving the origin, and take R=(k[x]\textasciicircum{}G) at its origin. The same result holds for any such geometrically normal rational germ whose algebraic-closure ring has the finite smooth-quotient presentation of n2. In the displayed linear case, invariants commute with field extension: the fixed-subspace equations on each finite-dimensional polynomial degree piece commute with tensoring, and localization commutes by invariant orbit denominator products. The invariant ring is finite type and k[x] finite over it: each variable satisfies its monic orbit polynomial, giving finiteness over the finite coefficient subalgebra; the invariant ring is its Noetherian submodule. All nonleading orbit-polynomial coefficients vanish at the origin, so modulo the invariant origin ideal every variable is nilpotent. Thus the origin is the unique centre above it, and the localized smooth cover is actually finite local. Normality follows from the integral invariant-fraction argument in n2, and the same argument after any field extension gives geometric normality and integrality. Thus R\_s is the exact algebraically closed characteristic-zero finite smooth quotient of n2. That note applies BFJ ONLY there. Our independently proved full-fibre and ideal descent now gives a greatest continuous geometric C/D envelope for EVERY finite continuous signed obstacle on R over ANY characteristic-zero field k.

For each signed REAL Cartier obstacle on an ACTUAL primary model, G331's section formula is a finite signed primary combination. Its scalar pullback is therefore a model obstacle in n2. The n2 quotient O(1/m) full-degree canonical estimate transfers EXACTLY to R through the every-degree identity above. The constant may depend on the geometric source model and obstacle; there is no field-extension-degree factor or finite-generation hypothesis. Exact primary-gauge changes leave all canonical ideals unchanged and divide errors by the positive gauge denominator.

In particular k=Q and R=Q[a,b,c,z\_1,...,z\_r]\_(a,b,c,z)/(ac-b\textasciicircum{}2), r\textgreater{}=1, are actual normal nonisolated germs covered by the theorem. The same nonlinear signed primary obstacle and two cancellation-sensitive valuations in n2 exist over Q. \subsection*{Expanded field-descent equalities}
The infinite group is used by finite clopen compatibility conditions:
\[
 X_{k^s}=\varprojlim_E X_E,\qquad
 \bigcap_E C_E\ne\varnothing,\qquad
 \rho^{-1}(v)=\Gamma\cdot w.
\]
Trace-dual extraction on a stable ideal is an actual ring identity:
\[
 s=\sum_jr_je_j\in I_E\ \Longrightarrow\
 r_i=\sum_{\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(E/k)}\sigma(c_is)
 \in I_E\cap R.
\]
It uses separability, not division by the group order. In particular it
also applies when the field characteristic divides that order. It yields
\[
 A_m^{R_{k^s}}(\rho^*f)=A_m^R(f)R_{k^s},\qquad
 h_m^{R_{k^s}}=\rho^*h_m^R,\qquad
 p_{R_{k^s}}(\rho^*f)=\rho^*p_R(f).
\]
Unlike a coefficient norm approximation, this carries the canonical
degree $m$ itself unchanged. The characteristic-zero application is a
descent theorem proved here, after using the published smooth theory
only over the algebraic closure. It is not an enlarged citation of BFJ.

\section{n4. New all-support geometric cone and envelope invariance for finite and specified infinite Frobenius-root extensions.}
\textit{Supports: G331, n1, n3.}

NEW Frobenius-root invariance on the entire geometric envelope class. Let R subset S be an injective finite local extension of excellent reduced positive-dimensional rings of characteristic p\textgreater{}0. Assume a fixed q=p\textasciicircum{}e satisfies s\textasciicircum{}q in R for EVERY s in S. This hypothesis holds when R is a normal domain, S a finite domain, and Frac(S)/Frac(R) is finite purely inseparable: choose q killing that extension; s\textasciicircum{}q lies in Frac(R), is integral over R and hence lies in R. No perfection, F-finiteness, CM, Q-Gorenstein or resolution hypothesis is imposed. This is a proved envelope transport theorem; it supplies no unproved positive-characteristic regularity input.

Fix a primary ideal a in R. Restriction rho:V\_(aS)(S)-\textgreater{}V\_a(R) is an actual homeomorphism with inverse

 w(s)=v(s\textasciicircum{}q)/q, including infinity/q=infinity.

The formula has w|R=v. Frobenius additivity (s+t)\textasciicircum{}q=s\textasciicircum{}q+t\textasciicircum{}q and multiplicativity prove the semivaluation axioms. Because aS is primary and w(aS)=1, the source maximal ideal has positive finite value. For example n\textasciicircum{}N subset mS subset n gives 0\textless{}w(m)/N\textless{}=w(n)\textless{}=w(m)\textless{}infinity. Supports are determined by s\textasciicircum{}q in supp(v), including nonminimal supports. Any lift must have this value by multiplicativity, so it is unique. Both maps are continuous by coordinate evaluations and scalar division, or by compact bijection. This proves full fibre compatibility rather than assuming generic inseparability controls every support.

The independently geometric classes C and D are isometrically identical under rho. One may invoke G331's full finite-injection positive descent since every fibre is singleton, but there is also an explicit ideal proof. If I=(s\_1,...,s\_l) is unit or proper primary in S, put J=(s\_1\textasciicircum{}q,...,s\_l\textasciicircum{}q) in R. Then v(J)=q w(I) on EVERY support. If I contains (aS)\textasciicircum{}N, raising any expression x=sum\_i s\_i u\_i for x in a\textasciicircum{}N to the qth power shows x\textasciicircum{}q in J, since all u\_i\textasciicircum{}q are in R. Thus J has radical m; it is proper when I is proper and is unit when I is unit. Hence the rational profile -w(I)/r is exactly the pullback of -v(J)/(qr). Primary ideal extension gives the reverse inclusion. Rational density and uniform closure identify C; actual decreasing C-nets identify D in both directions. Thus for EVERY pointwise obstacle psi, whenever the raw supremum is defined with the usual bottom convention,

 rho\textasciicircum{}*p\_R(psi)=p\_S(rho\textasciicircum{}*psi).

For finite continuous obstacles, a continuous greatest geometric envelope exists on one side iff it exists on the other. In particular the all-obstacle CE property, any genuine continuous-obstacle CE failure, and continuity of the full canonical approximation transfer both ways. No norm average or positivity of a USC regularization is used. This is the exact operator compatibility required for these Frobenius-root maps, without any Monge-Ampere/product assertion.

There is quantitative canonical transport, even though same-degree scalar extension of canonical ideals is NOT asserted. Let B\_m=A\_m\textasciicircum{}S(rho\textasciicircum{}*f) and A\_m=A\_m\textasciicircum{}R(f). Surjectivity gives A\_m=B\_m intersect R. Let J\_m be generated by qth powers of generators of B\_m. Then kappa\_m=-v(J\_m)/(qm) pulls back to -w(B\_m)/m and J\_m subset A\_(qm). If a source estimate 0\textless{}=p\_S-h\_m\textasciicircum{}S\textless{}=E/m holds, n1's residue grading with M\_1=||v(A\_1)|| gives, for k\textgreater{}=2q,

 0\textless{}=p\_R-h\_k\textasciicircum{}R\textless{}=E/floor(k/q)+qM\_1/k\textless{}=(2qE+qM\_1)/k.

This is a conditional rate with its source hypothesis explicit. Uniform source convergence alone suffices for uniform target convergence, either by the exact envelope homeomorphism and n1 or by the same residue argument. Frobenius exponent q is not identified with generic degree or a ramification/residue sum.

An infinite-root version is also proved. Suppose R subset S is an injective extension of excellent reduced local rings of characteristic p, S is the union of local finite R-subalgebras, and every element of S has SOME p-power in R. Assume S is Noetherian and the marked maximal ideal and primary gauge are the extensions of those of R, as in the scalar example below. Define w(s)=v(s\textasciicircum{}(p\textasciicircum{}e))/p\textasciicircum{}e using any admissible e. Passing to a common larger exponent proves independence of e and proves all axioms for sums and products. Each coordinate formula uses a finite exponent, so the inverse is continuous; centredness follows from the extended maximal ideal. Every support is retained and rho is again a boundary homeomorphism. Every finitely generated primary source ideal and finitely many coefficients witnessing a primary-power containment have a common Frobenius exponent. Raising those expressions as above gives a genuine primary ideal J in R with exact rational profile. Thus C and actual D again coincide isometrically and envelopes commute for ALL obstacles. There need not be one global q, so no global degree-rate constant is claimed.

For a geometrically integral geometrically normal rational-point finite-type local k-domain in characteristic p, S=R tensor\_k k\textasciicircum{}perf is such an infinite-root example. It is the corresponding Noetherian excellent normal local ring, with mS its maximal ideal. Finite purely inseparable coefficient extensions form local finite stages. Each element is a finite sum of tensors; choose one exponent sending all its finitely many coefficients into k, and Frobenius sends the element into R. Thus CE is equivalent over k and its perfect closure, even for imperfect k, with every support included. This reduces the imperfect-field issue for this geometrically normal finite-type class; it does not prove CE in positive characteristic over the perfect closure.

Combining n3's separable-field descent with this root theorem gives a precise further reduction. For such geometrically normal rational-point germs in characteristic p, pass first to k\textasciicircum{}s and then to its perfect closure, which is an algebraic closure of k. Root invariance identifies the latter two envelope problems, and n3 gives rho\textasciicircum{}*p\_R(f)=p\_(R tensor k\textasciicircum{}s)(rho\textasciicircum{}*f) on compatible obstacles. Therefore geometric-algebraic-closure CE implies downstairs CE at these exact hypotheses, without enlarging BFJ to characteristic p. Mixed-characteristic rings have no Frobenius-root formula of this kind and are not covered. General nonnormal/conductor envelope commutation remains conditional outside these uniquely lifting maps, and all literal radial distinctions remain unchanged.

\subsection*{Expanded root transport and its quantitative limit}
For $q=p^e$ and $S^q\subset R$, all supports obey
\[
 w(s)=q^{-1}v(s^q),\qquad
 v((s_1^q,\ldots,s_l^q))=q\,w((s_1,\ldots,s_l)).
\]
The primaryness proof raises actual module expressions, not just
generic field identities: if $x\in\mathfrak a^N$ is expressed as
$\sum s_i u_i$, then $x^q=\sum s_i^qu_i^q\in J$ in $R$.
Thus the transported profiles have actual primary Cartier presentations.
Under an explicitly assumed source bound, and $k\ge2q$,
\[
 0\le p_R-h_k^R\le
 \frac{E}{\lfloor k/q\rfloor}+\frac{qM_1}{k}
 \le\frac{2qE+qM_1}{k}.
\]
An infinite coefficient perfection need not have bounded exponent.
Each finite ideal still has one common exponent, giving the exact
cone/operator transport, but the display supplies no uniform infinite
extension rate without additional bounds.

\section{n2. Full conductor-envelope equivalence when the entire normalized boundary is bijective; explicit radicial and primary-conductor criteria.}
\textit{Supports: G331, n1.}

New conductor theorem, relative to ENTIRE qualified G331 and own n1. Let R be excellent reduced local with finite normalization S and conductor c. Set X=V\_a(R) and Xtilde=V\_(aS)(S), using every closed normalization centre and EVERY semivaluation support. Suppose restriction on the conductor quotient boundaries is injective. More precisely, the boundary of (S/c)\_red maps injectively to that of (R/c)\_red, with the quotient of the extended gauge, omitting empty zero-dimensional sections. Then rho:Xtilde-\textgreater{}X is a homeomorphism. Indeed G331 grants surjectivity and compact Hausdorff quotient topology. At finite conductor value every fibre is singleton. At infinite value its ENTIRE fibre is precisely the conductor-quotient restriction fibre. The assumed injectivity handles all those fibres. Compact bijectivity gives the homeomorphism. This is a sufficient condition, not an asserted necessity for radiciality of an algebraic conductor map.

Here are two algebraically checkable sufficient cases. First, if R/c has dimension zero, c contains a power of m, so every centred semivaluation has finite conductor value. No quotient boundary remains; multiple normalization centres are allowed. Second, let B=(R/c)\_red and T=(S/c)\_red. Assume each prime p of B has exactly one prime P of T above it, and the finite field extension Frac(T/P)/Frac(B/p) is purely inseparable (in characteristic zero this means equal). These are the usual finite radicial conditions, stated explicitly. The reduction map B-\textgreater{}T is injective: nilpotence upstairs of an element of R/c is already nilpotence in its injected subring. For a quotient semivaluation with support p, any lift has support P, uniquely. After quotienting the supports, its value on any nonzero field element x is forced by w(x)=v(x\textasciicircum{}(p\textasciicircum{}e))/p\textasciicircum{}e when an appropriate power lies in the old field; in characteristic zero it is already the same field. This proves uniqueness on every support, not just generic valuations. Existence is G331 finite lifting. Thus the quotient boundary is injective. No global common Frobenius exponent, perfection, F-finiteness or characteristic-zero restriction is required for this uniqueness proof. We do not invent a real field valuation through a nonzero support.

Because EVERY rho-fibre is singleton, G331's FULL positive C and D descent implies order bijections rho*:C\_R-\textgreater{}C\_S and rho*:D\_R-\textgreater{}D\_S. On C this is an isometry, since rho is surjective; continuity in either direction follows from the homeomorphism. Thus, for ANY obstacle for which the raw supremum is interpreted pointwise, the completed order bijection gives p\_S(rho*f)=rho*p\_R(f). For finite continuous signed obstacles the raw suprema are finite by n1. The continuous-envelope property is EQUIVALENT on R and S: every continuous source obstacle is the pullback of a continuous target obstacle, and an envelope belongs to C on one side iff it does on the other. The descended continuous envelope is independently geometric by positive descent, not by an unsupported assertion that a pointwise supremum is positive.

The canonical degree-m ideals satisfy A\_m\textasciicircum{}R(f)=A\_m\textasciicircum{}S(rho*f) intersect R, directly from surjective restriction and ALL defining inequalities. Equality after extension to S is NOT asserted. When CE holds, n1 gives uniform convergence in EVERY downstairs canonical degree. Each such profile has an ACTUAL negative effective Cartier presentation -E\_(A\_m)/m on its ACTUAL primary blowup; its degree on EVERY contracted integral curve is positive by ampleness. Consequently the uniform geometric envelope has actual positive approximants on the required model system. A continuous envelope need not itself have a single-model determination. Neither a source O(1/m) bound nor source finite generation is automatically inherited through contraction; n3 establishes an explicit rate and failure of finite generation for a particular family by a different argument.

The exact primary-gauge cocycle commutes with rho since w(aS)=v(a). For a new gauge b, d(v)=v(b), source and target divide by the same bounded positive denominator. Canonical ideals remain unchanged when the obstacle is transported homogeneously. Completion follows G331 and n1. For decreasing continuous obstacles with continuous envelopes, the actual D rule of n1 transports as well, with partial bottom and bottom retained. This theorem supplies envelope descent only under the stated singleton-fibre criterion; it does not settle arbitrary nonnormal gluing along a positive-dimensional conductor quotient.

Consequences: any excellent reduced local germ whose conductor is primary has CE exactly when all of its normal local centres have CE. In particular, the dimension-two normal theorem of n1 gives CE for every such germ whose normal centres all have dimension at most two. Under the finite radicial conductor-quotient condition the same equivalence holds even when the infinite-conductor boundary is NONEMPTY. If S is a normal local surface it has CE in any equal/mixed characteristic by n1; if its centres are smooth affine closed germs over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field it has CE in every dimension by n1. These are narrowed conclusions with explicit source hypotheses, not added premises for unrestricted ORIGINAL P12.3.

The point where the unrestricted descent problem remains is now precise: for a quotient boundary with nonsingleton fibres there is no automatic constancy of a source greatest minorant. This note neither takes a fibrewise minimum as psh nor asserts arbitrary finite-map envelope compatibility. Products, energy and full finite operators remain separate.

This is a mathematical proof using G331 only for its qualified boundary/cone/descent results and n1 for envelopes. No new published premise is needed for the radicial uniqueness argument. \subsection*{Expanded conductor theorem}
With $\mathfrak c=(R:S)$, assume the reduced conductor quotient boundary
restriction is injective. Then
\[
\rho:V_{\mathfrak aS}(S)\xrightarrow{\sim}V_{\mathfrak a}(R),\quad
\rho^*C_R=C_S,\quad\rho^*D_R=D_S,
\]
\[
\rho^*p_R(f)=p_S(\rho^*f),\qquad
\operatorname{CE}(R)\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{CE}(S),\qquad
A_m^R=A_m^S\cap R.
\]
This condition includes the entire infinite-conductor support stratum.
The last identity is contraction only, not an extension identity.

Here is the universal bound, including EVERY support and infinite coordinate. Write s=w(t), u=w(z\_1), B=w(b), U=min\_(j\textgreater{}=2)w(z\_j), so min(2s,u,U)=1 and A=min(B,2s,U). A is finite. Every displayed generator has value \textgreater{}=mA, hence w(K\_m)\textgreater{}=mA. If U=A, the added ideal has value mU=mA, giving equality. Otherwise A\textless{}U. If 2s\textless{}=B, then s is finite and u=s: unequal values would force B=min(s,u)\textless{}2s. Since U\textgreater{}2s and min(2s,s,U)=1, s=u=1. The last original generator then has value mA+2. In the remaining case B\textless{}2s, A=B\textless{}U. If s\textless{}=u, then s is finite; B\textgreater{}=s. If s\textgreater{}1 all of 2s,u,U would exceed one, a contradiction. Thus s\textless{}=1, and t\textasciicircum{}2 b\textasciicircum{}m has value mA+2s\textless{}=mA+2. If s\textgreater{}u (including s=infinity), B=w(z\_1-mt)=u: for m nonzero in k, m is a unit and the values are unequal, and if m=0 in k the second expression is simply z\_1. The normalization and U\textgreater{}u give u=1, so the first generator has value mA+1. These cases exhaust all possibilities, including B=infinity, U=infinity, killed coordinates and cancellation. Consequently
0\textless{}=v(K\_m)/m-A(v)\textless{}=2/m on the ENTIRE normalized boundary.

Therefore f is a uniform limit from below of -v(K\_m)/m. Each profile is the evaluation of ACTUAL -E\_(K\_m)/m on ACTUAL Bl\_(K\_m)(R), negative effective and relatively ample, with positive degree on EVERY contracted integral curve. Thus f belongs to independently geometric C even in higher positive characteristic where general CE is unknown. It is its own greatest C/D minorant. Since K\_m subset A\_m\textasciicircum{}R(f), the canonical profiles themselves obey the EVERY-degree uniform estimate 0\textless{}=p(f)-h\_m\textasciicircum{}R(f)\textless{}=2/m. This establishes a quantitative geometric envelope across the infinite-conductor stratum without a conductor-value/N error or a root-map assumption.

In characteristic ZERO f is outside the ENTIRE finite REAL raw negative ideal cone Q\_R, and its canonical algebra is NOT finitely generated. Define w\_infinity by killing t,z\_2,... and giving z\_1 value one; define w\_star by killing z\_2,... and using monomial weights (t,b)=(1,2), with z\_1=b-t. Both satisfy the chosen gauge, and A(w\_infinity)=1, A(w\_star)=2. For ANY proper primary downstairs ideal I, its image after killing the other z\_j is primary in k[t\textasciicircum{}2,t\textasciicircum{}3,z\_1]. Let e=w\_infinity(I)\textgreater{}0. A generator attaining e has a unit denominator at both valuations. Its formal expansion has no t-degree-one terms, has nonzero z\_1\textasciicircum{}e coefficient, and has zero t z\_1\textasciicircum{}(e-1) coefficient. Its total-degree-e homogeneous part therefore cannot be a scalar multiple of b\textasciicircum{}e in characteristic zero. After z\_1=b-t it contains some t\textasciicircum{}(e-j)b\textasciicircum{}j with j\textless{}e, of w\_star-value e+j\textless{}=2e-1. Other total degrees cannot cancel this monomial. Thus w\_star(I)\textless{}2w\_infinity(I). Every nonzero finite nonnegative REAL combination of proper primary gauges preserves this strict inequality; unit terms vanish. A has equality, so A is outside the raw positive cone and f outside Q\_R. Finite homogeneous generation of the canonical algebra would force a rational primary envelope by the elementary argument in n1, contradicting this separation. No claim of non-finite-generation in positive characteristic follows from the characteristic-zero argument.

This is continuous-envelope regularity WITH a canonical O(1/m) bound and WITHOUT canonical finite generation for an explicit cancellation-sensitive nonnormal higher-dimensional example. It is not a counterexample to CE, nor a raw geometric-core attainment claim. Under another gauge the same homogeneously transported obstacle keeps all canonical ideals, and the bound is divided by min v(new gauge)\textgreater{}0. G331's literal radial scope distinction, curve min(f,0), nilpotent reduction and empty dimension-zero case remain unchanged.

\subsection*{Expanded higher-dimensional cusp construction}
For a numerical semigroup $H$ of conductor $c$,
\[
R_H=k[t^H,z_1,\ldots,z_{d-1}]_0,\quad
S=k[t,z_1,\ldots,z_{d-1}]_0,\quad\mathfrak c=t^cS,
\]
\[
(R_H/\mathfrak c)_{\rm red}=(S/\mathfrak c)_{\rm red}=k[z_1,\ldots,z_{d-1}]_0.
\]
For $H=\langle2,3\rangle$, $b=z_1+t$ and
$A=w((b,t^2,z_2,\ldots,z_{d-1}))$, put
\[
K_m=(b^m(z_1-mt),\ t^2b^m,\ t^{2m+2})+(z_2,\ldots,z_{d-1})^m.
\]
The proof covers all supports and establishes
\[
0\leq \frac{v(K_m)}m-A\leq\frac2m,\qquad
0\leq p(-A)-h_m^R(-A)\leq\frac2m.
\]
In characteristic zero the two test points give $A(w_\infty)=1$,
$A(w_*)=2$, whereas every nonzero finite real positive primary combination
satisfies $u(w_*)<2u(w_\infty)$. Hence $-A\notin Q_R$ and the canonical
algebra is not finitely generated. Neither conclusion is a CE failure.

## Distinct expanded exposition n4
\section{n4. Explicit actual-primary threefold obstruction: generic sections on exceptional surfaces do not imply all-curve-nef divisorial parts.}
\textit{Supports: G331, n1.}

Precise THREE-dimensional obstruction to the surface competitor method; this is NOT a continuous-envelope counterexample. Support: ENTIRE qualified G331 and own n1 for the finite section/ACTUAL primary presentation argument. Let R=k[x,y,z]\_(x,y,z) for ANY field k, m=(x,y,z), and I=(z)+m\textasciicircum{}2, a proper primary ideal. Blow up the origin, with exceptional E\_0=P\textasciicircum{}2\_k. Blow up the two distinct k-rational points P=[1:0:0], Q=[0:1:0] of E\_0. Their disjoint point ideals can be blown up at once; equivalently do the two point blowups successively. All charts are regular (ordinary point blowups in regular coordinates). Let Y be the result, E\_1 the strict transform of E\_0, and E\_2,E\_3 the new exceptional planes. Then E\_1=Bl\_(P,Q)(P\textasciicircum{}2), while E\_2,E\_3 are disjoint copies of P\textasciicircum{}2.

This explicit Y is an ACTUAL primary model. Its second-stage negative tautological bundle O(-E\_2-E\_3) is relatively ample for Y-\textgreater{}Bl\_m(R); this is the blowup of the disjoint union of the two point ideals, invertible/unit on the complement. The first negative tautological bundle O(-E\_0) is ample. The COMPLETE immediately read Stacks29.38.7--8 gives, for an integer a sufficiently large, O(-E\_2-E\_3-a pullback(E\_0)) ample over R. Here pullback(E\_0)=E\_1+E\_2+E\_3. Thus E=aE\_1+(a+1)E\_2+(a+1)E\_3 is ACTUAL effective Cartier, full exceptional support, and O(-E) relatively ample. Stacks37.53.6 gives H\textasciicircum{}0(Y,O)=R. The finite affine-section localization/projective immersion/Rees argument proved in n1 applies verbatim in this dimension to THIS explicit Y: it requires normal target, ample negative exceptional bundle and projectivity, not surface resolution. A finite set of sections of O(-nE) gives a proper primary J and identifies Y with Bl\_J(R). This is an explicit construction and no cofinality assertion for arbitrary threefold modifications.

The divisorial part of I on Y is F\_I=E\_1+2E\_2+2E\_3. The order at E\_0 is one, realized by z. In the x-chart of the first blowup, with v=y/x and w=z/x, I O=x(w,x). At P the regular local parameters are x,v,w. Thus the residual ideal (w,x) has point order one, so the second exceptional order is two. The y-chart gives the identical calculation at Q. The strict E\_1 order remains one. All ideal generators are global sections of O(-F\_I) by normal height-one intersection, and at the generic point of EACH E\_i at least one realizes the minimum and restricts to a nonzero section, exactly as in the surface competitor proof.

Nevertheless A=-F\_I fails the mandatory contracted-curve positivity test. On E\_1 let H be the pullback of a line in P\textasciicircum{}2 and e\_P,e\_Q its two exceptional curves. Restricting divisors gives E\_1|\_(E\_1)=-H-e\_P-e\_Q, E\_2|\_(E\_1)=e\_P and E\_3|\_(E\_1)=e\_Q: the strict first divisor is pullback(E\_0)-E\_2-E\_3, and O(E\_0)|\_(E\_0)=O\_P2(-1). Hence
O(-F\_I)|\_(E\_1) has class H-e\_P-e\_Q.
Let L be the strict transform of the line z=0 through P and Q. It is a proper integral contracted curve with class H-e\_P-e\_Q. The usual point-blowup chart calculation gives H\textasciicircum{}2=1, H.e\_P=H.e\_Q=e\_P.e\_Q=0 and e\_P\textasciicircum{}2=e\_Q\textasciicircum{}2=-1; these are local normal-bundle degrees, with residue degrees one. Therefore deg\_L O(-F\_I)=1-1-1=-1. Equivalently the nonzero restricted generator z determines an effective divisor whose fixed component is the negative curve L. A nonzero section on the exceptional SURFACE does not imply nonnegative degree on that curve.

On E\_2 and E\_3 the restrictions of -F\_I are O(1), since E\_1 restricts to a hyperplane and each new exceptional normal bundle is O(-1). Nonnegativity there cannot repair the degree -1 on L in E\_1. Thus positivity was checked on an ACTUAL primary model, and a SPECIFIC actual contracted integral curve violates it; no purely numerical abstract matrix was substituted.

The every-support inequality -v(I)\textless{}=f\_(-F\_I) still holds: the ideal-sheaf inclusion I O\_Y subset O(-F\_I) pulls to the valuation ring of Frac(R/p) for each support p, with generic centre outside the exceptional fibre, and regular ratios give the inequality even for killed generators. What fails is the subsequent inference that f\_(-F\_I) is an all-curve-nef geometric-core competitor on Y. In contrast -v(I) has a negative effective relatively ample Cartier presentation on ACTUAL Bl\_I(R). The example therefore pinpoints a false step in the surface strategy while preserving the positivity of genuine primary profiles and existing smooth characteristic-zero CE. It gives no failure of CE in any characteristic and no theorem about arbitrary higher-dimensional model cofinality.

The intersection numbers are proved by the explicit blowup geometry, not by a program. Own finite\_diagnostics.py only evaluates the recorded integer degree expression and divisor coefficients; it is a diagnostic. Artifacts n4.md, n4.tex and reports/finite-diagnostics.json; rerun python finite\_diagnostics.py; python assemble.py; python verify.py.

\subsection*{Expanded threefold degree obstruction}
For $I=(z)+\mathfrak m^2$ on the explicit regular threefold model,
\[
F_I=E_1+2E_2+2E_3,\quad
(-F_I)|_{E_1}=H-e_P-e_Q,\quad L\sim H-e_P-e_Q,
\]
\[
\deg_L\mathcal O_Y(-F_I)=1-1-1=-1.
\]
The ample actual primary presentation uses
$E=aE_1+(a+1)E_2+(a+1)E_3$ for a sufficiently large integer $a$,
proved by relative composition ampleness and the finite section/Rees
argument. The nonzero generic sections on the $E_i$ therefore fail the
all-contracted-curve test on an actual primary model, not an abstract
unrealized divisor.

\begin{abstract}
On the intrinsic centred semivaluation boundary of an excellent local germ,
we define a geometric core by actual negative effective real Cartier divisors
on actual primary blowups, with nonnegative degrees on all contracted integral
curves. We prove its continuous uniform closure and actual decreasing completion
equal the corresponding ideal classes. A fixed primary correction to finite
global sections, corrected Keeler generation on the full closed fibre, and
explicit real ample perturbation prove the comparison without a normality,
smoothness or characteristic restriction. We reconstruct full finite-injection
and normalization/conductor descent, including mixed-zero and bottom patterns,
and recover the full smooth BFJ class on all semivaluations at its exact published
hypotheses. A nonisolated cusp separates the entire finite-real raw cone from its
completion. This is an unverified complete-solution candidate for P12.2;
independent whole-original review remains required.
\end{abstract}

\section*{Main theorem and proof map}
Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be excellent local and replace it by its reduction.
For every proper primary $\mathfrak a$, let $V_{\mathfrak a}$ be the compact
section of centred real semivaluations with $v(\mathfrak a)=1$, retaining every
prime support. Define $Q$ by finite nonnegative real sums of negative
unit-or-primary ideal values, $C$ by uniform closure, and $D$ by actual infima
of nonempty decreasing $C$-nets, with bottom allowed.

On actual primary blowups, take actual negative effective finite real Cartier
presentations having nonnegative degree on every contracted proper integral
curve. Their evaluations define $M_{\rm geom}$ independently of ideal
positivity. Then
\[
 Q\subset M_{\rm geom}\subset C,\qquad
 C_{\rm geom}=C,\qquad D_{\rm geom}=D.
\]
For every reduced finite injection, the pullback image of either completed
class is precisely its full-fibre-constant subclass. Normalization fibres are
singletons at finite conductor value and precisely conductor-quotient fibres
at infinite value. Primary changes obey the exact homogeneous cocycle.
At a smooth affine closed germ over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero
field, $C$ is exactly the finite continuous BFJ subclass and $D$ is the full
BFJ all-semivaluation extension with the identically bottom function adjoined.
Smooth DVR and empty dimension zero are direct.

The proofs are the numbered local chain below: n1 gives the boundary; n2--n6
give full algebraic descent; n7 discharges the exact published geometric inputs;
n8 constructs and compares the independent cone; n9 gives full BFJ recovery;
n10--n11 preserve raw-cone and radial distinctions; n12 records the exact
original-target decision. Each support list contains only earlier local IDs.
Source applications are ordinary published applications, with disclosed
recursive historical dependencies, and no supplied draft is an accepted premise.
Separate envelopes, products, energy and their geometric operator theory are
the P12.3--P12.6 targets. They are not claimed here.
\section{n1. Boundary, finite lifting, conductor fibres, and completion}
\textit{Earlier local supports: none.}

All rings below are commutative. For a Noetherian local ring \((R,\mathfrak m)\), a centred real semivaluation is a map to \([0,+\infty]\) satisfying \(v(0)=+\infty\), \(v(1)=0\), multiplicativity, the ultrametric inequality, and \(0<v(\mathfrak m)<+\infty\). Its support \(v^{-1}(+\infty)\) is a prime strictly below \(\mathfrak m\); no minimal-support restriction is imposed. Ideal values are minima over finite generating sets. Relations between generating sets prove independence and
\[
v(IJ)=v(I)+v(J),\qquad v(I+J)=\min\{v(I),v(J)\}.
\]
Units have value zero. A proper primary ideal always means primary for the marked maximal ideal.

Fix a proper primary ideal \(\mathfrak a\). The section \(V_{\mathfrak a}(R)=\{v:v(\mathfrak a)=1\}\) is compact Hausdorff. Indeed semivaluation axioms and \(v(\mathfrak m)=1\) are closed conditions in the compact product \([0,+\infty]^R\); addition, minimum and the order relation have the required continuity/closedness. Choose \(\mathfrak m^r\subset\mathfrak a\subset\mathfrak m^s\), with \(r\ge s\ge1\). Then \(s v(\mathfrak m)\le v(\mathfrak a)\le r v(\mathfrak m)\). Rescaling identifies the two sections. Every primary ideal value is finite positive continuous and bounded there. For another primary ideal \(\mathfrak b\),
\[
H_{\mathfrak a,\mathfrak b}(v)=v/v(\mathfrak b),\qquad
u_{\mathfrak b}(H_{\mathfrak a,\mathfrak b}v)=u_{\mathfrak a}(v)/v(\mathfrak b).
\]
The denominator and its inverse are bounded. Substitution proves the inverse and the exact three-gauge cocycle. The centred cone is the product of its section and the positive radial coordinate \(v(\mathfrak a)\); hence these sections represent its intrinsic ray quotient. Nonprimary proper ideals give only their open finite-value domain, which can be noncompact. Units and zero ideals have no level-one section.

Nilpotents have infinite value. Comparing \(f+n\) and \((f+n)-n\) proves that reduction preserves every semivaluation and ideal gauge. A zero-dimensional reduced local ring is a field and has empty centred boundary. For a positive-dimensional excellent reduced local ring, a penultimate prime of a saturated chain to the maximal ideal gives a one-dimensional excellent domain quotient. Its finite normalization has a local DVR factor, whose order pulls back and normalizes into the section. This proves nonemptiness. Ordinary background used throughout is lying over, prime avoidance, finite Artinian decompositions, and the quotient/finite-type-localization stability, Nagata finiteness and universal catenarity consequences of excellence. None is used to assert resolution in arbitrary characteristic.

Every finite integral injection \(R\hookrightarrow B\), with \(B\) reduced and nonzero, gives a continuous surjective restriction \(V_{\mathfrak aB}(B)\to V_{\mathfrak a}(R)\). Here a finite algebra has the finite union of its closed-centre sections above \(\mathfrak m\). To lift \(v\) with support \(\mathfrak p\), choose a prime \(P\) of \(B\) above \(\mathfrak p\) and form the finite field extension \(\operatorname{Frac}(B/P)/\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak p)\). Extend the valuation ring by taking the integral closure, a prime over its maximal ideal, and a dominating valuation ring. The domination assertion follows from Zorn: in a maximal dominating local subring, either adjoining \(x\) or \(x^{-1}\) leaves the maximal ideal proper. If \(1=\sum a_i x^{-i}\) with all \(a_i\) in that ideal, multiplying by a power and dividing by \(1-a_0\) makes \(x\) integral, so lying over makes the ideal proper after adjoining \(x\). Localizing contradicts maximality unless one of the two elements already belongs. Intersection with the old field is the original valuation ring: an element outside it has inverse in its maximal ideal. An algebraic equation for any new nonzero field element has two least-valued terms; thus an integer multiple of its value is in the old value group. Dividing this old real value by the integer gives a well-defined order-preserving real embedding, using common multiples. Integral elements have nonnegative value by the least-term test for a monic equation. Compose with \(B\to B/P\), assigning \(P\) infinite value. This construction first kills the support; it never extends a nonzero-support semivaluation to the original fraction field. Compactness makes restriction a quotient map.

Let \(S\) be the finite normalization of an excellent reduced \(R\), and \(\mathfrak c=(R:S)\). Clearing denominators of finitely many generators of \(S\) gives a regular conductor element. The conductor is an ideal of both rings and
\[
R=S\times_{S/\mathfrak c}(R/\mathfrak c).
\]
An element of \(S\) whose residue comes from \(R\) differs from an element of \(R\) by an element of \(\mathfrak c\), proving this identity. The normalization boundary is the finite disjoint union of local normal centres above \(\mathfrak m\). Idempotents choose a minimal component; localization at its centre changes no values of denominators. Chinese remainder elements separating the finitely many centres, and their complements, have open positive-value loci selecting these pieces. The pieces are therefore clopen. Branches mean these local centres, not merely minimal primes.

If \(v(\mathfrak c)<+\infty\), choose \(c\in\mathfrak c\) of finite value. Every lift satisfies \(w(s)=v(cs)-v(c)\), so it is unique. The subtracted number is finite. If \(v(\mathfrak c)=+\infty\), all lifts kill the conductor, and equality after restriction \(S/\mathfrak c\to R/\mathfrak c\) is exactly their identification. This infinity stratum is closed; its finite complement is open, without a closedness claim. A fibre-constant continuous function descends continuously by the compact quotient. A fibre-constant extended nonpositive upper semicontinuous function descends upper semicontinuously: its closed superlevel sets have compact, hence closed, images. These assertions alone supply no positivity descent.

Completion preserves the entire boundary for every Noetherian local ring. For \(F\in\widehat R\), choose representatives \(F_N\) modulo \(\mathfrak m^N\), and put \(d=v(\mathfrak m)>0\). Differences have value at least \(Nd\). If some \(v(F_N)<Nd\), later values stabilize; otherwise they tend to infinity. Define \(\widehat v(F)\) by this limit. It is independent of representatives and satisfies
\[
\min\{\widehat v(F),Nd\}=\min\{v(F_N),Nd\}.
\]
Applying this to sums and products proves all axioms and uniqueness, including infinite values; completed units have unit representatives. Compose with \(q(t)=t/(1+t)\), \(q(+\infty)=1\). The displayed continuous truncations have uniform error at most \((1+N/r)^{-1}\), because \(d\ge1/r\). Thus completed evaluation is continuous and completion restriction is a homeomorphism. Every completed primary \(J\) contains \(\widehat{\mathfrak m}^N\). Representatives modulo that power of its generators belong to \(J\cap R\) and, with the boundary power, generate \(J\). Hence \(J=(J\cap R)\widehat R\). The quotient isomorphism also proves contraction of an extended primary ideal recovers it. Unit-or-primary profiles and their uniform and decreasing classes therefore agree under completion. No equivalence of geometric model categories is asserted.

This is a mathematical argument with the stated ordinary background. Swanson--Huneke 6.4.1--2 were read in full and agree with the domination proof. Artifact n1.md is authoritative and is reproduced in argument.md and the paper. Rerun: python audit\_inputs.py; python build\_delivery.py. Execution does not verify the mathematics.

\section{n2. Exact algebraic applications and their qualifications}
\textit{Earlier local supports: n1.}

Use n1 for boundary conventions. The following are ordinary published theorem applications at their stated hypotheses, with their immediate units checked from the bound primary data. This is not an independent reconstruction of all historical proofs.

Swanson--Huneke is the current author PDF created July 2024, not asserted byte-identical to the 2006 printing. Its complete 6.8.1--4 statements and proofs give the following consequence. Let \(E\) be Noetherian semilocal, \(J\) contain a boundary power, and \(Q\) be a finite ideal. If every normalized centred semivaluation satisfies \(w(Q)\ge w(J)\), and \(Q\) has zero image on every zero-dimensional minimal component where \(J\) is nonunit, then
\[
Q\subset\overline J.
\]
Apply 6.8.4 on each positive-dimensional local domain component, normalizing each centred rank-one DVR by the boundary ideal. Apply 6.8.3 to all minimal components. On zero-dimensional components there are no boundary points; the extra zero-image condition is needed. In all uses below \(Q=K(\mathfrak aE)^L\), with \(L>0\), so this condition holds. Unit components of \(J\) impose no condition. For nonreduced \(E\), lift the componentwise monic equations, multiply them over the finitely many minimal primes, then raise to a power to kill the nilpotent error. The resulting equation is monic with degree-i coefficients in \(J^i\). This is the finite-minimal-prime argument of 1.1.5, also read completely. PDF inspection of printed page 140 confirmed the integral-closure bars omitted in the text extraction.

The common exponent needed later has a short direct proof. Each \(qt\), \(q\in Q\), is integral over \(E[Jt]\) with its homogeneous ideal-integrality equation. Thus \(E[(J+Q)t]\) is finite graded over \(E[Jt]\). Choose homogeneous module generators of degrees at most \(h\). Its degree \(N+h\) terms have coefficients in \(J^{N+h-d}\subset J^N\). Consequently
\[
Q^{N+h}\subset (J+Q)^{N+h}\subset J^N\quad(N\ge1).
\]
This works for nonreduced rings and assumes no finiteness of the full normalized Rees algebra. The complete 1.2.3--5 reduction chain was checked too; printed page 6 confirms the criterion uses integral closure.

For an excellent local domain \(A\) of positive dimension and a nonzero proper primary ideal, 10.2.2, including its proof ending at 10.2.3, constructs finitely many Rees DVRs centred at the closed point. The full 10.4.3 proof gives their residue transcendence degree \(\dim A-1\) when \(A\) is formally equidimensional. Excellence supplies universal catenarity, and the full B.5.1 statement/proof identifies this with local formal equidimensionality for Noetherian domains. B.3.2 and its immediate context give, for a finite-type birational domain \(B\) over excellent local domain \(A\), and \(P\cap A=\mathfrak m\),
\[
\dim B_P+\operatorname{trdeg}_{A/\mathfrak m}\kappa(P)=\dim A.
\]
The book describes B.3.2's proof as a modification of an earlier dimension argument. Its recursive historical dependencies, including Mori--Nagata and Ratliff, are disclosed rather than claimed independently read.

Stacks 0C23, full immediate HTML lemma/proof, states that normal Noetherian local rings with normal formal fibres have normal completion; excellence suffices. Its proof refers to Algebra 10.163.8, not recursively read. A normal local completed ring is a domain. Thus an excellent normal local domain is analytically irreducible and analytically unramified. This is not claimed for an arbitrary nonnormal domain.

Exact Rond--Spivakovsky arXiv 1404.4885v1, complete pages 1--2 definitions and statements 1.3, 1.4 and 1.7, yields an order bound at precisely this analytic domain. For a centred divisorial valuation \(\nu\) and the finitely many maximal-ideal Rees valuations \(\nu_j\), 1.3 gives \(\nu(f)\le c_j\nu_j(f)\). Set \(C_0=\max_j c_j\nu_j(\mathfrak m)\). Statements 1.4 and 1.7 imply
\[
\nu(f)\le C_0\min_j\frac{\nu_j(f)}{\nu_j(\mathfrak m)}
=C_0\overline{\operatorname{ord}}_{\mathfrak m}(f)
\le C_0(\operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak m}(f)+K).
\]
For nonzero nonunits the order is at least one and finite by Krull intersection, giving \(\nu(f)\le C_0(1+K)\operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak m}(f)\). Units have both values zero and are handled separately. The literal strict Remark 1.6 fails on units and is not used. Swanson's full Rees-valuations Section 5 was read; its 5.2 is stated for complete domains. The general-domain application here uses exact Rond--Spivakovsky 1.3. Original Rees 1989 and the historical Izumi proofs have not been independently read. Published applications with these disclosed dependencies are allowed by the task; metadata and old reading receipts are not grants.
