\subsection{Explicit saturated-monoid certificate and finite arithmetic implementation}

Support: G331, with its entire source, annotation, ledger and scope unchanged. No result of current401, B341 or E350 is a premise. The argument below reconstructs the required monomial facts and proves the new envelope theorem directly.

Let M be a rank-d lattice, T a pointed full-dimensional rational polyhedral cone, S=T intersect M, and R the completion of k[S] at its monomial maximal ideal, over any field k. Let a be any monomial primary gauge, X=V\_a(R), and C,D the independently geometric classes of qualified G331. In particular, C is the uniform closure of negative finite real primary profiles, rational profiles are uniformly dense, and D is made of actual decreasing C-nets. These are consequences of the granted geometric comparison, not new definitions of positivity. Every semivaluation support is included.

The monoid is finitely generated by the rational-cone lattice-point theorem. The affine ring is normal: in its fraction field it is the intersection of the normal Laurent polynomial ring k[M] and the valuation rings of the primitive facet weights. For a Laurent polynomial each facet minimum is the minimum of its term weights; nonnegativity of all these minima says exactly that every exponent belongs to T. The finite-type ring is excellent, and its normal local ring has normal excellent completion. Thus the stipulated R is an excellent normal local domain over arbitrary k. These exact conventional algebraic facts require neither perfection nor a finite extension of a regular local ring. Its elements have unique formal monomial expansions in the maximal-adic topology.

Fix a nonunit monomial primary ideal J and a positive integer q. Put H(v)=-v(J)/q. This is an actual geometric core function: on Bl\_J(R) its negative effective Cartier exceptional divisor has an ample negative bundle and nonnegative degree on every contracted proper integral curve, as granted and proved in G331. H is finite continuous on all X. Write
\[
 P_J=\operatorname{conv}\{u_1,\ldots,u_h\}+T
\]
for its Newton polyhedron, using a finite monomial generating set. A finite rational half-space presentation consists of the cone inequalities together with finitely many inequalities
\[
 \langle x,w_j\rangle\ge b_j,\qquad b_j>0.                 \tag{1}
\]
Every w\_j in (1) is in the interior of the dual cone. Indeed, a supporting normal is nonnegative on the recession cone T. If it has zero value on a nonzero monoid generator g, primaryness puts some Ng in P\_J, so its supporting intercept is zero. Such zero-intercept inequalities are already consequences of x in T. Consequently all positive-intercept facet normals are strictly positive on all monoid generators. The elementary finite rational polyhedral half-space/vertex theorem applies here; no toric test-ideal theorem is used.

For an interior dual weight w, the minimum weight of terms defines a centred monomial valuation of the completed ring. Positivity on the finitely many generators bounds the number of monomials of bounded weight and proves the minimum exists. The associated graded monomials cannot cancel, so multiplication and the ultrametric inequality hold. Normalize by w(a). Denote the resulting point associated to w\_j by x\_j. Then
\[
 v_{x_j}(J)=b_j/w_j(a).
\]
The finite set E\_J=\{x\_j\} is a contact certificate for H in the following strong sense:
\[
 u\in D,\quad u(x_j)\le H(x_j)\ (\text{every }j)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad u(v)\le H(v)\ (\text{every }v\in X).       \tag{2}
\]

Here is a proof on every support that avoids approximating an infinite monomial weight. First let u=-v(I)/r be a rational primary or unit profile. Let M(I) be the monomial ideal generated by all terms in a finite collection of formal generators of I. Noetherianity makes it generated by finitely many of those terms. Moreover I is contained in M(I): each finite truncation of a generator belongs to this monomial ideal, and the ideal is adically closed by separation of its finite quotient. At every interior monomial valuation v\_w(I)=v\_w(M(I)), because a least term in a generator cannot cancel against distinct monomials.

The contact inequalities imply, for every occurring exponent u\_0,
\[
 q\langle u_0,w_j\rangle\ge r b_j,
 \qquad q u_0\in rP_J.                                    \tag{3}
\]
The second statement follows from the complete half-space presentation and u\_0 in S. Write q u\_0 as a rational convex combination of the r u\_i plus a rational vector in T. Such a rational decomposition exists: it solves a finite rational linear system with nonnegative unknowns, and row reduction on the minimal face of a real solution gives rational feasible points. Clear its denominators by a positive integer D\_0. The recession remainder then lies in S, by saturation, and
\[
 \chi^{D_0 q u_0}\in J^{rD_0}.
\]
Thus chi\textasciicircum{}\{q u\_0\} is integral over J\textasciicircum{}r, using the equation Z\textasciicircum{}\{D\_0\}-chi\textasciicircum{}\{D\_0 q u\_0\}=0. For any semivaluation v in X, J has finite value because it is primary. Integral dependence implies
\[
 qv(\chi^{u_0})\ge r v(J).                                 \tag{4}
\]
If the left side is infinite this is automatic. Otherwise a hypothetical strict inequality makes the leading monic term in the integral equation have uniquely smallest finite value, contradicting the ultrametric inequality. Taking the minimum over the finite monomial generators of M(I), then using I subset M(I), proves v(I)/r>=v(J)/q on EVERY support. This proves (2) for rational profiles without assuming that monomialization preserves an arbitrary obstacle.

For g in C satisfying the contact inequalities, approximate g uniformly by a rational primary profile within epsilon. Subtract a rational primary-gauge constant between epsilon and 2epsilon. This subtraction is again a single rational profile after clearing denominators and taking an ideal product. It satisfies the exact contact inequalities, hence is at most H everywhere by the preceding proof. Let epsilon tend to zero to obtain g<=H. For u=inf\_i g\_i in D, the finite contact set and directedness select one term with g\_i(x\_j)<H(x\_j)+epsilon for every j, even if u has poles at some contacts. Then g\_i-epsilon is in C and satisfies the contact inequalities. Hence u<=H+epsilon, and epsilon tends to zero. This proves (2) for the ACTUAL decreasing completion, including bottom and partial poles; no flattening or increasing closure is used.

Now let f be ANY finite continuous obstacle on X, with no weight-dependence assumption, such that
\[
 f\ge H\text{ on }X,\qquad f(x_j)=H(x_j)\text{ for every }j.             \tag{5}
\]
H is a geometric competitor. Every geometric D competitor below f satisfies (2), so is below H. Consequently
\[
 \sup\{u\in D:u\le f\}=H\in C.
\]
This is an actually positive continuous greatest geometric envelope among ALL competitors. The same proof works for ANY bounded-above extended upper semicontinuous f satisfying (5); its envelope is still the continuous function H. Here (5) forces f to be finite below, although its upper size may vary. The unit case J=R has H=0 and no contacts; every obstacle f>=0 has envelope zero by nonpositivity.

There is a quantitative version with no presumed continuity of the raw envelope. If f>=H-epsilon everywhere and f(x\_j)<=H(x\_j)+delta at the finite contacts, for epsilon,delta>=0, then
\[
 H-\epsilon\le p(f)\le H+\delta.                           \tag{6}
\]
The lower inequality uses the actual C competitor H-epsilon. The upper inequality applies (2) to each competitor shifted by -delta. Thus increasingly accurate lower barriers and contact bounds give uniform approximation of raw envelopes to H, even when CE is not established for each perturbed obstacle. Conditions (5) are sufficient; no necessity or density among all obstacles is claimed.

This advances beyond weight-dependent obstacles: arbitrary cancellation-sensitive functions satisfying the finite contacts are allowed. The general theorem above removes the toric hypothesis for the finite-contact obstacle sector. Neither theorem supplies arbitrary-obstacle CE or an envelope counterexample. Finite geometry controls the competitors; the obstacle is never averaged or monomialized. G331 remains the sole correctness grant. The proof's conventional backgrounds are finite rational polyhedral geometry, Gordan's finite-generation lemma, normal excellent completion, and finite-module adic separation, at exactly the stated hypotheses.

Artifacts: n1.md, proof-companion.md and P12.3-contact-envelopes.tex. The explicit finite certificate used in n2 is implemented by the independently written contact\_certificate.py, with contact-input.json and contact-output.json. Rerun: python contact\_certificate.py. Program success is only finite arithmetic evidence, not a proof of (2) or of general CE.


\section{n2. Explicit nonmonomial primary obstacles on normal nonisolated fourfolds, including mixed characteristic}

Support: G331 and earlier own n1. We use n1's finite-contact theorem, not the current401 toric-envelope theorem or a finite-cover theorem.

For ANY field k let
\[
 R=k[[a,b,c,d,z]]/(ad-bc),\quad \mathfrak m=(a,b,c,d,z),\quad
 J=(a^2,b^3,c^3,d^2,z^4),\quad
 K=(a+b,c+d,z)+\mathfrak m^2.                               \tag{7}
\]
Both J and K are genuine primary ideals. J contains powers of every maximal generator, and K contains m\textasciicircum{}2. Write the saturated monoid cone in Z\textasciicircum{}4 with generators
\[
 g_a=(1,0,0,0),\ g_b=(1,1,0,0),\ g_c=(1,0,1,0),\
 g_d=(1,1,1,0),\ g_z=(0,0,0,1).
\]
The cone consists of x\_2,x\_3,x\_4>=0, x\_1>=x\_2,x\_3. Every integer point is generated by these vectors: choose the coefficient of g\_d between max(0,x\_2+x\_3-x\_1) and min(x\_2,x\_3), then use g\_b,g\_c,g\_a for the remainder and g\_z for x\_4. The only lattice relation among the first four generators is g\_a+g\_d=g\_b+g\_c. Reducing monomials by ad=bc gives the monoid algebra presentation. Thus (7) is the normal excellent complete germ of n1. Its dimension is four. It is regular where any of a,b,c,d is invertible, by solving its equation for the opposite variable. At P=(a,b,c,d), the equation has no linear term in the four normal variables, so that localization has embedding dimension four and dimension three. Its singular locus is exactly the positive-dimensional line P, over every k, including characteristic two. This is a normal nonisolated germ.

The Newton polyhedron of J has the following COMPLETE presentation: the cone inequalities and
\[
 \langle x,w_+\rangle\ge1,\quad \langle x,w_-\rangle\ge1,\qquad
 w_\pm=(1/2,\ \pm1/6,\ \mp1/6,\ 1/4).                  \tag{8}
\]
Both normals are interior to the dual cone: their values on the five generators are respectively (1/2,2/3,1/3,1/2,1/4) and (1/2,1/3,2/3,1/2,1/4). To check completeness without assuming a program's answer, the section at x\_4=0 is the cone over the unit square x\_1=1, cut by (3x\_1+x\_2-x\_3)/6>=1 and (3x\_1-x\_2+x\_3)/6>=1. Its four vertices are (2,0,0),(3,3,0),(3,0,3),(2,2,2). This follows by considering the four square-edge equalities x\_2=0, x\_3=0, x\_1=x\_2, x\_1=x\_3; intersections of both cutting planes force x\_2=x\_3 and x\_1=2, whose endpoints are (2,0,0) and (2,2,2). Each individual cutting plane's remaining endpoint is the corresponding opposite square corner at x\_1=3. There are no other vertex intersections. For 0<=x\_4<=4, the right sides for this three-dimensional section are 1-x\_4/4. For x\_4>4 the section is the whole recession cone. Consequently the full polyhedron has precisely those four vertices with fourth coordinate zero and (0,0,0,4), and recession cone T. These are exactly the five generating exponents in (7), proving (8).

Normalize by the monomial primary gauge m. The two contacts v\_+,v\_- in n1 have generator values
\[
 (a,b,c,d,z)=(2,8/3,4/3,2,1),\quad (2,4/3,8/3,2,1),
\]
respectively. Both have v(m)=1 and v(J)=4. At EVERY interior monomial valuation, a+b and c+d have their least term values without cancellation, so v(K)=v(m). This also follows at the two contacts directly from the displayed numbers. For an arbitrary semivaluation in V\_m, containment m\textasciicircum{}2 subset K subset m gives 1<=v(K)<=2. Define for any real delta>=0
\[
 f_\delta=-v(J)+\delta\big(v(K)-v(\mathfrak m)\big).
                                                                    \tag{9}
\]
This is a finite continuous obstacle on the entire compact boundary. It is at least H=-v(J), and agrees with H at both contacts. By n1 its greatest geometric D envelope is exactly
\[
 P(f_\delta)=-v(J).
                                                                    \tag{10}
\]
For delta=1/2 this is a rational signed PRIMARY model obstacle:
\[
 f_{1/2}=\big(v(K)-v(J^2\mathfrak m)\big)/2.
\]
The primary product blowup principalizes J,K,m, so it is the evaluation of an actual signed exceptional rational Cartier divisor there. Its obstacle need not be nef. Its envelope is the actual negative effective nef Cartier profile on Bl\_J(R), not positivity conferred by upper regularization. Since J subset m\textasciicircum{}2, f\_\{1/2\}<=-3/2 throughout V\_m; it is a genuinely negative example.

To prove the obstacle is genuinely nonmonomial, consider the quotient map to k[[r,h,z]] given by
\[
 a=c=r,\qquad b=d=r(h-1),\qquad z=z,
\]
followed by the monomial valuation with r,h,z weights 1,1,3. The relation ad=bc is identically satisfied. The kernel on R is (c-a,d-b): the quotient is k[[a,b,z]], and substitution a=r,b=r(h-1) is injective because replacing b by a+b sends its two coordinates to r,rh, whose distinct monomials r\textasciicircum{}\{i+j\}h\textasciicircum{}j have distinct exponent pairs. This is a prime support strictly below m. It is an allowed centred semivaluation, normalized already by v(m)=1, and
\[
 v(a,b,c,d,z)=(1,1,1,1,3),\quad v(K)=2,\quad v(J)=2.
\]
The equalities a+b=c+d=rh hold over every field, including characteristic two. At the monomial valuation w\_0=(1,0,0,3) on R, the monomial weights of all five generators are identical, but w\_0(K)=1 and w\_0(J)=2. Therefore
\[
 f_{1/2}(v)=-3/2,\qquad f_{1/2}(w_0)=-2.
\]
They have the same values on EVERY monomial by additivity. Hence (9) cannot be a function only of monomial weights. This is an actual nonmonomial continuous signed primary/model obstacle, not a coordinate re-description of a weight-only obstacle.

The retained singular-supported valuation killing P and giving z value one has v(m)=v(K)=1, v(J)=4, and f\_delta=-4. Its Jacobian value v((a,b,c,d)) is infinite. Formula (10) includes this point and all other supports. No nonprimary correction is divided by an index, and no support is discarded. The proof uses finite contact inequalities and genuine primary profiles. It is independent of the Frobenius/test-ideal route and works over imperfect fields and all characteristics. It proves an obstacle sector, not CE for arbitrary obstacles on this ring. It does not prove that this ring lacks a finite regular cover, and no such premise is needed.

Evidence: the own program contact\_certificate.py enumerates the five choose four candidate positive facets and the seven choose four candidate vertices by exact rational row reduction. Its observed output is two positive facet normals, five vertices, and PASS on 23 explicitly enumerated positive rational monomial-weight cases. It records the normalized contacts and the exact cancellation and singular-support values above in contact-output.json. The polyhedral and semivaluation arguments above are mathematical proofs; the program checks only this finite certificate. Rerun: python contact\_certificate.py. Inputs, source and full output are in contact-input.json, contact\_certificate.py and contact-output.json; no supplied program is executed or imported.

\subsection{A mixed-characteristic normal nonisolated example}

The general theorem in n1 also yields an explicit sector outside equicharacteristic field germs. Fix any prime p, take V=Z\_p with uniformizer pi=p, and put
\[
 R_V=V[[a,b,c,d]]/(ad-bc),\quad \mathfrak n=(\pi,a,b,c,d),\quad
 K_V=(a+b,c+d,\pi)+\mathfrak n^2.                         \tag{11}
\]
This is a complete excellent normal domain of dimension four with a singular line (a,b,c,d). Here are explicit checks, so no general mixed-characteristic positivity theorem is assumed. The standard monomials after replacing ad by bc form a V-basis, also after completion degree by degree. The parametrization a=xy,b=xw,c=ty,d=tw in V[[x,y,t,w]] identifies distinct standard monomials with distinct exponent vectors. Thus the quotient is a domain. It is a hypersurface in a regular local ring, so is S2. At a prime not containing all four a,b,c,d, a partial derivative d,-c,-b or a is a unit. In the regular ambient localization the defining equation is outside the square of the maximal ideal (apply that derivation), so the quotient localization is regular. The ideal (a,b,c,d) has height three, by the catenary hypersurface dimension formula and quotient V. Every height-one localization is regular, and Serre's R1+S2 criterion proves normality. At the generic point of that line the quadric has embedding dimension four and dimension three, hence is singular. These CM/S2 facts check this SPECIFIC hypersurface; they are not imposed on the general theorem or formal audit.

The n-adic graded ring is exactly
\[
 \operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak n}(R_V)
   =\mathbf F_p[\Pi,A,B,C,D]/(AD-BC),                       \tag{12}
\]
a domain. The regular ambient ring has polynomial associated graded ring. For any h there, ord(h(ad-bc))=ord(h)+2, because its associated graded ring is a domain. Its initial form is in(h)(AD-BC). Thus the initial ideal of the principal relation is precisely (AD-BC), with no extra initial relation. The quotient polynomial ring is a domain by the same monomial parametrization. Consequently nu=ord\_n is a valuation, not merely a subadditive order, and nu(n)=1.

For EVERY centred semivaluation v with v(n)=1, membership f in n\textasciicircum{}r gives v(f)>=r, so v(f)>=nu(f). Selecting an element of least finite v-value in a primary ideal I gives v(I)>=nu(I). Every negative rational or real primary profile g therefore satisfies g(v)<=g(nu). Uniform limits and the ACTUAL infima defining D preserve this inequality. This is a one-point contact certificate at nu, proved directly; no count of normalized-blowup components is needed.

K\_V is proper primary and n\textasciicircum{}2 subset K\_V subset n. Since a+b has order one, nu(K\_V)=1. For any delta>=0 the finite continuous obstacle
\[
 F_\delta=-v(\mathfrak n)+\delta\big(v(K_V)-v(\mathfrak n)\big)           \tag{13}
\]
is at least -1 and equals -1 at nu. Every D competitor below it is at most -1 at nu, hence everywhere. The primary profile -v(n) is itself a geometric competitor, proving
\[
 P(F_\delta)=-v(\mathfrak n)=-1
\]
on the entire normalized boundary. For delta=1/2, (13) is (v(K\_V)-v(n\textasciicircum{}3))/2, an actual rational signed primary/model obstacle on the product primary blowup. Its greatest geometric envelope is actual nef Cartier. Since v(K\_V)<=2, this obstacle lies in [-1,-1/2].

It is cancellation-sensitive even with the uniformizer weight retained. Map a=c=r,b=d=r(h-1) into V[[r,h]] and use the weighted valuation with pi,r,h weights 3,1,1. For a formal series sum c\_ij r\textasciicircum{}i h\textasciicircum{}j its value is min(3 ord\_pi(c\_ij)+i+j); its associated graded coefficient/monomial ring over F\_p is a domain, proving multiplicativity. Pullback is centred, with prime support (c-a,d-b) strictly below n, and
\[
 v(\pi,a,b,c,d)=(3,1,1,1,1),\qquad v(K_V)=2.
\]
The matching monomial valuation on R\_V has the same generator and uniformizer weights but K\_V value one. It exists by the standard monomial expansion over V, with value 3 ord\_pi(coefficient)+total monomial degree. Its associated graded ring is the domain monoid algebra over F\_p with a uniformizer variable, so distinct monomials cannot cancel. Thus F\_(1/2) has values -1/2 and -1 at these equal-weight semivaluations. The supported valuation killing (a,b,c,d) and giving pi value one has K\_V value one and envelope -1, even though the ideal (a,b,c,d) has infinite value. Every support is retained.

This is an unconditional mixed-characteristic excellent normal nonisolated obstacle sector relative to G331. It is not arbitrary-obstacle mixed-characteristic CE. The proofs above establish its universal statements. The own finite program checks only the equicharacteristic Newton instance and is not a p-adic ring computation.


\section{n3. Exact gauges, compatible normalization contacts, and geometric curve clipping}

Support: incoming qualified G331 and earlier own n1,n2. No B341/E350 product or energy result is used.

The contact theorem of n1 applies to every excellent germ and is homogeneous on rays. If b is another primary gauge, write d(v)=v(b) on V\_a, T(v)=v/d(v), and transport obstacle, barrier and contacts by
\[
 f_b(Tv)=f_a(v)/d(v),\quad H_b(Tv)=H_a(v)/d(v),\quad x_{j,b}=T(x_{j,a}).
\]
The positive bounded continuous denominator preserves inequalities, contact equalities, uniform convergence and actual decreasing representations. G331 gives precisely this bijection of C,D competitors. Taking their suprema proves the exact envelope rule
\[
 P_b(f_b)(Tv)=P_a(f_a)(v)/d(v).
\]
Substitution supplies the exact three-primary-gauge cocycle. The contact normals remain centred under every primary section; the barrier remains -v(J)/q in the new section. Completion transport is the already granted all-support homeomorphism and exact primary contraction, not a new algebraization or equivalence of geometric model categories.

Here is a full-fibre normalization extension of the new contact sector, which does not assume general CE upstairs. Let R be any excellent reduced germ with finite normalization S, and suppose each positive-dimensional normal local centre S\_i is of the saturated monoid type of n1. Take barriers H\_i=-v(J\_i)/q\_i as in n1, or the zero barrier. Require their tuple H to be constant on EVERY restriction fibre of rho:X\_S->X\_R. Qualified G331 positively descends the continuous tuple to h in C\_R. Let f be any finite continuous obstacle on X\_R such that f>=h, and for every nonzero barrier's finite contact x\_\{ij\} require
\[
 f(\rho(x_{ij}))=H_i(x_{ij}).
\]
For a D\_R competitor u<=f, its pullback on each nonzero branch is at most H\_i by n1. On a zero-barrier branch its nonpositivity gives the same inequality. Thus u<=h by surjectivity of rho, while h is itself a competitor. Its greatest D\_R envelope is h. The same statement holds for a bounded-above extended upper semicontinuous obstacle satisfying these bounds and contacts. A contact condition at one source point never replaces the imposed FULL-fibre compatibility of H.

Specifically, if c is the conductor, G331 identifies a fibre as a singleton when v(c)<infinity. When v(c)=infinity, lifts kill c and equality of their restrictions through S/c -> R/c is exactly the identification rule. The finite-value locus is open, the infinite-value locus closed. Both are retained in the contact argument. No value v(c)/m is used as a uniform error. Compatibility includes all branches, nonminimal supports, mixed-zero and partial-bottom patterns. This theorem does not assert that an incompatible tuple of source envelopes descends positively or that an arbitrary fibre maximum is psh.

On EVERY excellent reduced curve, normalization has the finite collection of DVR local centres over the closed point, including multiple branches on one irreducible component. A regular conductor element has finite order on every branch, so normalized boundary fibres are singleton. On each DVR the marked point is an actual effective Cartier divisor and there are no contracted integral curves to test. All finite nonpositive coordinates are independently geometric there; G331's positive full-fibre continuous descent gives all finite nonpositive branch vectors downstairs. For an extended nonpositive vector u, max(u,-j) is an actual decreasing sequence of these C vectors with infimum u. Thus D is exactly every extended nonpositive branch vector. For any branch obstacle phi its greatest geometric D minorant is min(phi,0). This is the exact complete ideal-envelope comparison by G331's independently proved cone comparison. The branch coordinate for two primary gauges rescales by ord\_i(a)/ord\_i(b), with the exact cocycle above.

Nilpotents remain invisible and are removed by reduction; if the local reduction has dimension zero the centred boundary is empty and statements concern its unique empty function. Literal classical or CLD logarithmic radial extension classes are not changed: their stated multibranch mixed-zero obstruction remains. The boundary class may contain (-1,0) without such a literal radial extension. At a smooth affine CLOSED germ over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, G331 identifies this exact C,D class with the full published BFJ all-semivaluation class, with bottom adjoined. Wherever our contact theorem applies at that specialization, its greatest minorant is therefore the BFJ envelope in the SAME class. This does not extend BFJ's published hypotheses to arbitrary smooth excellent, imperfect or mixed-characteristic germs. Dimension-one and empty cases above are direct.

Artifacts: n3.md, proof-companion.md and P12.3-contact-envelopes.tex, retaining the full incoming G331 proof/annotation/ledger. Rerun delivery and data checks: python prepare\_delivery.py. This scope leaves P12.4 products, P12.5 energy and P12.6 full operator theory separate.


\section{n4. Current401 audit, formal reconstruction boundary, and unchanged original residual}

Support: G331 and earlier own n1,n2,n3 for the new contact theorem, geometric comparison, gauges and curves. Supplied current401, ROOT392, native verdicts, programs, ledgers and inherited B341/E350 are DATA, not grants. None is listed as support or used as an unproved mathematical premise of n1--n3.

The seven actual current401 FINAL objects were read in their entirety, all five fields. The separate expanded JSON agrees in every field except actual n2's two spacing-command backslashes around its d tensor1 arrow label; the displayed algebra is identical. Both complete objects and the full terminal framing remain separately retained. The proof companion is exactly the expanded text join. The current standalone is retained byte-for-byte, including its full qualified G331, B341 and E350 appendices and every annotation/ledger/qualification. Incoming G331's whole 93375-byte text occurs literally in that standalone. Neither an inherited B341/E350 acceptance label nor a native PASS is an additional incoming envelope premise. Data retention and duplicate identity confer no fresh proof/source reading credit.

The following is my independent reconstruction of the active formal chain and the limits of the present audit. It concerns complete normal characteristic-p rings with perfect coefficient/residue field, not arbitrary original germs.

Completed algebra: for a finite complete local k-module V, continuous duality gives V=(V\textasciicircum{}o)\textasciicircum{}*, with V\textasciicircum{}o the union of the duals of its finite-dimensional adic quotients. Artin--Rees identifies the topology of a finite submodule with its induced topology; linear functionals extend in a finite quotient. Thus continuous duality is exact. The identity V completed-tensor\_k W=(V\textasciicircum{}o tensor\_k W\textasciicircum{}o)\textasciicircum{}* proves exactness in both slots. Applying kernels of two finite presentation matrices then proves the FULL Hom factorization
\[
 \operatorname{Hom}_{R\widehat\otimes_k R}(M\widehat\otimes_k N,R\widehat\otimes_k R)
 =\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)\widehat\otimes_k\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,R).
\]
Paired generators generate every map; individual maps need not be decomposable. Perfect coefficients and exponent grouping identify the root of S=R completed-tensor\_k R with R\textasciicircum{}(1/q) completed-tensor\_k R\textasciicircum{}(1/q). Exactness applied twice to the root injections proves S reduced. A parameter ring k[[x\_1,...,x\_d]] makes R finite torsion-free; embedding it into a finite free module and applying completed exactness makes S finite torsion-free over k[[x,y]]. Its minimal primes contract to zero, so every minimal quotient has dimension 2d. Normality or Cohen--Macaulayness of S is not used.

Different/lift: for a fixed k-parameter normalization A, the adjugate of a square matrix of differences of the presentation equations annihilates all diagonal generators. Its product image is the relative Jacobian minor; hence the Kahler different is contained in the Noether different. If its generic extension is separable, a Noether-different element d is the product image of d times the separability idempotent. The identity
\[
 dw=\sum_i r_i\operatorname{Tr}(s_iw)
\]
base changes through the linearly disjoint purely inseparable K\textasciicircum{}(1/q)/K. For w in R\textasciicircum{}(1/q), trace coefficients are integral and lie in the fraction field of the normal regular A\textasciicircum{}(1/q); they therefore lie in A\textasciicircum{}(1/q). This proves d R\textasciicircum{}(1/q) subset P\_q=A\textasciicircum{}(1/q)[R], and P\_q is finite FREE over R because its generic multiplication is injective and A\textasciicircum{}(1/q) tensor\_A R is an R-free torsion-free module. It does not make R free over A.

For T=R\textasciicircum{}(1/q), lift multiplication from the B-free module P\_q completed-tensor T through B=R completed-tensor T -> T. Compose with ROOT multiplication d on the first T and 1 completed-tensor phi on the target. After multiplication into R its value is phi(dxy)=d phi(xy). This holds on all completed elements by finite-module continuity, factors through the SURJECTIVE root multiplication, and sends its ENTIRE kernel into the ordinary diagonal ideal. The lift induces output d phi. In F\_*\textasciicircum{}e notation its source multiplier is d\textasciicircum{}q. Multiplication by d\textasciicircum{}q in the root module instead gives output d\textasciicircum{}q phi. The latter is the historical immutable false paragraph, not the corrected401 formula. A concrete check in k[[x]], q=3, phi selecting x\textasciicircum{}(2/3), gives phi(x\textasciicircum{}3 x\textasciicircum{}(2/3))=x\textasciicircum{}3 while x phi(x\textasciicircum{}(2/3))=x. The corrected lift is consistent and the whole root kernel is essential.

The fixed-common-field sum of relative Jacobian ideals is exactly Wang's formal Jacobian, not an unrestricted choice of normalization fields.     The label “ideal-psh” is a scope marker, not a comparison theorem. No argument here iden-

    The most direct comparison can nevertheless be computed exactly whenever the ﬁnite
normalization is a union of q closed discs, is an isomorphism away from one point, and its
conductor contains suﬃciently high separated branch powers. By Book Theorem 70.1.9, a
homogeneous proﬁle c ∈ [−∞, 0]q has a literal logarithmic radial extension which is classically

                                        {0} ∪ [−∞, 0)q .
The positive direction forms the normalized tuple whose retained components are the mono-
mials tki i , whose −∞-components are zero, and descends it through the conductor to one
analytic function; scaled logarithms and a decreasing limit then give all remaining slopes.
For the converse, a zero branch forces a nonnegative nodal value by upper semicontinuity;
any simultaneously negative branch then contradicts its closed-disc Shilov maximum prin-
ciple. Hence the mixed-zero ideal proﬁle (−1, 0) is excluded, while every proﬁle with all
coordinates strictly negative or −∞ does extend. The conductor realizes the required branch-
wise monomials by single downstairs analytic functions, so this supplies the exact branch-
compatibility rule throughout the stated disc-normalized curve range. The ordinary multinode
theorem Book Theorem 70.1.10 records the explicit coordinate-ring instance. At the oppo-

is therefore genuinely multibranch. The result does not decide whether a diﬀerent boundary-
trace comparison exists, or treat a singular germ outside this normalization-and-conductor
range.
    There is a genuine, but diﬀerent, global boundary case. Over an algebraically closed
ﬁeld of characteristic zero, the global trivially-valued framework used in [BJ23, §2] treats an
integral projective variety without initially assuming normality: it supplies a global psh class,
its ﬁnite-energy space and energy, and a Monge–Ampère operator with dense ﬁnite-energy
image. Exact surjectivity there is equivalent to the envelope property, which that source
records in the smooth case. This global construction neither selects a normalized link for an
excellent local germ nor supplies the curve-local conductor realization above, local bounded
products, or the required local ﬁnite-map formula. It therefore does not discharge any part
of Problem 6.1.
    The remaining programme tests higher-dimensional normal crossings, quotient singulari-
ties, and purely inseparable universal homeomorphisms. Any claim of independence of psh
or intersection constructions from boundary choices must respect the established radial com-
parison and conductor quotient. Relative b-divisors can be deﬁned on suitable model sys-
tems, but beyond the normalized boundary and, in dimension one, the branch link, its ideal-
psh candidate and envelope, its arbitrary ﬁnite-map pullback, its branch-surjective generic
trace and conductor descent, its ﬁnite conditional-expectation calculus, its ﬁnite-ﬂat canoni-

and intersection-theoretic package is presently open.
    Two older local-volume questions should not be carried forward as open. For the
Boucksom–de Fernex–Favre local volume, Yuchen Zhang proves a positive dimension-
dependent lower bound for every nonzero volume of an isolated Gorenstein singularity and

resolved history, not additional problems.

The native assertion phi(d\textasciicircum{}q z)=d phi(z), for an R-linear phi:R\textasciicircum{}(1/q)->R, is false. In k[[x]] over a perfect field of characteristic3, q=3, use the free root basis 1,x\textasciicircum{}(1/3),x\textasciicircum{}(2/3) and the linear functional selecting the last basis vector. With d=x and z=x\textasciicircum{}(2/3), phi(d\textasciicircum{}q z)=x\textasciicircum{}3 whereas d phi(z)=x. The corrected formula is phi(dz)=d phi(z). Root multiplication by d is underlying Frobenius-source multiplication by d\textasciicircum{}q. The complete repair and full rooted-kernel argument are proved in n2; this note does not give the immutable paragraph a positive verdict.

For finite continuous f on the compact primary section X, define p(f)=sup\{u in D:u<=f\}. A sufficiently negative primary constant is a competitor. If g\_i decreases in C to u<=f, the open sets \{g\_i<f+epsilon\} cover X. Compactness and directedness select one term satisfying the inequality everywhere. Its negative constant shift g\_i-epsilon is in C and below f, and is at least u-epsilon. Therefore C and D give the same raw supremum. It is finite, bounded, lower semicontinuous and nonexpansive in the uniform norm. Negative shifts in both directions prove the latter; no positive-translation invariance is used.

If p(f) is continuous, finitely many continuous competitors and their maximum approximate it uniformly from below, so p(f) belongs to C. If p(f) belongs to D, upper semicontinuity plus the preceding lower semicontinuity makes it continuous. Any maximal D minorant is greatest, since its maximum with another minorant is again a minorant. Conversely a greatest minorant equals the raw supremum. If the upper regularization p(f)\textasciicircum{}* belongs to D, continuity of f gives p(f)\textasciicircum{}*<=f, so it too is a competitor and equals p(f). Thus raw continuity, C positivity, D positivity, a greatest/maximal D minorant, and positive upper regularization are equivalent. Regularization by itself is not positivity recognition.

Actual decreasing closure of D needs a proof. On each normal centre G331 gives the zero dichotomy: a nonzero D function is everywhere strictly negative and hence bounded above by -c on the compact section. For u\_i in D decreasing to u, either all terms are zero or a tail has this common bound. Given finite continuous F>u, compactness of the open strict tests selects u\_i<F everywhere, then a continuous representing term g with u\_i<=g<F and g<-c/2. A small positive b keeps (1-b)g below F and makes it strictly above u at each finite point, with bottom automatic. The family of continuous C majorants strictly above u is downward directed: apply this insertion to the continuous minimum of two majorants. Upper semicontinuity of u and a Urysohn cutoff give, at each point and finite t>u(x), a continuous F>u with F(x)<t. Insertion then shows this single decreasing net has infimum u. On a reduced germ pull back to the finitely many normal centres, apply the argument there, and use G331 full-fibre D descent. This avoids flattening nested representations and assumes no increasing closure.

If CE holds (p(f) in C for every continuous f), the finite continuous nonpositive majorants of min(phi,0), for bounded-above extended upper semicontinuous phi, are directed by minima and have that infimum. Their envelopes form a single decreasing C net. Its infimum is in D by the preceding closure proof, is below phi, and dominates every D competitor. This is the greatest D envelope. The same reasoning proves commutation with decreasing obstacle nets having a specified upper semicontinuous limit. The statements include poles and bottom.

For another primary gauge b, d(v)=v(b) and its inverse are bounded positive continuous. The section map T(v)=v/d(v) and the homogeneous rule u\_b(Tv)=u\_a(v)/d(v) give a bijection of competitors. Hence p\_b(f\_b)(Tv)=p\_a(f\_a)(v)/d(v), with the exact three-gauge cocycle. G331 already proves the all-support completion homeomorphism, exact primary contraction and C/D identification. The envelope transport is a corollary; it is not new algebraization or model-category equivalence.

The Jensen calculation was also checked, but remains a reduction. For positive Radon subprobabilities set J\_x=\{mu:h(x)<=integral h dmu for all h in C\}. They are nonempty compact convex sets with closed graph. Separate (f,t), t>p(f)(x), from the closure of \{(g,s):some h in C has h<=g, s<=h(x)\} in C(X) times R. Nonexpansivity keeps the point outside that closure. A separating functional has form mu(g)-alpha s, with mu positive and alpha>=0. Testing (-a,-a) rules out alpha=0, since then mu(X)=0. Normalize alpha=1; testing (h,h(x)) gives the Jensen inequalities, and h=-1 gives mass<=1. Let t decrease and use compactness to obtain p(f)(x)=min\_\{mu in J\_x\} integral f dmu. Conversely, failure of weak lower hemicontinuity of J\_x is detected by finitely many continuous tests. Their compact convex projections avoid a fixed ball about a member of J\_x; unit separating vectors have a convergent subnet and retain half the gap by uniform boundedness. A fixed linear combination of the tests then has discontinuous p. Thus CE iff this correspondence is weakly lower hemicontinuous. Hahn--Banach, Riesz and positive-dual weak compactness are named ordinary foundations. No general lower hemicontinuity is proved.

\section{n2. Corrected completed free lift and full root kernel}

All statements here are reconstructed; neither corrected396 nor ROOT392 is a grant. Let R be a complete normal local domain of characteristic p>0 with perfect coefficient/residue field k. Set S=R completed-tensor\_k R, multiplication mu:S->R, I=ker(mu), q=p\textasciicircum{}e, and T=R\textasciicircum{}(1/q). A presentation R=k[[u]]/(f) gives S=k[[u,v]]/(f(u),f(v)), a Noetherian complete local ring. Exponent grouping and perfect coefficient roots make both rings F-finite and identify S\textasciicircum{}(1/q)=T completed-tensor\_k T. The compatible kernel is I\textasciicircum{}(1/q), the whole kernel of root multiplication, not merely the extension of I to the root ring.

Here is the exactness argument needed for these completed tensors. A finite module V over R is the inverse limit of its finite-dimensional k quotients; its continuous dual V\textasciicircum{}o is their direct-limit dual. Artin--Rees makes a finite submodule's induced topology cofinal with its adic topology. A continuous functional on a submodule extends through a sufficiently deep finite quotient. Thus continuous duality is exact on the relevant finite-module sequences. Algebraic vector-space tensor and duality are exact, and
\[
 V\widehat\otimes_k W=(V^o\otimes_k W^o)^*.
\]
This proves completed exactness in either slot. It does not appeal to completion over an uncompleted non-Noetherian tensor ring. Applied twice to R->R\textasciicircum{}(1/p), it makes S->S\textasciicircum{}(1/p) injective. This is the Frobenius map under the root presentation, so S is reduced.

Present finite R modules M,N by finite free modules. In S\textasciicircum{}(ab), impose the M-relation matrix, then the N-relation matrix. Completed exactness identifies the first kernel with Hom\_R(M,R) completed-tensor R\textasciicircum{}b and the second with the corresponding completed tensor of Hom modules. Therefore
\[
\operatorname{Hom}_S(M\widehat\otimes_k N,S)
=\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)\widehat\otimes_k\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,R).
\]
This is the full Hom factorization, including finite ideals/twists and every S Cartier map. Finite paired generators generate the right-hand module; no decomposability assertion for individual maps is needed.

If a regular Noetherian subring A makes R module finite, integral locality makes A local. Its maximal-adic and R maximal-adic topologies on R are cofinal. Exact completion embeds A-hat in R, so A-hat/A is a finite A module, with zero residue quotient. Nakayama gives A=A-hat. The residue field F has finite extension k; perfection of k and [k:F]=[k\textasciicircum{}p:F\textasciicircum{}p] force F perfect. Cohen structure then gives A=F[[x]], whose roots are finite free. This broader ROOT392 claim is valid, but the Jacobian sum below uses only the fixed common field k.

Fix A=k[[x\_1,...,x\_d]] inside R, finite over A. Let K\_A=Fitt\_0 Omega\_(R/A) and N\_A=mu\_A(Ann ker(mu\_A)) in R tensor\_A R. A finite polynomial presentation R=A[z]/(g) expresses differences g(z tensor 1)-g(1 tensor z) as a matrix times the diagonal generators z\_i tensor1-1tensor z\_i. Each square adjugate makes its determinant annihilate all these generators. After multiplication its determinant is the corresponding relative Jacobian minor. Hence K\_A subset N\_A. This uses ordinary finite relative differentials and no CM or A-flatness.

For K\_A nonzero the fraction field extension L/K is separable. If d in N\_A, choose z=sum r\_i tensor s\_i annihilating the diagonal with product d. Over L tensor\_K L, z is d times the separability idempotent. The trace in the second slot gives
\[
d w=\sum_i r_i\operatorname{Tr}(s_i w).
\]
The purely inseparable extension K\textasciicircum{}(1/q)/K is linearly disjoint from L/K, and L K\textasciicircum{}(1/q)=L\textasciicircum{}(1/q). The same identity holds there. Elements of R\textasciicircum{}(1/q) are integral over A\textasciicircum{}(1/q), so their trace coefficients are integral and in its fraction field. Normality of the regular A\textasciicircum{}(1/q) puts them in A\textasciicircum{}(1/q). Consequently dT subset A\textasciicircum{}(1/q)[R]. The multiplication of P=A\textasciicircum{}(1/q) tensor\_A R into L\textasciicircum{}(1/q) is injective: its generic map is an isomorphism and the free R module P is torsion-free over A. Thus P is the indicated submodule of T and is finite free over R. Freeness of R over A is not asserted.

Set B=R completed-tensor\_k T. The multiplication B->T is surjective and B-linear. The module P completed-tensor\_k T is free over B, so its multiplication into T lifts to a B-linear map Psi into B, by lifting its finite free basis. Compose
\[
T\widehat\otimes_k T\xrightarrow{,d\otimes1,}
P\widehat\otimes_k T\xrightarrow{\Psi}
R\widehat\otimes_k T\xrightarrow{1\widehat\otimes\phi}S
\]
for any R-linear phi:T->R. This is S-linear with the Frobenius root source action. On pure tensors, applying mu gives phi(dxy)=d phi(xy). Finite-module continuity extends this equality to the completed tensor. Its reduction therefore factors through the surjective root multiplication to T. It takes the ENTIRE kernel I\textasciicircum{}(1/q) into I, and induces the OUTPUT multiple d phi. In the identification F\_*\textasciicircum{}e z->z\textasciicircum{}(1/q), the first arrow uses underlying source multiplier d\textasciicircum{}q. Multiplication by d\textasciicircum{}q in T would instead induce d\textasciicircum{}q phi, the immutable error demonstrated in n1. No claim about only pure tensors or the ordinary extended diagonal kernel suffices.

Let D\_e be the quotient-restriction image of all compatible S maps in C\_e=Hom\_R(F\_*\textasciicircum{}e R,R). These finite kernel/image modules form a Cartier algebra: lift left/right scalars arbitrarily to S and compose compatible maps. The root kernel remains preserved. Summing lifts over finitely many parameter normalizations proves J\_norm C\_e subset D\_e for every degree, where J\_norm=sum\_A K\_A.

Wang's fixed-coefficient-field Definition4.1/4.2 and whole Lemma4.3 identify this sum with the formal Jacobian Fitt\_d of continuous differentials. Finite residue fields require no generic rational-coordinate assumption: prescribe a basis modulo m\textasciicircum{}2, and at each stage avoid the finitely many nonmaximal minimal primes of subset-generated ideals. Discard contained primes. For incomparable P\_i, choose a\_i in m\textasciicircum{}2 intersect all other P\_j but outside P\_i, using products and prime avoidance. Add a\_i only where the original representative lies in P\_i. Its cotangent coset is unchanged and every bad prime is avoided. The height theorem/catenarity preserves the expected drop for every subset, so each d-subset is a parameter system. Formal coordinate changes preserving the cotangent basis have invertible Jacobian. Their complementary minors give the required finite sum exactly as in Wang. This explicitly repairs the finite-field reading boundary.

The singular-locus criterion used is ONLY for reduced equidimensional complete equicharacteristic rings with perfect residue. \section{n3. BIG minima, late tails, and the actual completed diagonal}

Use the completed module and lift theorem of n2, not a grant from396. Let B be reduced excellent Noetherian F-finite. Let C be a Cartier subalgebra with finite degree modules and C\_0=B. Assume c in B\textasciicircum{}o has B\_c regular, all C\_e become the full Hom modules there, and finitely many regular-element pair ideals a\_i become units there. These explicit regular-open hypotheses will be verified for the product and diagonal; no graded finite generation is presumed. Put r\_i(e)=ceil(t\_i(p\textasciicircum{}e-1)). Stability means that all maps in C\_e take F\_*\textasciicircum{}e((product a\_i\textasciicircum{}r\_i(e))H) into H. The twisted maps compose because r\_i(e)+p\textasciicircum{}e r\_i(f)>=r\_i(e+f).

Every stable H meeting B\textasciicircum{}o has H\_c=B\_c. At a regular maximal localization of B\_c, F-finiteness and Kunz give a finite free Frobenius module. A regular h in H is outside n\textasciicircum{}[q] for large q, since n\textasciicircum{}[q] subset n\textasciicircum{}q and Krull intersection. Thus F\_*h is primitive in that free module and a linear map sends it to1. Hom localization holds by finite presentation; localized stability gives the unit ideal. This holds at every maximal localization. Kunz is the named ordinary theorem at exactly regular Noetherian characteristic-p rings; its full statement in Smolkinv3 2.3 was read, not its entire original historical proof.

There is one universal power of c in EVERY such H. Choose a positive degree q. Evaluation at1 splits on B\_c; clear denominators to obtain theta in C\_e with theta(F\_*1)=c\textasciicircum{}a. Choose B\_0 so c\textasciicircum{}(q B\_0) belongs to that degree's pair coefficient ideal. For the least n with c\textasciicircum{}n in H, stability and the Frobenius scalar rule give c\textasciicircum{}(B\_0+ceil(n/q)+a) in H. Therefore
\[
n\le B_0+a+\lceil n/q\rceil\le B_0+a+n/q+1,
\qquad n\le\frac{q(B_0+a+1)}{q-1}.
\]
Fix an integer L at least this bound. The intersection of all stable ideals meeting B\textasciicircum{}o is stable and contains c\textasciicircum{}L in B\textasciicircum{}o, so it is the actual smallest such ideal tau. This is BIG, not finitistic. The ideal generated by all twisted maps of an arbitrary regular d, with degree zero included, is stable and generically nonzero, and therefore contains c\textasciicircum{}L. Thus the construction supplies the required universal BIG test element, rather than assuming arbitrary-Cartier-algebra existence.

If d belongs to tau intersect B\textasciicircum{}o, every late tail generated by twisted images of dB lies in tau. Composition shows the tail is stable. On B\_c the pair ideals are units; for each maximal localization a sufficiently large degree sends the regular d to1 by the preceding primitive-vector argument. Hence the tail is generically nonzero and minimality makes it equal tau. This holds for EVERY cutoff E, not merely for all degrees starting at0.

Both exponent conventions ceil(t\_i q) and ceil(t\_i(q-1)) give the same ideal and all their late tails. Their gaps are bounded by ceil(t\_i)+1 independently of e. Construct the minima for both conventions by the same argument and choose a common regular seed in their intersection. Multiplication by a fixed regular element of product a\_i\textasciicircum{}(ceil(t\_i)+1) is enough to bridge the bounded gaps. Since a seed in tau can be multiplied by a regular element and remains a seed, the two tail sums sandwich each other. The same argument proves power invariance tau((a\textasciicircum{}r)\textasciicircum{}(t/r))=tau(a\textasciicircum{}t): the exponents ceil(qt) and r ceil(qt/r) differ by at most r-1. No finite-tail approximation or Q-Gorenstein index enters.

Localization of these ideals follows from finite Hom localization and shared nonzero seeds. Full-algebra completion is also exact for excellent F-finite normal local A: the m-adic and Frobenius filtrations are cofinal, so F\_*A completes to F\_*(A-hat), and finite Hom commutes with faithful flat completion. Extending tau\_A is stable, giving tau\_hat subset tau\_A A-hat. Choose c in A with A\_c regular and pair ideals unit. Regular formal fibres make A-hat\_c regular; the same cleared splitting supplies a common c\textasciicircum{}L in tau\_hat. Its contraction is nonzero and stable, giving the reverse inclusion. An arbitrary nonzero formal ideal is never assumed to have nonzero contraction. This proves the completion rule for full algebras only.

If J C\_e subset D\_e, the correct comparison is J tau\_C subset tau\_D. Choose a regular seed in both minima. The C late-tail formula expresses tau\_C; multiplying each output by J turns the map into a D map, whose image of the common seed lies in tau\_D. This proves the comparison without claiming J tau\_C is itself D-stable.

Return to n2's S. It is reduced F-finite and equidimensional of dimension2d. Indeed a parameter ring A\_0=k[[x\_1,...,x\_d]] makes R finite torsion-free. Clear denominators of a generic basis to embed R in a finite free A\_0 module. Completed exactness embeds S in a free module over k[[x,y]]. Every minimal prime of this finite torsion-free algebra contracts to0, so all minimal quotients have dimension2d. A nonzero d-codimensional Jacobian minor j of R yields the block minor j(u)j(v) in Jac(S). At the diagonal prime I its image is j\textasciicircum{}2, nonzero in R. The exact reduced-equidimensional perfect-residue singular-locus criterion of n2 makes S\_I regular. No S normality or product-domain assertion is needed.

Choose regular a\_0 in a and b\_0 in b and set c\_S=j(u)j(v)(a\_0 tensor b\_0). Completed exactness makes multiplication by a\_0 and b\_0 injective in their slots, and similarly for j; thus c\_S is regular. Its diagonal image j\textasciicircum{}2 a\_0 b\_0 is nonzero. On S\_cS the ring is regular and both pair ideals A=aS, B=bS are units. For R's diagonal algebra D, n2 gives j C\_e subset D\_e, so localization at j is full and regular. Thus the BIG framework applies to all three actual algebras.

Let T\_S=tau\_S(A\textasciicircum{}t B\textasciicircum{}s). Its image mu(T\_S) is D-stable: compatible lifts carry its coefficient-twisted roots into T\_S, and passage to the quotient gives the required maps. Its image is nonzero because it contains mu(c\_S\textasciicircum{}L). Minimality therefore gives tau\_D(a\textasciicircum{}t b\textasciicircum{}s) subset mu(T\_S).

The completed product of tau\_R(a\textasciicircum{}t) and tau\_R(b\textasciicircum{}s), extended into S, is stable for EVERY full S Cartier map by n2's full Hom factorization and stability in each factor. It contains a regular pure tensor, again by completed exactness, so T\_S lies in this product ideal. Multiplication sends it to tau\_R(a\textasciicircum{}t) tau\_R(b\textasciicircum{}s). Combining the common-seed comparison with these two inclusions gives
\[
\operatorname{Jac}(R)\tau_R(a^t b^s)
\subset\tau_D(a^t b^s)
\subset\mu(T_S)
\subset\tau_R(a^t)\tau_R(b^s).
\]
Iteration yields Jac\textasciicircum{}(ell-1) tau(a\textasciicircum{}(ell t)) subset tau(a\textasciicircum{}t)\textasciicircum{}ell. This is the corrected direction. A primary multiplier is obtained only under isolatedness; no finite value of a nonprimary Jacobian on every support is inferred.

Verdict: the complete formal BIG/subadditivity gate is discharged for complete normal characteristic-p perfect-residue R, with no finite-type-over-field, CM, algebraizability, Q-Gorenstein or graded Cartier-finite-generation assumption. The verification uses the explicit nonzero diagonal seed, rather than a guessed image theorem. Local source and arithmetic checks are evidence, not a correctness grant.

\section{n4. Entire isolated formal envelope chain and scoped verdict}

\section{n5. New positive sector: all monomial-weight obstacles on complete normal toric germs}

Use G331 and the raw-envelope/nonexpansivity/decreasing-closure results proved in n1. This is new scoped progress on the original envelope target, valid over ANY field, including imperfect fields and every characteristic. It concerns actual geometric positivity and all geometric competitors, not a new order definition or a restriction to radial functions on a finite link.

Let M be a lattice of rank d, C\_0 a pointed full-dimensional rational polyhedral cone in M\_R, and S=C\_0 intersect M its saturated positive monoid. Let R be the completion at the monomial maximal ideal of k[S]. For precision, k[S] is the intersection, in its fraction field, of the normal Laurent polynomial ring k[M] with the valuation rings given by the finitely many primitive facet weights. On a Laurent polynomial the least facet weight is the least term weight, so these inequalities mean that every exponent belongs to C\_0 intersect M. This proves the asserted intersection and hence normality. Finite generation is the elementary rational-cone lattice-point theorem. The finite-type ring is excellent, and excellent normal completion is normal; thus R is an excellent normal local domain. Its elements are formal sums of monomials chi\textasciicircum{}u, with the maximal-adic completion topology. Fix a monomial primary gauge a. G331 supplies its full all-support compact boundary X and independently geometric C,D. These conventional algebraic foundations are used at this exact saturated positive affine-monoid setup; no perfect-field base change or torus averaging is used.

The monomial weight of v is w\_v(u)=v(chi\textasciicircum{}u). It is additive, may take infinity, and is strictly positive on nonzero monoid elements when finite. The finite-valued elements form a face of S. For finite weights w in the interior of the dual cone sigma=C\_0\textasciicircum{}vee, taking the least weight of the terms defines a monomial valuation v\_w on the completed ring. Positivity makes the least value well-defined and makes the operation compatible with the completion. Distinct monomials in its associated graded cannot cancel. Divide by w(a) to obtain its primary-section point.

Every extended monomial weight arising from v is a limit of these finite interior weights, after normalization. Indeed its finite face is cut out by a rational exposing functional lambda>=0, zero on that face and strictly positive on its complement. Extend its finite additive weight linearly from the face span to M\_R. Add N lambda, and if necessary a vanishing small positive interior functional. For large N the finitely many monoid generators outside the face become positive, and the generators inside the face have their given positive values. The outside values tend to infinity. Some primary-gauge generator has finite value; hence normalized primary values converge as well. Monomial primary profiles are continuous on all X by G331. Thus inequalities between such profiles and signed monomial obstacles, checked on finite interior weights, hold on every extended monomial weight and hence on EVERY semivaluation having that weight.

For any ideal I of R, let M(I) be the monomial ideal generated by all monomials appearing with nonzero coefficient in a finite set of formal generators. Noetherianity makes this ideal finitely generated. A monomial ideal is maximal-adically closed, since its finite-module quotient is separated; therefore each series whose terms lie in it belongs to it. Hence I subset M(I). If I contains a primary power then so does M(I). At a finite interior monomial valuation, v\_w(I)=v\_w(M(I)): the least appearing monomial realizes the value and cannot cancel. At a general semivaluation, -v(M(I))>=-v(I). This is a domination of arbitrary ideal profiles, proved by term membership, not by an averaging operation over k-rational torus points.

Consider a rational signed monomial primary obstacle on rays,
\[
F(w)=\frac{w(A)-w(B)}r,
\]
where A,B are monomial unit-or-primary ideals and r is a positive integer. Finite lattice combinations are of this form by synchronized products and sums. On X its restriction f is finite continuous. Write phi=-F, a homogeneous rational piecewise-linear function on sigma. Common normal fans of the finite exponent sets of A and B make phi linear on finitely many rational cones. Define
\[
P=\{x\in C_0:\langle x,w\rangle\ge\phi(w)\text{ for all }w\in\sigma\}.
\]
These conditions reduce to the finitely many rays of that fan, together with the cone inequalities. Thus P is a rational polyhedron. Because |f| is bounded on the a-section, phi(w)<=T w(a) for a finite T. Therefore P contains T times the Newton polyhedron of a and is nonempty. Its recession cone is exactly C\_0. The finite polyhedral vertex/recession decomposition, obtained by successively moving a nonvertex to bounding faces, gives P=conv(x\_1,...,x\_h)+C\_0, with rational vertices. Pointedness rules out a lineality factor.

Clear denominators with q so q x\_i belong to M and hence S. Add sufficiently large powers of EACH monoid generator to the ideal generated by chi\textasciicircum{}(q x\_i). These added exponents can be chosen inside qP: for a fan ray w with w(u)=0 on a nonzero monoid generator u, primaryness implies w(a)=0 and hence phi(w)=0. All remaining finite inequalities are met by a sufficiently large multiple of u. Call the resulting monomial ideal J. Its radical is the maximal ideal, unless P contains0, in which case include1 and use the unit ideal. Adding these points does not change its Newton polyhedron, which is qP. Thus
\[
h(w):=\min_{x\in P}\langle x,w\rangle=w(J)/q,
\qquad -h\le F
\]
for finite weights, and the preceding extended-weight continuity proves -v(J)/q<=f on ALL supports. This is an actual primary ideal profile and hence an actual negative effective curve-nef Cartier presentation on Bl\_J R by G331's independently proved geometric comparison/core inclusion.

It is the raw envelope among ALL geometric competitors. For any rational arbitrary-ideal profile -v(I)/l<=f, equality at monomial valuations shows -v(M(I))/l<=f there and hence everywhere, while this monomialized profile dominates the original. Each generating exponent u of M(I) satisfies u/l in P, so w(M(I))/l>=h(w); the same domination holds at extended weights by continuity. Consequently -v(I)/l<=-v(J)/q at every semivaluation. To handle C competitors, approximate by rational primary profiles, then make a negative rational gauge shift to keep them below f. Their errors vanish. N1 identifies the C and D raw suprema. Therefore
\[
p(f)=-v(J)/q\in C_{\rm geom}
\]
and this is the greatest D minorant. This controls arbitrary nonmonomial ideal profiles, their real uniform limits, and completed D competitors; it is not merely a toric-restricted supremum. The formula gives a finite rational polyhedral construction for every rational signed monomial model obstacle.

Let W be the compact image of X under all monomial evaluations. Primary monomial profile differences contain rational constants, form a lattice by products and ideal sums, and separate W using (chi\textasciicircum{}u)+a\textasciicircum{}N, whose value is min(w(u),N). The compact lattice approximation proof therefore makes their rational span uniformly dense in C(W). For every finite continuous obstacle f=F\_0 composed with the weight map, choose such rational signed obstacles tending uniformly to it. N1 nonexpansivity makes their raw envelopes uniformly Cauchy. Their limit is p(f), belongs to C\_geom, and is weight-dependent. Thus EVERY finite continuous monomial-weight obstacle has an actually positive continuous envelope, not just the rational ones.

For a bounded-above extended upper semicontinuous obstacle on W, take all finite continuous nonpositive majorants of its clipping to0, directed by minima. Their envelopes are in C\_geom by the preceding theorem and form one decreasing net. N1 decreasing closure shows its infimum is in D\_geom; it is below the obstacle and dominates every D competitor. This gives its greatest D envelope, with the appropriate upper semicontinuity, poles/bottom, and decreasing-obstacle-net stability for specified upper semicontinuous limits. The ray formulation and n1 give the exact gauge cocycle for ANY primary section; changing a monomial gauge is the immediate weight-coordinate formula. At these normal germs normalization is the identity and conductor fibres are singletons. No nonnormal monomial descent theorem is asserted.

This includes normal nonisolated toric germs of arbitrary dimension and monomial-weight obstacles over imperfect residue fields. For example k[[s\textasciicircum{}2,st,t\textasciicircum{}2,z]] has a nonisolated singular line in dimension3. The nonsimplicial rank3 saturated cone generated by (1,0,0),(1,1,0),(1,0,1),(1,1,1) gives k[[a,b,c,d]]/(ad-bc); adding formal monomial variables gives nonisolated examples. The theorem does NOT prove CE for arbitrary obstacles that distinguish valuations with the same monomial values, or for arbitrary excellent germs. Its smooth specialization uses the same G331 cone; in the published smooth affine closed/algebraically closed/characteristic-zero range it is the restriction of the BFJ envelope, because both are greatest minorants of that identical class. This does not extend BFJ's published hypotheses or identify literal analytic/CLD radial extensions.

\section{n6. New normal nonisolated obstruction to a universal primary correction}

Use the explicit BIG convention in n3 and the toric setup of n5 only at its stated scope. The calculation below proves its all-map test-ideal formula independently; no toric test-ideal formula or finite-map operator is imported. Let k be perfect of odd characteristic p, and
\[
R=k[[U,V,W,z]]/(UW-V^2)=k[[s^2,st,t^2,z]],
\quad B=k[[s,t,z]],\quad P=(U,V,W).
\]
R is an excellent normal three-dimensional domain, and its singular locus is the formal line P. This follows from the saturated monoid or the hypersurface and its codimension-two Jacobian locus. Write monomials as chi\textasciicircum{}m=s\textasciicircum{}a t\textasciicircum{}b z\textasciicircum{}c, with m in M=\{(a,b,c) in Z\textasciicircum{}3:a+b even\}, all coordinates nonnegative. For N>=1 set A\_N=(U,W\textasciicircum{}N,z\textasciicircum{}N), a genuine primary ideal, and
\[
w_N(a,b,c)=a/2+b/(2N)+c/N,\qquad
H_{N,t}=\langle\chi^m:w_N(m+(1,1,1))>t\rangle.
\]
We claim tau\_R(A\_N\textasciicircum{}t)=H\_(N,t) for every real t>=0, using stability exponents ceil(t(q-1)).

First every R Cartier map extends to a B Cartier map. The fraction field extension L/K is separable quadratic; purely inseparable root extension gives L tensor\_K K\textasciicircum{}(1/q)=L\textasciicircum{}(1/q). Hence an R-linear phi extends uniquely to an L-linear map on L\textasciicircum{}(1/q). Outside (s,t) the finite cover is etale: where s is invertible, B is given by S\textasciicircum{}2=U with derivative2S a unit, and similarly for t. Frobenius root base change on this chart is explicit, since s\textasciicircum{}(1/q)=s (U\textasciicircum{}(1/q))\textasciicircum{}(-(q-1)/2), with t=V/s; the t-chart is analogous. Thus the extended map carries the root module into B at every height-one localization. Since B\textasciicircum{}(1/q) is finite free and B is normal, the intersection-of-height-one-localizations criterion makes all its coefficients integral globally. The extension is an actual B-linear map B\textasciicircum{}(1/q)->B. Codimension-two etaleness and normality, not a general trace theorem, justify this step.

In the regular ring B, the root monomials with residues0,...,q-1 in each coordinate form a free basis. For any monomial chi\textasciicircum{}h in a source and any output monomial chi\textasciicircum{}n of any B Cartier map, these basis expansions give
\[
q n_i+(q-1)\ge h_i\quad(i=1,2,3).
\]
The map coefficients are power series with nonnegative exponents. Thus cancellation can only remove possible output monomials. If chi\textasciicircum{}h is in A\_N\textasciicircum{}r H\_(N,t), r=ceil(t(q-1)), then w\_N(h)+w\_N(1,1,1)>r+t. The displayed coordinate bound gives
\[
q w_N(n+(1,1,1))\ge w_N(h)+w_N(1,1,1)>r+t\ge qt.
\]
H\_(N,t) is therefore stable under every extended B map and hence EVERY R map. Monomial ideals are adically closed, so this calculation handles formal series as well as polynomial monomials. It is nonzero, indeed contains sufficiently high primary powers.

To prove minimality, let K be any generically nonzero stable ideal. Invert c=UW. The ring becomes regular and A\_N becomes unit. Finite Hom localization and the primitive-vector Frobenius argument of n3 give K\_c=R\_c. Hence d=(UW)\textasciicircum{}L belongs to K for some integer L. For a target m=(a,b,c\_0) satisfying w\_N(m+1)>t, choose q=p\textasciicircum{}e large and r=ceil(t(q-1)). The three capacities
\[
\left\lfloor\frac{q(a+1)-2L-1}{2}\right\rfloor,
\quad\left\lfloor\frac{q(b+1)-2L-1}{2N}\right\rfloor,
\quad\left\lfloor\frac{q(c_0+1)-1}{N}\right\rfloor
\]
are nonnegative and their sum exceeds r for all sufficiently large e: dividing by q gives w\_N(m+1)>t. Choose i,j,h within these capacities with i+j+h=r. The monomial d U\textasciicircum{}i W\textasciicircum{}(Nj) z\textasciicircum{}(Nh) lies in A\_N\textasciicircum{}r K; its exponent A has A\_i<q(m\_i+1). Put alpha=m-A/q, so alpha\_i>-1 and alpha in (1/q)M.

Define the R-linear map pi\_alpha on root monomials chi\textasciicircum{}u by pi\_alpha(chi\textasciicircum{}u)=chi\textasciicircum{}(u+alpha) if u+alpha belongs to M, and0 otherwise. Whenever the lattice condition holds, its coordinates are integers strictly greater than-1, hence nonnegative. It therefore maps into R, not merely its fraction field. Translation by an ordinary monoid exponent preserves the selection condition and proves R-linearity. Its residue-class selection and rescaling make it adically continuous; it extends to completed series. Applied to the chosen source root it returns chi\textasciicircum{}m. Stability implies chi\textasciicircum{}m belongs to K. This works for each target and every fixed L, with arbitrarily large Frobenius exponents. \title{A geometric valuative psh cone on excellent local germs\\
Actual Cartier positivity, uniform comparison, and full conductor descent}
\author{Fresh local reconstruction of ORIGINAL P12.2}

\maketitle
\begin{abstract}
On the intrinsic centred semivaluation boundary of an excellent local germ,
we define a geometric core by actual negative effective real Cartier divisors
on actual primary blowups, with nonnegative degrees on all contracted integral
curves. We prove its continuous uniform closure and actual decreasing completion
equal the corresponding ideal classes. A fixed primary correction to finite
global sections, corrected Keeler generation on the full closed fibre, and
explicit real ample perturbation prove the comparison without a normality,
smoothness or characteristic restriction. We reconstruct full finite-injection
and normalization/conductor descent, including mixed-zero and bottom patterns,
and recover the full smooth BFJ class on all semivaluations at its exact published
hypotheses. A nonisolated cusp separates the entire finite-real raw cone from its
completion. This is an unverified complete-solution candidate for P12.2;
independent whole-original review remains required.
\end{abstract}
