P12.3 (T4): An independently geometric singular envelope theory
Construct obstacle envelopes for the independently geometric singular psh cone, establish
their positivity and the appropriate regularity, and compare them with the complete ideal-
psh envelope already known on reduced-curve links.

ENTIRE ORIGINAL FAMILY DOSSIER

Active items: P12.2, P12.3, P12.4, P12.5, P12.6. Status: Open in the residual scope.

P12.3 (T4): An independently geometric singular envelope theory
Construct obstacle envelopes for the independently geometric singular psh cone, establish
their positivity and the appropriate regularity, and compare them with the complete ideal-
psh envelope already known on reduced-curve links.

P12.4 (T5): Model-independent bounded singular-local products
Construct bounded mixed Monge–Ampère products on singular and nonnormal normalized

continuity. The existing compact boundary construction alone supplies no such product.

P12.5 (T5): Finite energy on singular local boundaries
Construct an energy functional, ﬁnite-energy class, and its Monge–Ampère calculus for excel-
lent singular and nonnormal germs. Specify reference data, changes of primary gauge, and
the relation between bounded approximation and ﬁnite-energy limits.

P12.6 (T4): Geometric ﬁnite-map functoriality and conductor descent
Establish compatibility of independently geometric singular psh cones, envelopes and Monge–
Ampère products with ﬁnite maps, normalization and conductor descent. Finite restric-
tion, ideal-cone extrema, normal-domain norm traces, ﬁnite-ﬂat determinant traces and their
tower/gauge rules are known. They do not identify the geometric operators; an unrestricted
continuous degree trace is obstructed.

6.2   What constitutes a solution
The requested geometric cone, envelopes, bounded products, ﬁnite energy and map compat-
ibility are separate targets. Prove their smooth-germ specialization, primary-gauge changes
and normalization/conductor rules. Do not identify an ideal-generated order completion with
a geometric pluripotential theory without an additional comparison theorem.

6.3   Full statement and detailed state of the art
Finite-map progress is now available in Book Section 70.2: continuous positive trace over
normal targets without ﬂatness, ﬁber extrema for arbitrary ﬁnite maps onto their exact im-
ages, and the exact conductor criterion for continuous descent. The ideal-generated cones
are explicit; their identiﬁcation with a geometric singular psh class and compatibility with
envelopes and Monge–Ampère products are not claimed. This settles the valuative transfer
layer of P12.6 and narrows its remaining geometric target.

Problem 6.1. Extend the normalized local theory of Book Chapter 70 from smooth complex
germs to excellent singular and nonnormal germs. On the normalized boundary of Book
Section 70.1.1, construct, when possible, psh functions, envelopes, bounded products, ﬁnite
energy, and ﬁnite-map functoriality.
    The normalizing-boundary part is resolved in arbitrary dimension. Book Theorem 70.1.2
gives the intrinsic centered ray space and its nonempty compact sections for all m-primary
ideals, with exact change (Book 70.7a). Book Theorem 70.1.3 presents each section as a
quotient of the separated normalization branches. Fibers are singletons where the conductor
has ﬁnite value; on its inﬁnite-value stratum, equality of restrictions to the conductor quo-
tient is the precise identiﬁcation rule. Nonprimary ideals deﬁne the partial sections (Book
70.7e), which can be noncompact. Nilpotents are invisible to these semivaluations, and a zero-
dimensional local reduction has empty centered cone. This settles P12.1, while P12.2–P12.6
retain their separate psh, envelope, product, energy and ﬁnite-map targets. It does not assert
an intersection theory or resolution in positive characteristic.
    In dimension one, this construction reduces to a ﬁnite branch set. By Book Theorem 70.1.4,
the link normalized by an m-primary ideal a is the ﬁnite discrete set of normalization branches
q above the closed point, with point

                                         ordq / ordq (a).

Changing the primary ideal rescales this same branch set by the exact cocycle (Book Chap-
ter 70, †). In particular, branches cannot be indexed only by irreducible components: the irre-
ducible node in Book Example 70.1.4 has one minimal prime and two normalization branches.
    There is also an exact link-level ﬁnite-map formula. Book Proposition 70.1.2 applies to
an arbitrary ﬁnite local homomorphism of reduced Nagata curve germs, without injectivity.
When a source branch has ramiﬁcation index e over a target branch, both its order and the
order of the extended ideal aS acquire the factor e, so normalization cancels it. The resulting
restriction maps are compatible with composition and change of primary ideal. They need
not be surjective; this remains a link-level result.
    There is now also an exact conductor-controlled ideal-level range. Book Proposition 70.1.3
shows that every suﬃciently deep integral vector of branch orders is realized by one downstairs
nonzerodivisor generating an m-primary ideal. Consequently Book Theorem 70.1.5 identiﬁes
the principal-ideal proﬁles with the strictly negative rational orthant, their uniform closure
with all nonpositive functions on the ﬁnite link, and their raw obstacle envelope with min{φ, 0}.
The monotone boundary is sharp: all nonpositive proﬁles admit increasing approximation
from below, whereas a proﬁle with a zero branch coordinate cannot be a decreasing limit of
primary-ideal proﬁles. These conclusions concern only the explicitly deﬁned ideal-function
family.
    There is now also a complete order-theoretic calculus for the book-local ideal-closure can-
didate. By Book Theorem 70.1.6, its continuous ideal-psh class is every ﬁnite nonpositive
function on the branch link, and its decreasing completion is every extended nonpositive func-
tion. Equivalently, it is the intrinsic cone of nonpositive degree-one homogeneous functions
on the unnormalized branch-valuation rays. Changing the primary ideal merely changes the
cross-section and obeys an exact cocycle; ﬁnite local maps pull the class back, preserve prin-
cipal models, and commute with the envelope min{φ, 0}. Their pullback image is exactly the
ﬁber-constant subclass; pullback is injective precisely for a surjective branch map and sur-
jective precisely for an injective branch map, while surjective branch maps act isometrically
on the continuous class. On the completed lattices, ﬁberwise supremum and inﬁmum give
explicit left and right adjoints to pullback, with −∞ and zero as the two empty-ﬁber conven-
tions; the resulting source-side composites are the least ﬁber-constant majorant and greatest
ﬁber-constant minorant, so their ﬁxed points are exactly the functions descending through

    There is a genuine, but diﬀerent, global boundary case. Over an algebraically closed
ﬁeld of characteristic zero, the global trivially-valued framework used in [BJ23, §2] treats an

    The remaining programme tests higher-dimensional normal crossings, quotient singulari-

or intersection constructions from boundary choices must respect the established radial com-

and intersection-theoretic package is presently open.

# n1. Finite contact certificates on every excellent germ

Support: G331, with its entire source, annotation, ledger and scope unchanged. No result of current401, B341 or E350 is a premise. We prove 
a general excellent-germ theorem, followed by an explicit monomial certificate. No general CE is assumed.

Let R be an excellent local ring whose reduction has positive dimension, a a proper primary gauge, and X=V_a(R). All ideals and 
semivaluations below are interpreted on the reduction, as required by G331. Let J be ANY proper primary ideal and q a positive integer. 
There is a FINITE nonempty set E_J of centred semivaluations on X such that the independently geometric classes of G331 satisfy
\[
 u\in D,\quad u(x)\le -v_x(J)/q\ (x\in E_J)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad u(v)\le-v(J)/q\ (v\in X).       \tag{G1}
\]
Thus for ANY continuous obstacle f, however nonmonomial, the conditions
\[
 f\ge H=-v(J)/q\text{ everywhere},\qquad f|_{E_J}=H|_{E_J} \tag{G2}
\]
give its greatest geometric D envelope P(f)=H in the actual geometric core. The same holds for any bounded-above upper semicontinuous f 
satisfying (G2). If f>=H-epsilon and f(x)<=H(x)+delta at all contacts, epsilon,delta>=0, then H-epsilon<=p(f)<=H+delta, without assuming 
positivity of p(f). These are sufficient conditions, not a density or necessity theorem for arbitrary obstacles.

We construct and prove the certificate first when R is an excellent NORMAL local domain. Normalize the actual primary blowup Bl_J(R). 
Excellence makes normalization finite, so Y is projective, normal and Noetherian. The pulled-back ideal J O_Y=O_Y(-E) is invertible and E is

its actual nef primary-blowup presentation on Bl_J(R). No cofinality among arbitrary models, new cone definition, or positivity on a merely 
numerical Weil list is invoked.

The effective divisor E has finitely many prime components E_1,...,E_s, all of height one and all lying over the closed point. The DVR 
orders nu_i=ord_{E_i} restrict to valuations of Frac(R) centred at m. They have 0<nu_i(a)<infinity and nu_i(J)>0: every element of m is in 
the height-one maximal ideal at that centre, and a,J contain primary powers. Normalize nu_i by nu_i(a) to define E_J. There is at least one 
component: J O_Y is nonunit at any point of the nonempty closed fibre, and a nonunit regular local Cartier equation has a height-one prime. 
Proper birationality gives the nonempty fibre over the positive-dimensional domain.

Let u=-v(I)/r be any rational unit-or-primary profile and assume its contact inequalities. After clearing q and r they say
\[
 \nu_i(I^q)\ge r\nu_i(J)\quad (1\le i\le s).              \tag{G3}
\]
For each generator t of I^q, (G3) gives the height-one section condition t in O_Y(-rE) at every E_i. At all other height-one points E has 
coefficient zero and t, being in R, is regular. The normal codimension-one section criterion on every affine open therefore proves
\[
 I^q O_Y\subset J^r O_Y.                                  \tag{G4}
\]
This is a direct proof of the needed finite Rees-valuation implication. No toric or test-ideal theorem, or Rees integral-closure criterion, 
is imported as an additional premise.

To evaluate (G4) at ANY v in X, including nonzero prime support p, pass first to its valued quotient field Frac(R/p). The generic point p 
differs from m, so Y is isomorphic there. Properness and the valuative criterion lift the map of its valuation ring to Y. The local

argument below reconstructs the required monomial facts and proves the new envelope theorem directly.

Let M be a rank-d lattice, T a pointed full-dimensional rational polyhedral cone, S=T intersect M, and R the completion of k[S] at its 
monomial maximal ideal, over any field k. Let a be any monomial primary gauge, X=V_a(R), and C,D the independently geometric classes of 
qualified G331. In particular, C is the uniform closure of negative finite real primary profiles, rational profiles are uniformly dense, and
 D is made of actual decreasing C-nets. These are consequences of the granted geometric comparison, not new definitions of positivity. Every
 semivaluation support is included.

The monoid is finitely generated by the rational-cone lattice-point theorem. The affine ring is normal: in its fraction field it is the 
intersection of the normal Laurent polynomial ring k[M] and the valuation rings of the primitive facet weights. For a Laurent polynomial 
each facet minimum is the minimum of its term weights; nonnegativity of all these minima says exactly that every exponent belongs to T. The 
finite-type ring is excellent, and its normal local ring has normal excellent completion. Thus the stipulated R is an excellent normal local
 domain over arbitrary k. These exact conventional algebraic facts require neither perfection nor a finite extension of a regular local 
ring. Its elements have unique formal monomial expansions in the maximal-adic topology.

Fix a nonunit monomial primary ideal J and a positive integer q. Put H(v)=-v(J)/q. This is an actual geometric core function: on Bl_J(R) its
 negative effective Cartier exceptional divisor has an ample negative bundle and nonnegative degree on every contracted proper integral 
curve, as granted and proved in G331. H is finite continuous on all X. Write
\[
 P_J=\operatorname{conv}\{u_1,\ldots,u_h\}+T
\]
for its Newton polyhedron, using a finite monomial generating set. A finite rational half-space presentation consists of the cone 
inequalities together with finitely many inequalities
\[
 \langle x,w_j\rangle\ge b_j,\qquad b_j>0.                 \tag{1}
\]
Every w_j in (1) is in the interior of the dual cone. Indeed, a supporting normal is nonnegative on the recession cone T. If it has zero 
value on a nonzero monoid generator g, primaryness puts some Ng in P_J, so its supporting intercept is zero. Such zero-intercept 
inequalities are already consequences of x in T. Consequently all positive-intercept facet normals are strictly positive on all monoid 
generators. The elementary finite rational polyhedral half-space/vertex theorem applies here; no toric test-ideal theorem is used.

For an interior dual weight w, the minimum weight of terms defines a centred monomial valuation of the completed ring. Positivity on the 
finitely many generators bounds the number of monomials of bounded weight and proves the minimum exists. The associated graded monomials 
cannot cancel, so multiplication and the ultrametric inequality hold. Normalize by w(a). Denote the resulting point associated to w_j by 
x_j. Then
\[
 v_{x_j}(J)=b_j/w_j(a).
\]
The finite set E_J={x_j} is a contact certificate for H in the following strong sense:
\[
 u\in D,\quad u(x_j)\le H(x_j)\ (\text{every }j)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad u(v)\le H(v)\ (\text{every }v\in X).       \tag{2}
\]

Here is a proof on every support that avoids approximating an infinite monomial weight. First let u=-v(I)/r be a rational primary or unit 
profile. Let M(I) be the monomial ideal generated by all terms in a finite collection of formal generators of I. Noetherianity makes it 
generated by finitely many of those terms. Moreover I is contained in M(I): each finite truncation of a generator belongs to this monomial 
ideal, and the ideal is adically closed by separation of its finite quotient. At every interior monomial valuation v_w(I)=v_w(M(I)), because
 a least term in a generator cannot cancel against distinct monomials.

The contact inequalities imply, for every occurring exponent u_0,
\[
 q\langle u_0,w_j\rangle\ge r b_j,
 \qquad q u_0\in rP_J.                                    \tag{3}
\]
The second statement follows from the complete half-space presentation and u_0 in S. Write q u_0 as a rational convex combination of the r 
u_i plus a rational vector in T. Such a rational decomposition exists: it solves a finite rational linear system with nonnegative unknowns, 
and row reduction on the minimal face of a real solution gives rational feasible points. Clear its denominators by a positive integer D_0. 
The recession remainder then lies in S, by saturation, and
\[
 \chi^{D_0 q u_0}\in J^{rD_0}.
\]
Thus chi^{q u_0} is integral over J^r, using the equation Z^{D_0}-chi^{D_0 q u_0}=0. For any semivaluation v in X, J has finite value 
because it is primary. Integral dependence implies
\[
 qv(\chi^{u_0})\ge r v(J).                                 \tag{4}
\]
If the left side is infinite this is automatic. Otherwise a hypothetical strict inequality makes the leading monic term in the integral 
equation have uniquely smallest finite value, contradicting the ultrametric inequality. Taking the minimum over the finite monomial 
generators of M(I), then using I subset M(I), proves v(I)/r>=v(J)/q on EVERY support. This proves (2) for rational profiles without assuming
 that monomialization preserves an arbitrary obstacle.

For g in C satisfying the contact inequalities, approximate g uniformly by a rational primary profile within epsilon. Subtract a rational 
primary-gauge constant between epsilon and 2epsilon. This subtraction is again a single rational profile after clearing denominators and 
taking an ideal product. It satisfies the exact contact inequalities, hence is at most H everywhere by the preceding proof. Let epsilon tend
 to zero to obtain g<=H. For u=inf_i g_i in D, the finite contact set and directedness select one term with g_i(x_j)<H(x_j)+epsilon for 
every j, even if u has poles at some contacts. Then g_i-epsilon is in C and satisfies the contact inequalities. Hence u<=H+epsilon, and 
epsilon tends to zero. This proves (2) for the ACTUAL decreasing completion, including bottom and partial poles; no flattening or increasing
 closure is used.

Now let f be ANY finite continuous obstacle on X, with no weight-dependence assumption, such that
\[
 f\ge H\text{ on }X,\qquad f(x_j)=H(x_j)\text{ for every }j.             \tag{5}
\]
H is a geometric competitor. Every geometric D competitor below f satisfies (2), so is below H. Consequently
\[
 \sup\{u\in D:u\le f\}=H\in C.
\]
This is an actually positive continuous greatest geometric envelope among ALL competitors. The same proof works for ANY bounded-above 
extended upper semicontinuous f satisfying (5); its envelope is still the continuous function H. Here (5) forces f to be finite below, 
although its upper size may vary. The unit case J=R has H=0 and no contacts; every obstacle f>=0 has envelope zero by nonpositivity.

There is a quantitative version with no presumed continuity of the raw envelope. If f>=H-epsilon everywhere and f(x_j)<=H(x_j)+delta at the 
finite contacts, for epsilon,delta>=0, then
\[
 H-\epsilon\le p(f)\le H+\delta.                           \tag{6}
\]
The lower inequality uses the actual C competitor H-epsilon. The upper inequality applies (2) to each competitor shifted by -delta. Thus 
increasingly accurate lower barriers and contact bounds give uniform approximation of raw envelopes to H, even when CE is not established 
for each perturbed obstacle. Conditions (5) are sufficient; no necessity or density among all obstacles is claimed.

This advances beyond weight-dependent obstacles: arbitrary cancellation-sensitive functions satisfying the finite contacts are allowed. The 
general theorem above removes the toric hypothesis for the finite-contact obstacle sector. Neither theorem supplies arbitrary-obstacle CE or
 an envelope counterexample. Finite geometry controls the competitors; the obstacle is never averaged or monomialized. G331 remains the sole
 correctness grant. The proof's conventional backgrounds are finite rational polyhedral geometry, Gordan's finite-generation lemma, normal 
excellent completion, and finite-module adic separation, at exactly the stated hypotheses.

Artifacts: n1.md, proof-companion.md and P12.3-contact-envelopes.tex. The explicit finite certificate used in n2 is implemented by the 
independently written contact_certificate.py, with contact-input.json and contact-output.json. Rerun: python contact_certificate.py. Program
 success is only finite arithmetic evidence, not a proof of (2) or of general CE.


# n2. Explicit nonmonomial primary obstacles on normal nonisolated fourfolds, including mixed characteristic

Support: G331 and earlier own n1. We use n1's finite-contact theorem, not the current401 toric-envelope theorem or a finite-cover theorem.

For ANY field k let
\[
 R=k[[a,b,c,d,z]]/(ad-bc),\quad \mathfrak m=(a,b,c,d,z),\quad
 J=(a^2,b^3,c^3,d^2,z^4),\quad
 K=(a+b,c+d,z)+\mathfrak m^2.                               \tag{7}
\]
Both J and K are genuine primary ideals. J contains powers of every maximal generator, and K contains m^2. Write the saturated monoid cone 
in Z^4 with generators
\[
 g_a=(1,0,0,0),\ g_b=(1,1,0,0),\ g_c=(1,0,1,0),\
 g_d=(1,1,1,0),\ g_z=(0,0,0,1).
\]
The cone consists of x_2,x_3,x_4>=0, x_1>=x_2,x_3. Every integer point is generated by these vectors: choose the coefficient of g_d between 
max(0,x_2+x_3-x_1) and min(x_2,x_3), then use g_b,g_c,g_a for the remainder and g_z for x_4. The only lattice relation among the first four 
generators is g_a+g_d=g_b+g_c. Reducing monomials by ad=bc gives the monoid algebra presentation. Thus (7) is the normal excellent complete 
germ of n1. Its dimension is four. It is regular where any of a,b,c,d is invertible, by solving its equation for the opposite variable. At 
P=(a,b,c,d), the equation has no linear term in the four normal variables, so that localization has embedding dimension four and dimension 
three. Its singular locus is exactly the positive-dimensional line P, over every k, including characteristic two. This is a normal 
nonisolated germ.

The Newton polyhedron of J has the following COMPLETE presentation: the cone inequalities and
\[
 \langle x,w_+\rangle\ge1,\quad \langle x,w_-\rangle\ge1,\qquad
 w_\pm=(1/2,\ \pm1/6,\ \mp1/6,\ 1/4).                  \tag{8}
\]
Both normals are interior to the dual cone: their values on the five generators are respectively (1/2,2/3,1/3,1/2,1/4) and 
(1/2,1/3,2/3,1/2,1/4). To check completeness without assuming a program's answer, the section at x_4=0 is the cone over the unit square 
x_1=1, cut by (3x_1+x_2-x_3)/6>=1 and (3x_1-x_2+x_3)/6>=1. Its four vertices are (2,0,0),(3,3,0),(3,0,3),(2,2,2). This follows by 
considering the four square-edge equalities x_2=0, x_3=0, x_1=x_2, x_1=x_3; intersections of both cutting planes force x_2=x_3 and x_1=2, 
whose endpoints are (2,0,0) and (2,2,2). Each individual cutting plane's remaining endpoint is the corresponding opposite square corner at 
x_1=3. There are no other vertex intersections. For 0<=x_4<=4, the right sides for this three-dimensional section are 1-x_4/4. For x_4>4 the
 section is the whole recession cone. Consequently the full polyhedron has precisely those four vertices with fourth coordinate zero and 
(0,0,0,4), and recession cone T. These are exactly the five generating exponents in (7), proving (8).

Normalize by the monomial primary gauge m. The two contacts v_+,v_- in n1 have generator values
\[
 (a,b,c,d,z)=(2,8/3,4/3,2,1),\quad (2,4/3,8/3,2,1),
\]
respectively. Both have v(m)=1 and v(J)=4. At EVERY interior monomial valuation, a+b and c+d have their least term values without 
cancellation, so v(K)=v(m). This also follows at the two contacts directly from the displayed numbers. For an arbitrary semivaluation in 
V_m, containment m^2 subset K subset m gives 1<=v(K)<=2. Define for any real delta>=0
\[
 f_\delta=-v(J)+\delta\big(v(K)-v(\mathfrak m)\big).
                                                                    \tag{9}
\]
This is a finite continuous obstacle on the entire compact boundary. It is at least H=-v(J), and agrees with H at both contacts. By n1 its 
greatest geometric D envelope is exactly
\[
 P(f_\delta)=-v(J).
                                                                    \tag{10}
\]
For delta=1/2 this is a rational signed PRIMARY model obstacle:
\[
 f_{1/2}=\big(v(K)-v(J^2\mathfrak m)\big)/2.
\]
The primary product blowup principalizes J,K,m, so it is the evaluation of an actual signed exceptional rational Cartier divisor there. Its 
obstacle need not be nef. Its envelope is the actual negative effective nef Cartier profile on Bl_J(R), not positivity conferred by upper 
regularization. Since J subset m^2, f_{1/2}<=-3/2 throughout V_m; it is a genuinely negative example.

To prove the obstacle is genuinely nonmonomial, consider the quotient map to k[[r,h,z]] given by
\[
 a=c=r,\qquad b=d=r(h-1),\qquad z=z,
\]
followed by the monomial valuation with r,h,z weights 1,1,3. The relation ad=bc is identically satisfied. The kernel on R is (c-a,d-b): the 
quotient is k[[a,b,z]], and substitution a=r,b=r(h-1) is injective because replacing b by a+b sends its two coordinates to r,rh, whose 
distinct monomials r^{i+j}h^j have distinct exponent pairs. This is a prime support strictly below m. It is an allowed centred 
semivaluation, normalized already by v(m)=1, and
\[
 v(a,b,c,d,z)=(1,1,1,1,3),\quad v(K)=2,\quad v(J)=2.
\]
The equalities a+b=c+d=rh hold over every field, including characteristic two. At the monomial valuation w_0=(1,0,0,3) on R, the monomial 
weights of all five generators are identical, but w_0(K)=1 and w_0(J)=2. Therefore
\[
 f_{1/2}(v)=-3/2,\qquad f_{1/2}(w_0)=-2.
\]
They have the same values on EVERY monomial by additivity. Hence (9) cannot be a function only of monomial weights. This is an actual 
nonmonomial continuous signed primary/model obstacle, not a coordinate re-description of a weight-only obstacle.

The retained singular-supported valuation killing P and giving z value one has v(m)=v(K)=1, v(J)=4, and f_delta=-4. Its Jacobian value 
v((a,b,c,d)) is infinite. Formula (10) includes this point and all other supports. No nonprimary correction is divided by an index, and no 
support is discarded. The proof uses finite contact inequalities and genuine primary profiles. It is independent of the Frobenius/test-ideal
 route and works over imperfect fields and all characteristics. It proves an obstacle sector, not CE for arbitrary obstacles on this ring. 
It does not prove that this ring lacks a finite regular cover, and no such premise is needed.

Evidence: the own program contact_certificate.py enumerates the five choose four candidate positive facets and the seven choose four 
candidate vertices by exact rational row reduction. Its observed output is two positive facet normals, five vertices, and PASS on 23 
explicitly enumerated positive rational monomial-weight cases. It records the normalized contacts and the exact cancellation and 
singular-support values above in contact-output.json. The polyhedral and semivaluation arguments above are mathematical proofs; the program 
checks only this finite certificate. Rerun: python contact_certificate.py. Inputs, source and full output are in contact-input.json, 
contact_certificate.py and contact-output.json; no supplied program is executed or imported.

## A mixed-characteristic normal nonisolated example

The general theorem in n1 also yields an explicit sector outside equicharacteristic field germs. Fix any prime p, take V=Z_p with 
uniformizer pi=p, and put
\[
 R_V=V[[a,b,c,d]]/(ad-bc),\quad \mathfrak n=(\pi,a,b,c,d),\quad
 K_V=(a+b,c+d,\pi)+\mathfrak n^2.                         \tag{11}
\]
This is a complete excellent normal domain of dimension four with a singular line (a,b,c,d). Here are explicit checks, so no general 
mixed-characteristic positivity theorem is assumed. The standard monomials after replacing ad by bc form a V-basis, also after completion 
degree by degree. The parametrization a=xy,b=xw,c=ty,d=tw in V[[x,y,t,w]] identifies distinct standard monomials with distinct exponent 
vectors. Thus the quotient is a domain. It is a hypersurface in a regular local ring, so is S2. At a prime not containing all four a,b,c,d, 
a partial derivative d,-c,-b or a is a unit. In the regular ambient localization the defining equation is outside the square of the maximal 
ideal (apply that derivation), so the quotient localization is regular. The ideal (a,b,c,d) has height three, by the catenary hypersurface 
dimension formula and quotient V. Every height-one localization is regular, and Serre's R1+S2 criterion proves normality. At the generic 
point of that line the quadric has embedding dimension four and dimension three, hence is singular. These CM/S2 facts check this SPECIFIC 
hypersurface; they are not imposed on the general theorem or formal audit.

The n-adic graded ring is exactly
\[
 \operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak n}(R_V)
   =\mathbf F_p[\Pi,A,B,C,D]/(AD-BC),                       \tag{12}
\]
a domain. The regular ambient ring has polynomial associated graded ring. For any h there, ord(h(ad-bc))=ord(h)+2, because its associated 
graded ring is a domain. Its initial form is in(h)(AD-BC). Thus the initial ideal of the principal relation is precisely (AD-BC), with no 
extra initial relation. The quotient polynomial ring is a domain by the same monomial parametrization. Consequently nu=ord_n is a valuation,
 not merely a subadditive order, and nu(n)=1.

For EVERY centred semivaluation v with v(n)=1, membership f in n^r gives v(f)>=r, so v(f)>=nu(f). Selecting an element of least finite 
v-value in a primary ideal I gives v(I)>=nu(I). Every negative rational or real primary profile g therefore satisfies g(v)<=g(nu). Uniform 
limits and the ACTUAL infima defining D preserve this inequality. This is a one-point contact certificate at nu, proved directly; no count 
of normalized-blowup components is needed.

K_V is proper primary and n^2 subset K_V subset n. Since a+b has order one, nu(K_V)=1. For any delta>=0 the finite continuous obstacle
\[
 F_\delta=-v(\mathfrak n)+\delta\big(v(K_V)-v(\mathfrak n)\big)           \tag{13}
\]
is at least -1 and equals -1 at nu. Every D competitor below it is at most -1 at nu, hence everywhere. The primary profile -v(n) is itself a
 geometric competitor, proving
\[
 P(F_\delta)=-v(\mathfrak n)=-1
\]
on the entire normalized boundary. For delta=1/2, (13) is (v(K_V)-v(n^3))/2, an actual rational signed primary/model obstacle on the product
 primary blowup. Its greatest geometric envelope is actual nef Cartier. Since v(K_V)<=2, this obstacle lies in [-1,-1/2].

It is cancellation-sensitive even with the uniformizer weight retained. Map a=c=r,b=d=r(h-1) into V[[r,h]] and use the weighted valuation 
with pi,r,h weights 3,1,1. For a formal series sum c_ij r^i h^j its value is min(3 ord_pi(c_ij)+i+j); its associated graded 
coefficient/monomial ring over F_p is a domain, proving multiplicativity. Pullback is centred, with prime support (c-a,d-b) strictly below 
n, and
\[
 v(\pi,a,b,c,d)=(3,1,1,1,1),\qquad v(K_V)=2.
\]
The matching monomial valuation on R_V has the same generator and uniformizer weights but K_V value one. It exists by the standard monomial 
expansion over V, with value 3 ord_pi(coefficient)+total monomial degree. Its associated graded ring is the domain monoid algebra over F_p 
with a uniformizer variable, so distinct monomials cannot cancel. Thus F_(1/2) has values -1/2 and -1 at these equal-weight semivaluations. 
The supported valuation killing (a,b,c,d) and giving pi value one has K_V value one and envelope -1, even though the ideal (a,b,c,d) has 
infinite value. Every support is retained.

This is an unconditional mixed-characteristic excellent normal nonisolated obstacle sector relative to G331. It is not arbitrary-obstacle 
mixed-characteristic CE. The proofs above establish its universal statements. The own finite program checks only the equicharacteristic 
Newton instance and is not a p-adic ring computation.


# n3. Exact gauges, compatible normalization contacts, and geometric curve clipping

Support: incoming qualified G331 and earlier own n1,n2. No B341/E350 product or energy result is used.

The contact theorem of n1 applies to every excellent germ and is homogeneous on rays. If b is another primary gauge, write d(v)=v(b) on V_a,
 T(v)=v/d(v), and transport obstacle, barrier and contacts by
\[
 f_b(Tv)=f_a(v)/d(v),\quad H_b(Tv)=H_a(v)/d(v),\quad x_{j,b}=T(x_{j,a}).
\]
The positive bounded continuous denominator preserves inequalities, contact equalities, uniform convergence and actual decreasing 
representations. G331 gives precisely this bijection of C,D competitors. Taking their suprema proves the exact envelope rule
\[
 P_b(f_b)(Tv)=P_a(f_a)(v)/d(v).
\]
Substitution supplies the exact three-primary-gauge cocycle. The contact normals remain centred under every primary section; the barrier 
remains -v(J)/q in the new section. Completion transport is the already granted all-support homeomorphism and exact primary contraction, not
 a new algebraization or equivalence of geometric model categories.

Here is a full-fibre normalization extension of the new contact sector, which does not assume general CE upstairs. Let R be any excellent 
reduced germ with finite normalization S, and suppose each positive-dimensional normal local centre S_i is of the saturated monoid type of 
n1. Take barriers H_i=-v(J_i)/q_i as in n1, or the zero barrier. Require their tuple H to be constant on EVERY restriction fibre of 
rho:X_S->X_R. Qualified G331 positively descends the continuous tuple to h in C_R. Let f be any finite continuous obstacle on X_R such that 
f>=h, and for every nonzero barrier's finite contact x_{ij} require
\[
 f(\rho(x_{ij}))=H_i(x_{ij}).
\]
For a D_R competitor u<=f, its pullback on each nonzero branch is at most H_i by n1. On a zero-barrier branch its nonpositivity gives the 
same inequality. Thus u<=h by surjectivity of rho, while h is itself a competitor. Its greatest D_R envelope is h. The same statement holds 
for a bounded-above extended upper semicontinuous obstacle satisfying these bounds and contacts. A contact condition at one source point 
never replaces the imposed FULL-fibre compatibility of H.

Specifically, if c is the conductor, G331 identifies a fibre as a singleton when v(c)<infinity. When v(c)=infinity, lifts kill c and 
equality of their restrictions through S/c -> R/c is exactly the identification rule. The finite-value locus is open, the infinite-value 
locus closed. Both are retained in the contact argument. No value v(c)/m is used as a uniform error. Compatibility includes all branches, 
nonminimal supports, mixed-zero and partial-bottom patterns. This theorem does not assert that an incompatible tuple of source envelopes 
descends positively or that an arbitrary fibre maximum is psh.

On EVERY excellent reduced curve, normalization has the finite collection of DVR local centres over the closed point, including multiple 
branches on one irreducible component. A regular conductor element has finite order on every branch, so normalized boundary fibres are 
singleton. On each DVR the marked point is an actual effective Cartier divisor and there are no contracted integral curves to test. All 
finite nonpositive coordinates are independently geometric there; G331's positive full-fibre continuous descent gives all finite nonpositive
 branch vectors downstairs. For an extended nonpositive vector u, max(u,-j) is an actual decreasing sequence of these C vectors with infimum
 u. Thus D is exactly every extended nonpositive branch vector. For any branch obstacle phi its greatest geometric D minorant is min(phi,0).
 This is the exact complete ideal-envelope comparison by G331's independently proved cone comparison. The branch coordinate for two primary 
gauges rescales by ord_i(a)/ord_i(b), with the exact cocycle above.

Nilpotents remain invisible and are removed by reduction; if the local reduction has dimension zero the centred boundary is empty and 
statements concern its unique empty function. Literal classical or CLD logarithmic radial extension classes are not changed: their stated 
multibranch mixed-zero obstruction remains. The boundary class may contain (-1,0) without such a literal radial extension. At a smooth 
affine CLOSED germ over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, G331 identifies this exact C,D class with the full published BFJ 
all-semivaluation class, with bottom adjoined. Wherever our contact theorem applies at that specialization, its greatest minorant is 
therefore the BFJ envelope in the SAME class. This does not extend BFJ's published hypotheses to arbitrary smooth excellent, imperfect or 
mixed-characteristic germs. Dimension-one and empty cases above are direct.

Artifacts: n3.md, proof-companion.md and P12.3-contact-envelopes.tex, retaining the full incoming G331 proof/annotation/ledger. Rerun 
delivery and data checks: python prepare_delivery.py. This scope leaves P12.4 products, P12.5 energy and P12.6 full operator theory 
separate.


# n4. Current401 audit, formal reconstruction boundary, and unchanged original residual

Support: G331 and earlier own n1,n2,n3 for the new contact theorem, geometric comparison, gauges and curves. Supplied current401, ROOT392, 
native verdicts, programs, ledgers and inherited B341/E350 are DATA, not grants. None is listed as support or used as an unproved 
mathematical premise of n1--n3.

The seven actual current401 FINAL objects were read in their entirety, all five fields. The separate expanded JSON agrees in every field 
except actual n2's two spacing-command backslashes around its d tensor1 arrow label; the displayed algebra is identical. Both complete 
objects and the full terminal framing remain separately retained. The proof companion is exactly the expanded text join. The current 
standalone is retained byte-for-byte, including its full qualified G331, B341 and E350 appendices and every annotation/ledger/qualification.
 Incoming G331's whole 93375-byte text occurs literally in that standalone. Neither an inherited B341/E350 acceptance label nor a native 
PASS is an additional incoming envelope premise. Data retention and duplicate identity confer no fresh proof/source reading credit.

The following is my independent reconstruction of the active formal chain and the limits of the present audit. It concerns complete normal 
characteristic-p rings with perfect coefficient/residue field, not arbitrary original germs.

Completed algebra: for a finite complete local k-module V, continuous duality gives V=(V^o)^*, with V^o the union of the duals of its 
finite-dimensional adic quotients. Artin--Rees identifies the topology of a finite submodule with its induced topology; linear functionals 
extend in a finite quotient. Thus continuous duality is exact. The identity V completed-tensor_k W=(V^o tensor_k W^o)^* proves exactness in 
both slots. Applying kernels of two finite presentation matrices then proves the FULL Hom factorization
\[
 \operatorname{Hom}_{R\widehat\otimes_k R}(M\widehat\otimes_k N,R\widehat\otimes_k R)
 =\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)\widehat\otimes_k\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,R).
\]
Paired generators generate every map; individual maps need not be decomposable. Perfect coefficients and exponent grouping identify the root
 of S=R completed-tensor_k R with R^(1/q) completed-tensor_k R^(1/q). Exactness applied twice to the root injections proves S reduced. A 
parameter ring k[[x_1,...,x_d]] makes R finite torsion-free; embedding it into a finite free module and applying completed exactness makes S
 finite torsion-free over k[[x,y]]. Its minimal primes contract to zero, so every minimal quotient has dimension 2d. Normality or 
Cohen--Macaulayness of S is not used.

Different/lift: for a fixed k-parameter normalization A, the adjugate of a square matrix of differences of the presentation equations 
annihilates all diagonal generators. Its product image is the relative Jacobian minor; hence the Kahler different is contained in the 
Noether different. If its generic extension is separable, a Noether-different element d is the product image of d times the separability 
idempotent. The identity
\[
 dw=\sum_i r_i\operatorname{Tr}(s_iw)
\]
base changes through the linearly disjoint purely inseparable K^(1/q)/K. For w in R^(1/q), trace coefficients are integral and lie in the 
fraction field of the normal regular A^(1/q); they therefore lie in A^(1/q). This proves d R^(1/q) subset P_q=A^(1/q)[R], and P_q is finite 
FREE over R because its generic multiplication is injective and A^(1/q) tensor_A R is an R-free torsion-free module. It does not make R free
 over A.

For T=R^(1/q), lift multiplication from the B-free module P_q completed-tensor T through B=R completed-tensor T -> T. Compose with ROOT 
multiplication d on the first T and 1 completed-tensor phi on the target. After multiplication into R its value is phi(dxy)=d phi(xy). This 
holds on all completed elements by finite-module continuity, factors through the SURJECTIVE root multiplication, and sends its ENTIRE kernel

# n3. BIG minima, late tails, and the actual completed diagonal

\]

 enters.

Localization of these ideals follows from finite Hom localization and shared nonzero seeds. Full-algebra completion is also exact for 
excellent F-finite normal local A: the m-adic and Frobenius filtrations are cofinal, so F_*A completes to F_*(A-hat), and finite Hom 
commutes with faithful flat completion. Extending tau_A is stable, giving tau_hat subset tau_A A-hat. Choose c in A with A_c regular and 
pair ideals unit. Regular formal fibres make A-hat_c regular; the same cleared splitting supplies a common c^L in tau_hat. Its contraction 
is nonzero and stable, giving the reverse inclusion. An arbitrary nonzero formal ideal is never assumed to have nonzero contraction. This 
proves the completion rule for full algebras only.

If J C_e subset D_e, the correct comparison is J tau_C subset tau_D. Choose a regular seed in both minima. The C late-tail formula expresses
 tau_C; multiplying each output by J turns the map into a D map, whose image of the common seed lies in tau_D. This proves the comparison 
without claiming J tau_C is itself D-stable.

Return to n2's S. It is reduced F-finite and equidimensional of dimension2d. Indeed a parameter ring A_0=k[[x_1,...,x_d]] makes R finite 
torsion-free. Clear denominators of a generic basis to embed R in a finite free A_0 module. Completed exactness embeds S in a free module 
over k[[x,y]]. Every minimal prime of this finite torsion-free algebra contracts to0, so all minimal quotients have dimension2d. A nonzero 
d-codimensional Jacobian minor j of R yields the block minor j(u)j(v) in Jac(S). At the diagonal prime I its image is j^2, nonzero in R. The
 exact reduced-equidimensional perfect-residue singular-locus criterion of n2 makes S_I regular. No S normality or product-domain assertion 
is needed.

Choose regular a_0 in a and b_0 in b and set c_S=j(u)j(v)(a_0 tensor b_0). Completed exactness makes multiplication by a_0 and b_0 injective
 in their slots, and similarly for j; thus c_S is regular. Its diagonal image j^2 a_0 b_0 is nonzero. On S_cS the ring is regular and both 
pair ideals A=aS, B=bS are units. For R's diagonal algebra D, n2 gives j C_e subset D_e, so localization at j is full and regular. Thus the 
BIG framework applies to all three actual algebras.

Let T_S=tau_S(A^t B^s). Its image mu(T_S) is D-stable: compatible lifts carry its coefficient-twisted roots into T_S, and passage to the 
quotient gives the required maps. Its image is nonzero because it contains mu(c_S^L). Minimality therefore gives tau_D(a^t b^s) subset 
mu(T_S).

The completed product of tau_R(a^t) and tau_R(b^s), extended into S, is stable for EVERY full S Cartier map by n2's full Hom factorization 
and stability in each factor. It contains a regular pure tensor, again by completed exactness, so T_S lies in this product ideal. 
Multiplication sends it to tau_R(a^t) tau_R(b^s). Combining the common-seed comparison with these two inclusions gives
\[
\operatorname{Jac}(R)\tau_R(a^t b^s)
\subset\tau_D(a^t b^s)
\subset\mu(T_S)
\subset\tau_R(a^t)\tau_R(b^s).
\]
Iteration yields Jac^(ell-1) tau(a^(ell t)) subset tau(a^t)^ell. This is the corrected direction. A primary multiplier is obtained only 
under isolatedness; no finite value of a nonprimary Jacobian on every support is inferred.

Verdict: the complete formal BIG/subadditivity gate is discharged for complete normal characteristic-p perfect-residue R, with no 
finite-type-over-field, CM, algebraizability, Q-Gorenstein or graded Cartier-finite-generation assumption. The verification uses the 
explicit nonzero diagonal seed, rather than a guessed image theorem. Local source and arithmetic checks are evidence, not a correctness 
grant.

# n4. Entire isolated formal envelope chain and scoped verdict

Use n1--n3 and the full qualified G331. Let R be complete normal local, characteristic p>0, perfect residue, isolated singularity, dimension
 d>=2. This note reconstructs the entire model/trace/primary approximation chain. In dimension1 R is a DVR; dimension0 has empty boundary. 
No algebraizability, CM, Q-Gorenstein or resolution is assumed.

First justify model transfer. Exponent grouping in R over R^p makes ordinary Omega_(R/k) finite: every element is a finite sum b_i^p u^i and
 every k-derivation kills the pth powers and the perfect field. This agrees with continuous formal differentials. A finite-type affine model
 algebra A is F-finite and has finite Omega_(A/k). Grouping over A^p and cofinal filtrations similarly gives Omega_(A/k) completed at a 
closed point equal to the formal differential module of its completion. Its closed residue field is a finite extension of perfect k, hence 
perfect. Hensel lifting of that finite separable extension gives a coefficient field compatible with k, and its differentials vanish. Closed
 points of a projective birational model over this local base lie above m and have local dimension d by catenarity and the residue/dimension
 formula. Normality, F-finiteness and excellence pass to their completions. Consequently the dth Fitting Jacobian and full BIG ideals 
commute with this completion. Apply n3 at every completed closed model point and descend by faithful flatness. A coherent failure elsewhere 
has closed support and a closed point, so the Jacobian subadditivity holds on the entire model.

CEMS1412.6453v4 Setting2.1 explicitly includes schemes essentially of finite type over an F-finite LOCAL base with dualizing complexes and 
the stated Frobenius-duality compatibility. The complete base R has a dualizing complex, and the projective models inherit one. The 
canonical sheaf used is the divisorial reflexive rank-one sheaf, not a locally free CM canonical module. Definition2.2 and Lemmas2.3--2.4 
with their entire immediate proofs give the BIG trace formula, localization, monotonicity and Cartier shift at precisely this setting. Those
 immediate units were read in full. Their finite-duality/divisor foundations are named ordinary published background; no anti-canonical 
finite generation or Lemma2.10 is used. The following globalization uses their arbitrary-late formula, with BIG existence, roundings and 
seeds already proved in n3.

Principalize any finite primary collection, including the gauge, on its product blowup and normalize. Its pulled-back exceptional F_0 is 
actual Cartier with full-fibre positive coefficients and relatively ample negative bundle. On this normal model omega has rank one. Blow up 
Fitt_1(omega). On an affine G/a blowup chart, discard a-power torsion in the pullback. The full Stacks15.27.3--4 proof makes its first 
Fitting ideal unit. Its zeroth Fitting ideal vanishes after inverting a and hence vanishes in the chart domain. The full15.8.8--9 criterion 
makes the strict transform a rank-one line bundle. Normalize and pull back that bundle. Choose the SAME rational section for its Cartier 
divisor L_0 and for K_Y; they agree on the puncture. Thus K_Y-L_0 is an exceptional Weil divisor. For sufficiently large r,
\[
\Delta=rF_0-(K_Y-L_0)\ge0,\qquad K_Y+\Delta=L_0+rF_0=:L
\]
is Cartier. This allows non-CM models throughout.

The negative Fitting blowup bundle times a sufficiently high pullback power of O(-F_0) is ample; finite normalization preserves it. A high 
power A=O(-F), H=-F, is very ample and generated with full-fibre support. Its global sections J belong to R by normal Hartogs, are finite by
 proper coherence, unit off m and proper because they vanish on the nonempty fibre. Generation gives J O_Y=A. Very ample section generators 
give a closed immersion into the projective space of J; its integral image and Bl_J R have the same dense punctured graph. Scheme-theoretic 
closure proves Y=Bl_J R. This is an actual primary model in G331, rather than an assumed cofinal arbitrary model. Every prescribed factor 
remains invertible.

The coherent model Jacobian J_Y is unit on the puncture. Full-fibre support and a finite affine cover give integers a,b,N_J with J^a O_Y 
subset J_Y, Delta<=bF, and a_gauge^N_J subset J. The inequalities imply v(J_Y)<=a v(J)<=a N_J at EVERY support. This primary containment is 
the precise use of isolatedness.

For an integral signed exceptional Cartier obstacle C_0, set for EVERY m>=1
\[
I_m=\Gamma(Y,O(mC_0)),\quad
b_m=I_mO_Y O(-mC_0),\quad u_m=-v(I_m)/m.
\]
Hartogs gives I_m subset R. An actual Cartier order-unit bound C_0>=-M F_gauge gives a_gauge^(Mm) subset I_m. Therefore I_m is unit or 
primary at every index. Section products are graded and u_m=f_(C_0)-v(b_m)/m<=f_(C_0) at all valued centres, using the support quotient 
field and canonical punctured trivialization of the invertible sheaf. No total fraction field is mapped through a nonzero support.

For each v, v(I_m) is finite nonnegative and subadditive. Writing arbitrary indices as multiples plus bounded remainders proves the 
ALL-index Fekete limit u_m->sup_m u_m, without monotonicity of the sequence. A rational primary profile -v(I)/q below f_(C_0) satisfies the 
requisite order at every exceptional height-one point of the normal Y; at other height-one points it is automatically regular. The normal 
codimension-one section criterion gives I^r subset I_(rq) for all r. It follows that every rational competitor is below the Fekete limit. 
Rational density with negative shifts handles C; n1 handles D. Thus BEFORE positivity recognition,
\[
p(f_{C_0})=\lim_m u_m=\sup_m u_m,\qquad h=f_{C_0}-p(f_{C_0})\ge0.
\]

Define t_m=tau(Y,Delta,b_bullet^m) and s_m=tau(Y,b_bullet^m). Gradedness and n3 power invariance direct their defining families by common 
multiples. Noetherianity on a finite affine cover makes each stabilize at a common index for any finite list. The transferred subadditivity 
gives J_Y^(ell-1) s_(m ell) subset s_m^ell, with the correct direction.

A scheme-global effective Cartier test divisor D_0 exists. On a finite affine cover choose the BIG seeds and finite Weil rounding 
corrections. Dominate their divisors by an effective Weil E. A high ample negative-fibre twist of O(-E) is generated; a nonzero rational 
section has divisor at least E and cuts an effective Cartier divisor D_0>=E. Normal height-one regularity makes its local equations 
multiples of every chosen seed. By n3 any such regular multiples still give EVERY late tail. CEMS therefore yields, for a chosen stabilizing
 ell and every cutoff E_0,
\[
t_m=\sum_{e\ge E_0}\operatorname{Im}
\left[F_*^e\big(b_\ell^{\lceil q m/\ell\rceil}
 O(K_Y-qL-D_0)\big)\longrightarrow O_Y\right].
\]
D_0, ell and the Serre threshold may depend on m. The generation constant below does not.

The relative Koszul generation statement works over ANY Noetherian affine base. If A is ample generated and H^i(M A^(-i))=0 for 1<=i<=dim Y,
 choose finitely many generating sections. Their Koszul complex is locally split exact, so remains exact after tensoring M. Its higher 
groups successively prove the same vanishings at the next twist and surjectivity of multiplication by the generating sections. Beyond dim Y 
coherent cohomology vanishes. Repetition and high Serre generation show M generated. There is no flatness hypothesis on M or the base. Thus 
choose c_0 once so (c_0-i)H-L is ample for every required i. For each fixed finite coherent list M_j,
\[
F_*^e(M_j O(q(c_0H-L)))
\]
is generated for all sufficiently late e: projection formula makes the Koszul vanishings Serre vanishings for (c_0-i)H-L. Frobenius is 
finite; all sheaves are coherent.

Put a_e=ceil(qm/ell), j_e=ell a_e-qm, so 0<=j_e<ell. Products of the actual global I_ell sections generate b_ell^a_e O(ell a_e C_0). After 
twisting the trace target by O(mC_0+c_0H), its source is a quotient of finitely many copies of
\[
Q_{e,j}=F_*^e O(q(c_0H-L)+K_Y-D_0-jC_0).
\]
The multiplication is F_*t->F_*(s t), INSIDE Frobenius; coefficients are not extracted as ordinary R scalars. For fixed m the finite list 
j=0,...,ell-1 is coherent even when K_Y is not Cartier. The preceding regularity argument generates every sufficiently late source. The 
arbitrary-tail trace formula permits restriction to those degrees. A finite coherent image sum stabilizes on the quasicompact Noetherian 
scheme, possibly using DIFFERENT late exponents. Its target t_m O(mC_0+c_0H) is therefore generated. One exponent realizing the whole trace 
is neither asserted nor needed.

Set c=c_0+1. The sections of F_m=t_m O(mC_0) A^c form an actual ideal J_m of R, with J_m O_Y=F_m. Before the extra A twist the generated 
sheaf's sections are in R by Hartogs and it embeds in O_Y; afterwards it lies in J O_Y. Thus J_m is proper. Let T_0=tau(Y,Delta), unit on 
the puncture and containing J^r O_Y. The tail formula and the identity f phi(F_*z)=phi(F_*(f^q z)) give b_m T_0 subset t_m, by a common 
regular seed and the bounded exponent gap. Consequently I_m J^(r+c) subset J_m, proving primaryness for EVERY m. Its actual geometric 
profile satisfies
\[
g_m=-v(J_m)/m=f_{C_0}-(c v(J)+v(t_m))/m\le f_{C_0}.
\]

Now b_(m ell) T_0 subset t_(m ell) subset s_(m ell), and J_Y^(ell-1) s_(m ell) subset s_m^ell, yield
\[
\frac{v(s_m)}m\le
\frac{v(b_{m\ell})+v(T_0)}{m\ell}
 +\frac{\ell-1}{m\ell}v(J_Y).
\]
All values here are finite because the ideals contain closed-fibre primary powers. FIRST let ell tend to infinity pointwise. Fekete gives 
v(s_m)<=m h+v(J_Y); the finite v(T_0) term disappears. Cartier shift and Delta<=bF give O(-bF)s_m subset t_m subset s_m. Since g_m is 
already an actual competitor, substitution proves
\[
0\le p(f_{C_0})-g_m
\le\frac{(c+b)v(J)+v(J_Y)}m
\le\frac{(c+a+b)N_J}{m}
\]
on the ENTIRE link. The last step, after the pointwise limit, is uniformly primary and retains all nonminimal supports. Hence the raw 
envelope is in C. Signed rational primary lattice functions are dense by G331; each is determined by a finite collection principalized 
above. Clear denominators and use n1 nonexpansivity to obtain CE for every finite continuous obstacle.

The greatest D envelopes for bounded-above extended upper semicontinuous obstacles, decreasing-obstacle-net continuity and exact gauge 
cocycle now follow from n1. G331 completion transports the result exactly to excellent normal characteristic-p local rings whose completions
 have perfect residue and are regular away from the maximal ideal. Isolated excellent normal rings with perfect residue satisfy this: normal
 completion and regular formal fibres give regularity over every nonmaximal regular prime, and the fibre over m is the residue field. This 
is existing G331 completion transport, not new algebraization. At smooth closed affine algebraically closed characteristic-zero germs G331 
gives the exact published BFJ class; the historical BFJ envelope comparison remains at that scope, not at arbitrary singular/imperfect 
germs.

Independent scoped verdict: PASS corrected396's entire new formal BIG theorem and isolated perfect-residue formal CE theorem, as unverified 
mathematical drafts relative to G331 and the named ordinary foundations. The immutable native paragraph is rejected; corrected396 is

# n5. New positive sector: all monomial-weight obstacles on complete normal toric germs

Use G331 and the raw-envelope/nonexpansivity/decreasing-closure results proved in n1. This is new scoped progress on the original envelope 
target, valid over ANY field, including imperfect fields and every characteristic. It concerns actual geometric positivity and all geometric
 competitors, not a new order definition or a restriction to radial functions on a finite link.

Let M be a lattice of rank d, C_0 a pointed full-dimensional rational polyhedral cone in M_R, and S=C_0 intersect M its saturated positive 
monoid. Let R be the completion at the monomial maximal ideal of k[S]. For precision, k[S] is the intersection, in its fraction field, of 
the normal Laurent polynomial ring k[M] with the valuation rings given by the finitely many primitive facet weights. On a Laurent polynomial
 the least facet weight is the least term weight, so these inequalities mean that every exponent belongs to C_0 intersect M. This proves the
 asserted intersection and hence normality. Finite generation is the elementary rational-cone lattice-point theorem. The finite-type ring is
 excellent, and excellent normal completion is normal; thus R is an excellent normal local domain. Its elements are formal sums of monomials
 chi^u, with the maximal-adic completion topology. Fix a monomial primary gauge a. G331 supplies its full all-support compact boundary X and
 independently geometric C,D. These conventional algebraic foundations are used at this exact saturated positive affine-monoid setup; no 
perfect-field base change or torus averaging is used.

The monomial weight of v is w_v(u)=v(chi^u). It is additive, may take infinity, and is strictly positive on nonzero monoid elements when 
finite. The finite-valued elements form a face of S. For finite weights w in the interior of the dual cone sigma=C_0^vee, taking the least 
weight of the terms defines a monomial valuation v_w on the completed ring. Positivity makes the least value well-defined and makes the 
operation compatible with the completion. Distinct monomials in its associated graded cannot cancel. Divide by w(a) to obtain its 
primary-section point.

Every extended monomial weight arising from v is a limit of these finite interior weights, after normalization. Indeed its finite face is 
cut out by a rational exposing functional lambda>=0, zero on that face and strictly positive on its complement. Extend its finite additive 
weight linearly from the face span to M_R. Add N lambda, and if necessary a vanishing small positive interior functional. For large N the 
finitely many monoid generators outside the face become positive, and the generators inside the face have their given positive values. The 
outside values tend to infinity. Some primary-gauge generator has finite value; hence normalized primary values converge as well. Monomial 
primary profiles are continuous on all X by G331. Thus inequalities between such profiles and signed monomial obstacles, checked on finite 
interior weights, hold on every extended monomial weight and hence on EVERY semivaluation having that weight.

For any ideal I of R, let M(I) be the monomial ideal generated by all monomials appearing with nonzero coefficient in a finite set of formal
 generators. Noetherianity makes this ideal finitely generated. A monomial ideal is maximal-adically closed, since its finite-module 
quotient is separated; therefore each series whose terms lie in it belongs to it. Hence I subset M(I). If I contains a primary power then so
 does M(I). At a finite interior monomial valuation, v_w(I)=v_w(M(I)): the least appearing monomial realizes the value and cannot cancel. At
 a general semivaluation, -v(M(I))>=-v(I). This is a domination of arbitrary ideal profiles, proved by term membership, not by an averaging 
operation over k-rational torus points.

Consider a rational signed monomial primary obstacle on rays,
\[
F(w)=\frac{w(A)-w(B)}r,
\]
where A,B are monomial unit-or-primary ideals and r is a positive integer. Finite lattice combinations are of this form by synchronized 
products and sums. On X its restriction f is finite continuous. Write phi=-F, a homogeneous rational piecewise-linear function on sigma. 
Common normal fans of the finite exponent sets of A and B make phi linear on finitely many rational cones. Define
\[
P=\{x\in C_0:\langle x,w\rangle\ge\phi(w)\text{ for all }w\in\sigma\}.
\]
These conditions reduce to the finitely many rays of that fan, together with the cone inequalities. Thus P is a rational polyhedron. Because
 |f| is bounded on the a-section, phi(w)<=T w(a) for a finite T. Therefore P contains T times the Newton polyhedron of a and is nonempty. 
Its recession cone is exactly C_0. The finite polyhedral vertex/recession decomposition, obtained by successively moving a nonvertex to 
bounding faces, gives P=conv(x_1,...,x_h)+C_0, with rational vertices. Pointedness rules out a lineality factor.

Clear denominators with q so q x_i belong to M and hence S. Add sufficiently large powers of EACH monoid generator to the ideal generated by
 chi^(q x_i). These added exponents can be chosen inside qP: for a fan ray w with w(u)=0 on a nonzero monoid generator u, primaryness 
implies w(a)=0 and hence phi(w)=0. All remaining finite inequalities are met by a sufficiently large multiple of u. Call the resulting 
monomial ideal J. Its radical is the maximal ideal, unless P contains0, in which case include1 and use the unit ideal. Adding these points 
does not change its Newton polyhedron, which is qP. Thus
\[
h(w):=\min_{x\in P}\langle x,w\rangle=w(J)/q,
\qquad -h\le F
\]
for finite weights, and the preceding extended-weight continuity proves -v(J)/q<=f on ALL supports. This is an actual primary ideal profile 
and hence an actual negative effective curve-nef Cartier presentation on Bl_J R by G331's independently proved geometric comparison/core 
inclusion.

It is the raw envelope among ALL geometric competitors. For any rational arbitrary-ideal profile -v(I)/l<=f, equality at monomial valuations
 shows -v(M(I))/l<=f there and hence everywhere, while this monomialized profile dominates the original. Each generating exponent u of M(I) 
satisfies u/l in P, so w(M(I))/l>=h(w); the same domination holds at extended weights by continuity. Consequently -v(I)/l<=-v(J)/q at every 
semivaluation. To handle C competitors, approximate by rational primary profiles, then make a negative rational gauge shift to keep them 
below f. Their errors vanish. N1 identifies the C and D raw suprema. Therefore
\[
p(f)=-v(J)/q\in C_{\rm geom}
\]
and this is the greatest D minorant. This controls arbitrary nonmonomial ideal profiles, their real uniform limits, and completed D 
competitors; it is not merely a toric-restricted supremum. The formula gives a finite rational polyhedral construction for every rational 
signed monomial model obstacle.

Let W be the compact image of X under all monomial evaluations. Primary monomial profile differences contain rational constants, form a 
lattice by products and ideal sums, and separate W using (chi^u)+a^N, whose value is min(w(u),N). The compact lattice approximation proof 
therefore makes their rational span uniformly dense in C(W). For every finite continuous obstacle f=F_0 composed with the weight map, choose
 such rational signed obstacles tending uniformly to it. N1 nonexpansivity makes their raw envelopes uniformly Cauchy. Their limit is p(f), 
belongs to C_geom, and is weight-dependent. Thus EVERY finite continuous monomial-weight obstacle has an actually positive continuous 
envelope, not just the rational ones.

For a bounded-above extended upper semicontinuous obstacle on W, take all finite continuous nonpositive majorants of its clipping to0, 
directed by minima. Their envelopes are in C_geom by the preceding theorem and form one decreasing net. N1 decreasing closure shows its 
infimum is in D_geom; it is below the obstacle and dominates every D competitor. This gives its greatest D envelope, with the appropriate 
upper semicontinuity, poles/bottom, and decreasing-obstacle-net stability for specified upper semicontinuous limits. The ray formulation and
 n1 give the exact gauge cocycle for ANY primary section; changing a monomial gauge is the immediate weight-coordinate formula. At these 
normal germs normalization is the identity and conductor fibres are singletons. No nonnormal monomial descent theorem is asserted.

This includes normal nonisolated toric germs of arbitrary dimension and monomial-weight obstacles over imperfect residue fields. For example
 k[[s^2,st,t^2,z]] has a nonisolated singular line in dimension3. The nonsimplicial rank3 saturated cone generated by 
(1,0,0),(1,1,0),(1,0,1),(1,1,1) gives k[[a,b,c,d]]/(ad-bc); adding formal monomial variables gives nonisolated examples. The theorem does 
NOT prove CE for arbitrary obstacles that distinguish valuations with the same monomial values, or for arbitrary excellent germs. Its smooth
 specialization uses the same G331 cone; in the published smooth affine closed/algebraically closed/characteristic-zero range it is the 
restriction of the BFJ envelope, because both are greatest minorants of that identical class. This does not extend BFJ's published 
hypotheses or identify literal analytic/CLD radial extensions.

Artifacts: n5.md, toric_envelope.py, inputs/toric-examples.json and reports/toric-envelopes.json. The own exact program implements the 
finite rational fan/vertex construction for its two explicitly supplied rank3 examples; its finite outputs are certificates of those 
computations, not a proof of the universal theorem. Rerun: python toric_envelope.py. No supplied code, solver, compiler, field extension, 
network or resource-heavy computation is used.

# n6. New normal nonisolated obstruction to a universal primary correction

Use the explicit BIG convention in n3 and the toric setup of n5 only at its stated scope. The calculation below proves its all-map 
test-ideal formula independently; no toric test-ideal formula or finite-map operator is imported. Let k be perfect of odd characteristic p, 
and
\[
R=k[[U,V,W,z]]/(UW-V^2)=k[[s^2,st,t^2,z]],
\quad B=k[[s,t,z]],\quad P=(U,V,W).
\]
R is an excellent normal three-dimensional domain, and its singular locus is the formal line P. This follows from the saturated monoid or 
the hypersurface and its codimension-two Jacobian locus. Write monomials as chi^m=s^a t^b z^c, with m in M={(a,b,c) in Z^3:a+b even}, all 
coordinates nonnegative. For N>=1 set A_N=(U,W^N,z^N), a genuine primary ideal, and
\[
w_N(a,b,c)=a/2+b/(2N)+c/N,\qquad
H_{N,t}=\langle\chi^m:w_N(m+(1,1,1))>t\rangle.
\]
We claim tau_R(A_N^t)=H_(N,t) for every real t>=0, using stability exponents ceil(t(q-1)).

First every R Cartier map extends to a B Cartier map. The fraction field extension L/K is separable quadratic; purely inseparable root 
extension gives L tensor_K K^(1/q)=L^(1/q). Hence an R-linear phi extends uniquely to an L-linear map on L^(1/q). Outside (s,t) the finite 
cover is etale: where s is invertible, B is given by S^2=U with derivative2S a unit, and similarly for t. Frobenius root base change on this
 chart is explicit, since s^(1/q)=s (U^(1/q))^(-(q-1)/2), with t=V/s; the t-chart is analogous. Thus the extended map carries the root 
module into B at every height-one localization. Since B^(1/q) is finite free and B is normal, the intersection-of-height-one-localizations 
criterion makes all its coefficients integral globally. The extension is an actual B-linear map B^(1/q)->B. Codimension-two etaleness and 
normality, not a general trace theorem, justify this step.

In the regular ring B, the root monomials with residues0,...,q-1 in each coordinate form a free basis. For any monomial chi^h in a source 
and any output monomial chi^n of any B Cartier map, these basis expansions give
\[
q n_i+(q-1)\ge h_i\quad(i=1,2,3).
\]
The map coefficients are power series with nonnegative exponents. Thus cancellation can only remove possible output monomials. If chi^h is 
in A_N^r H_(N,t), r=ceil(t(q-1)), then w_N(h)+w_N(1,1,1)>r+t. The displayed coordinate bound gives
\[
q w_N(n+(1,1,1))\ge w_N(h)+w_N(1,1,1)>r+t\ge qt.
\]
H_(N,t) is therefore stable under every extended B map and hence EVERY R map. Monomial ideals are adically closed, so this calculation 
handles formal series as well as polynomial monomials. It is nonzero, indeed contains sufficiently high primary powers.

To prove minimality, let K be any generically nonzero stable ideal. Invert c=UW. The ring becomes regular and A_N becomes unit. Finite Hom 
localization and the primitive-vector Frobenius argument of n3 give K_c=R_c. Hence d=(UW)^L belongs to K for some integer L. For a target 
m=(a,b,c_0) satisfying w_N(m+1)>t, choose q=p^e large and r=ceil(t(q-1)). The three capacities
\[
\left\lfloor\frac{q(a+1)-2L-1}{2}\right\rfloor,
\quad\left\lfloor\frac{q(b+1)-2L-1}{2N}\right\rfloor,
\quad\left\lfloor\frac{q(c_0+1)-1}{N}\right\rfloor
\]
are nonnegative and their sum exceeds r for all sufficiently large e: dividing by q gives w_N(m+1)>t. Choose i,j,h within these capacities 
with i+j+h=r. The monomial d U^i W^(Nj) z^(Nh) lies in A_N^r K; its exponent A has A_i<q(m_i+1). Put alpha=m-A/q, so alpha_i>-1 and alpha in
 (1/q)M.

\section*{Main theorem and proof map}
Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be excellent local and replace it by its reduction.
For every proper primary $\mathfrak a$, let $V_{\mathfrak a}$ be the compact
section of centred real semivaluations with $v(\mathfrak a)=1$, retaining every
prime support. Define $Q$ by finite nonnegative real sums of negative
unit-or-primary ideal values, $C$ by uniform closure, and $D$ by actual infima
of nonempty decreasing $C$-nets, with bottom allowed.

On actual primary blowups, take actual negative effective finite real Cartier
presentations having nonnegative degree on every contracted proper integral
curve. Their evaluations define $M_{\rm geom}$ independently of ideal
positivity. Then
\[
 Q\subset M_{\rm geom}\subset C,\qquad
 C_{\rm geom}=C,\qquad D_{\rm geom}=D.
\]
For every reduced finite injection, the pullback image of either completed
class is precisely its full-fibre-constant subclass. Normalization fibres are
singletons at finite conductor value and precisely conductor-quotient fibres
at infinite value. Primary changes obey the exact homogeneous cocycle.
At a smooth affine closed germ over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero
field, $C$ is exactly the finite continuous BFJ subclass and $D$ is the full
BFJ all-semivaluation extension with the identically bottom function adjoined.
Smooth DVR and empty dimension zero are direct.

give full algebraic descent; n7 discharges the exact published geometric inputs;

\section{n1. Boundary, finite lifting, conductor fibres, and completion}
\textit{Earlier local supports: none.}

All rings below are commutative. For a Noetherian local ring \((R,\mathfrak m)\), a centred real semivaluation is a map to \([0,+\infty]\) 
satisfying \(v(0)=+\infty\), \(v(1)=0\), multiplicativity, the ultrametric inequality, and \(0<v(\mathfrak m)<+\infty\). Its support 
\(v^{-1}(+\infty)\) is a prime strictly below \(\mathfrak m\); no minimal-support restriction is imposed. Ideal values are minima over 
finite generating sets. Relations between generating sets prove independence and
\[
v(IJ)=v(I)+v(J),\qquad v(I+J)=\min\{v(I),v(J)\}.
\]
Units have value zero. A proper primary ideal always means primary for the marked maximal ideal.

Fix a proper primary ideal \(\mathfrak a\). The section \(V_{\mathfrak a}(R)=\{v:v(\mathfrak a)=1\}\) is compact Hausdorff. Indeed 
semivaluation axioms and \(v(\mathfrak m)=1\) are closed conditions in the compact product \([0,+\infty]^R\); addition, minimum and the 
order relation have the required continuity/closedness. Choose \(\mathfrak m^r\subset\mathfrak a\subset\mathfrak m^s\), with \(r\ge s\ge1\).
 Then \(s v(\mathfrak m)\le v(\mathfrak a)\le r v(\mathfrak m)\). Rescaling identifies the two sections. Every primary ideal value is finite
 positive continuous and bounded there. For another primary ideal \(\mathfrak b\),
\[
H_{\mathfrak a,\mathfrak b}(v)=v/v(\mathfrak b),\qquad
u_{\mathfrak b}(H_{\mathfrak a,\mathfrak b}v)=u_{\mathfrak a}(v)/v(\mathfrak b).
\]
The denominator and its inverse are bounded. Substitution proves the inverse and the exact three-gauge cocycle. The centred cone is the 
product of its section and the positive radial coordinate \(v(\mathfrak a)\); hence these sections represent its intrinsic ray quotient. 
Nonprimary proper ideals give only their open finite-value domain, which can be noncompact. Units and zero ideals have no level-one section.

Nilpotents have infinite value. Comparing \(f+n\) and \((f+n)-n\) proves that reduction preserves every semivaluation and ideal gauge. A 
zero-dimensional reduced local ring is a field and has empty centred boundary. For a positive-dimensional excellent reduced local ring, a 
penultimate prime of a saturated chain to the maximal ideal gives a one-dimensional excellent domain quotient. Its finite normalization has 
a local DVR factor, whose order pulls back and normalizes into the section. This proves nonemptiness. Ordinary background used throughout is
 lying over, prime avoidance, finite Artinian decompositions, and the quotient/finite-type-localization stability, Nagata finiteness and 
universal catenarity consequences of excellence. None is used to assert resolution in arbitrary characteristic.

Every finite integral injection \(R\hookrightarrow B\), with \(B\) reduced and nonzero, gives a continuous surjective restriction 
\(V_{\mathfrak aB}(B)\to V_{\mathfrak a}(R)\). Here a finite algebra has the finite union of its closed-centre sections above \(\mathfrak 
m\). To lift \(v\) with support \(\mathfrak p\), choose a prime \(P\) of \(B\) above \(\mathfrak p\) and form the finite field extension 
\(\operatorname{Frac}(B/P)/\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak p)\). Extend the valuation ring by taking the integral closure, a prime over its 
maximal ideal, and a dominating valuation ring. The domination assertion follows from Zorn: in a maximal dominating local subring, either 
adjoining \(x\) or \(x^{-1}\) leaves the maximal ideal proper. If \(1=\sum a_i x^{-i}\) with all \(a_i\) in that ideal, multiplying by a 
power and dividing by \(1-a_0\) makes \(x\) integral, so lying over makes the ideal proper after adjoining \(x\). Localizing contradicts 
maximality unless one of the two elements already belongs. Intersection with the old field is the original valuation ring: an element 
outside it has inverse in its maximal ideal. An algebraic equation for any new nonzero field element has two least-valued terms; thus an 
integer multiple of its value is in the old value group. Dividing this old real value by the integer gives a well-defined order-preserving 
real embedding, using common multiples. Integral elements have nonnegative value by the least-term test for a monic equation. Compose with 
\(B\to B/P\), assigning \(P\) infinite value. This construction first kills the support; it never extends a nonzero-support semivaluation to
 the original fraction field. Compactness makes restriction a quotient map.

Let \(S\) be the finite normalization of an excellent reduced \(R\), and \(\mathfrak c=(R:S)\). Clearing denominators of finitely many 
generators of \(S\) gives a regular conductor element. The conductor is an ideal of both rings and
\[
R=S\times_{S/\mathfrak c}(R/\mathfrak c).
\]
An element of \(S\) whose residue comes from \(R\) differs from an element of \(R\) by an element of \(\mathfrak c\), proving this identity.
 The normalization boundary is the finite disjoint union of local normal centres above \(\mathfrak m\). Idempotents choose a minimal 
component; localization at its centre changes no values of denominators. Chinese remainder elements separating the finitely many centres, 
and their complements, have open positive-value loci selecting these pieces. The pieces are therefore clopen. Branches mean these local 
centres, not merely minimal primes.

If \(v(\mathfrak c)<+\infty\), choose \(c\in\mathfrak c\) of finite value. Every lift satisfies \(w(s)=v(cs)-v(c)\), so it is unique. The 
subtracted number is finite. If \(v(\mathfrak c)=+\infty\), all lifts kill the conductor, and equality after restriction \(S/\mathfrak c\to 
R/\mathfrak c\) is exactly their identification. This infinity stratum is closed; its finite complement is open, without a closedness claim.
 A fibre-constant continuous function descends continuously by the compact quotient. A fibre-constant extended nonpositive upper 
semicontinuous function descends upper semicontinuously: its closed superlevel sets have compact, hence closed, images. These assertions 
alone supply no positivity descent.

Completion preserves the entire boundary for every Noetherian local ring. For \(F\in\widehat R\), choose representatives \(F_N\) modulo 
\(\mathfrak m^N\), and put \(d=v(\mathfrak m)>0\). Differences have value at least \(Nd\). If some \(v(F_N)<Nd\), later values stabilize; 
otherwise they tend to infinity. Define \(\widehat v(F)\) by this limit. It is independent of representatives and satisfies
\[
\min\{\widehat v(F),Nd\}=\min\{v(F_N),Nd\}.
\]
Applying this to sums and products proves all axioms and uniqueness, including infinite values; completed units have unit representatives. 
Compose with \(q(t)=t/(1+t)\), \(q(+\infty)=1\). The displayed continuous truncations have uniform error at most \((1+N/r)^{-1}\), because 
\(d\ge1/r\). Thus completed evaluation is continuous and completion restriction is a homeomorphism. Every completed primary \(J\) contains 
\(\widehat{\mathfrak m}^N\). Representatives modulo that power of its generators belong to \(J\cap R\) and, with the boundary power, 
generate \(J\). Hence \(J=(J\cap R)\widehat R\). The quotient isomorphism also proves contraction of an extended primary ideal recovers it. 
Unit-or-primary profiles and their uniform and decreasing classes therefore agree under completion. No equivalence of geometric model 
categories is asserted.

This is a mathematical argument with the stated ordinary background. Swanson--Huneke 6.4.1--2 were read in full and agree with the 
domination proof. Artifact n1.md is authoritative and is reproduced in argument.md and the paper. Rerun: python audit\_inputs.py; python 
build\_delivery.py. Execution does not verify the mathematics.
