\section{n1. Finite contact certificates on every excellent germ}

Support: G331, with its entire source, annotation, ledger and scope unchanged. No result of current401, B341 or E350 is a premise. We prove 
a general excellent-germ theorem, followed by an explicit monomial certificate. No general CE is assumed.

Let R be an excellent local ring whose reduction has positive dimension, a a proper primary gauge, and X=V\_a(R). All ideals and 
semivaluations below are interpreted on the reduction, as required by G331. Let J be ANY proper primary ideal and q a positive integer. 
There is a FINITE nonempty set E\_J of centred semivaluations on X such that the independently geometric classes of G331 satisfy
\[
 u\in D,\quad u(x)\le -v_x(J)/q\ (x\in E_J)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad u(v)\le-v(J)/q\ (v\in X).       \tag{G1}
\]
Thus for ANY continuous obstacle f, however nonmonomial, the conditions
\[
 f\ge H=-v(J)/q\text{ everywhere},\qquad f|_{E_J}=H|_{E_J} \tag{G2}
\]
give its greatest geometric D envelope P(f)=H in the actual geometric core. The same holds for any bounded-above upper semicontinuous f 
satisfying (G2). If f>=H-epsilon and f(x)<=H(x)+delta at all contacts, epsilon,delta>=0, then H-epsilon<=p(f)<=H+delta, without assuming 
positivity of p(f). These are sufficient conditions, not a density or necessity theorem for arbitrary obstacles.

We construct and prove the certificate first when R is an excellent NORMAL local domain. Normalize the actual primary blowup Bl\_J(R). 
Excellence makes normalization finite, so Y is projective, normal and Noetherian. The pulled-back ideal J O\_Y=O\_Y(-E) is invertible and E 
is an ACTUAL effective Cartier divisor supported over the closed point. Normalization is only used to test inequalities; H itself already 
has its actual nef primary-blowup presentation on Bl\_J(R). No cofinality among arbitrary models, new cone definition, or positivity on a 
merely numerical Weil list is invoked.

The effective divisor E has finitely many prime components E\_1,...,E\_s, all of height one and all lying over the closed point. The DVR 
orders nu\_i=ord\_\{E\_i\} restrict to valuations of Frac(R) centred at m. They have 0<nu\_i(a)<infinity and nu\_i(J)>0: every element of m 
is in the height-one maximal ideal at that centre, and a,J contain primary powers. Normalize nu\_i by nu\_i(a) to define E\_J. There is at 
least one component: J O\_Y is nonunit at any point of the nonempty closed fibre, and a nonunit regular local Cartier equation has a 
height-one prime. Proper birationality gives the nonempty fibre over the positive-dimensional domain.

Let u=-v(I)/r be any rational unit-or-primary profile and assume its contact inequalities. After clearing q and r they say
\[
 \nu_i(I^q)\ge r\nu_i(J)\quad (1\le i\le s).              \tag{G3}
\]
For each generator t of I\textasciicircum{}q, (G3) gives the height-one section condition t in O\_Y(-rE) at every E\_i. At all other 
height-one points E has coefficient zero and t, being in R, is regular. The normal codimension-one section criterion on every affine open 
therefore proves
\[
 I^q O_Y\subset J^r O_Y.                                  \tag{G4}
\]
This is a direct proof of the needed finite Rees-valuation implication. No toric or test-ideal theorem, or Rees integral-closure criterion, 
is imported as an additional premise.

To evaluate (G4) at ANY v in X, including nonzero prime support p, pass first to its valued quotient field Frac(R/p). The generic point p 
differs from m, so Y is isomorphic there. Properness and the valuative criterion lift the map of its valuation ring to Y. The local 
generator of J O\_Y at this valued centre has nonzero image, because J has finite value and its canonical generic trivialization is off the 
closed fibre. Pull (G4) to the valuation ring. The value of the invertible J ideal is exactly v(J), since the base generators generate it 
and one local coefficient is a unit. Hence qv(I)>=rv(J). This proves u<=H on EVERY support. No map from the original total fraction ring 
through p or subtraction of infinite values is attempted.

For a general excellent reduced R, its finite normalization is the semilocal union of normal local centres S\_i. Every extension J S\_i is 
proper primary for its marked centre. Form the preceding finite certificate at every S\_i with gauge a S\_i and restrict all these points to
 X\_R. Their union is finite. A D\_R function satisfying those downstairs tests has a positive pullback by G331, satisfying the tests on 
every normal centre. The normal theorem controls it on EVERY source point, and surjectivity of the boundary restriction controls it on every
 downstairs point. This proves (G1). The full conductor relation is respected: H is the evaluation of a DOWNSTAIRS primary ideal, so its 
pullback is constant on all fibres, including the infinite-conductor quotient stratum. No separate compatibility of arbitrary source extrema
 is asserted.

The C,D steps require no completion shortcut. For g in C with the contact bounds, approximate by a rational primary profile within epsilon 
and subtract a rational primary-gauge constant between epsilon and 2epsilon. This is again a rational profile after clearing denominators 
and multiplying by a power of a. It satisfies all exact contact bounds, hence is below H by (G3)--(G4). Let epsilon tend to zero. For 
u=inf\_i g\_i in D, finitely many strict contact tests and directedness select one term with g\_i(x)<H(x)+epsilon at EVERY contact, even if 
u has poles there. Apply the C implication to g\_i-epsilon and let epsilon tend to zero. This proves (G1) for ACTUAL decreasing nets, bottom
 and partial poles, without flattening, increasing closure or CE. H is an actual geometric competitor under (G2), so the envelope statement 
follows. The quantitative statement applies (G1) to competitors shifted by -delta and uses H-epsilon as an actual C competitor.

For nilpotent R this is exactly the reduction theory of G331, without unreduced intersection multiplicities. In dimension zero the boundary 
is empty and the unique empty envelope is direct. The unit barrier is zero and needs no contacts. Thus this theorem supplies a nonmonomial 
obstacle sector over EVERY excellent singular or nonnormal germ, including mixed characteristic and imperfect residue. It does not assert 
continuity for obstacles which do not satisfy (G2). Its conventional backgrounds are finite normalization, proper valuative criterion and 
normal codimension-one sections at their actual Noetherian excellent hypotheses. These are disclosed backgrounds, not new incoming grants.

Rerun delivery: python prepare\_delivery.py; python verify\_delivery.py. The entire explicit toric specialization follows in this same 
authoritative n1 note. Artifact paths and commands are evidence of retention, not theorem premises.

\subsection{Explicit saturated-monoid certificate and finite arithmetic implementation}

Support: G331, with its entire source, annotation, ledger and scope unchanged. No result of current401, B341 or E350 is a premise. The 
argument below reconstructs the required monomial facts and proves the new envelope theorem directly.

Let M be a rank-d lattice, T a pointed full-dimensional rational polyhedral cone, S=T intersect M, and R the completion of k[S] at its 
monomial maximal ideal, over any field k. Let a be any monomial primary gauge, X=V\_a(R), and C,D the independently geometric classes of 
qualified G331. In particular, C is the uniform closure of negative finite real primary profiles, rational profiles are uniformly dense, and
 D is made of actual decreasing C-nets. These are consequences of the granted geometric comparison, not new definitions of positivity. Every
 semivaluation support is included.

The monoid is finitely generated by the rational-cone lattice-point theorem. The affine ring is normal: in its fraction field it is the 
intersection of the normal Laurent polynomial ring k[M] and the valuation rings of the primitive facet weights. For a Laurent polynomial 
each facet minimum is the minimum of its term weights; nonnegativity of all these minima says exactly that every exponent belongs to T. The 
finite-type ring is excellent, and its normal local ring has normal excellent completion. Thus the stipulated R is an excellent normal local
 domain over arbitrary k. These exact conventional algebraic facts require neither perfection nor a finite extension of a regular local 
ring. Its elements have unique formal monomial expansions in the maximal-adic topology.

Fix a nonunit monomial primary ideal J and a positive integer q. Put H(v)=-v(J)/q. This is an actual geometric core function: on Bl\_J(R) 
its negative effective Cartier exceptional divisor has an ample negative bundle and nonnegative degree on every contracted proper integral 
curve, as granted and proved in G331. H is finite continuous on all X. Write
\[
 P_J=\operatorname{conv}\{u_1,\ldots,u_h\}+T
\]
for its Newton polyhedron, using a finite monomial generating set. A finite rational half-space presentation consists of the cone 
inequalities together with finitely many inequalities
\[
 \langle x,w_j\rangle\ge b_j,\qquad b_j>0.                 \tag{1}
\]
Every w\_j in (1) is in the interior of the dual cone. Indeed, a supporting normal is nonnegative on the recession cone T. If it has zero 
value on a nonzero monoid generator g, primaryness puts some Ng in P\_J, so its supporting intercept is zero. Such zero-intercept 
inequalities are already consequences of x in T. Consequently all positive-intercept facet normals are strictly positive on all monoid 
generators. The elementary finite rational polyhedral half-space/vertex theorem applies here; no toric test-ideal theorem is used.

For an interior dual weight w, the minimum weight of terms defines a centred monomial valuation of the completed ring. Positivity on the 
finitely many generators bounds the number of monomials of bounded weight and proves the minimum exists. The associated graded monomials 
cannot cancel, so multiplication and the ultrametric inequality hold. Normalize by w(a). Denote the resulting point associated to w\_j by 
x\_j. Then
\[
 v_{x_j}(J)=b_j/w_j(a).
\]
The finite set E\_J=\{x\_j\} is a contact certificate for H in the following strong sense:
\[
 u\in D,\quad u(x_j)\le H(x_j)\ (\text{every }j)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad u(v)\le H(v)\ (\text{every }v\in X).       \tag{2}
\]

Here is a proof on every support that avoids approximating an infinite monomial weight. First let u=-v(I)/r be a rational primary or unit 
profile. Let M(I) be the monomial ideal generated by all terms in a finite collection of formal generators of I. Noetherianity makes it 
generated by finitely many of those terms. Moreover I is contained in M(I): each finite truncation of a generator belongs to this monomial 
ideal, and the ideal is adically closed by separation of its finite quotient. At every interior monomial valuation v\_w(I)=v\_w(M(I)), 
because a least term in a generator cannot cancel against distinct monomials.

The contact inequalities imply, for every occurring exponent u\_0,
\[
 q\langle u_0,w_j\rangle\ge r b_j,
 \qquad q u_0\in rP_J.                                    \tag{3}
\]
The second statement follows from the complete half-space presentation and u\_0 in S. Write q u\_0 as a rational convex combination of the r
 u\_i plus a rational vector in T. Such a rational decomposition exists: it solves a finite rational linear system with nonnegative 
unknowns, and row reduction on the minimal face of a real solution gives rational feasible points. Clear its denominators by a positive 
integer D\_0. The recession remainder then lies in S, by saturation, and
\[
 \chi^{D_0 q u_0}\in J^{rD_0}.
\]
Thus chi\textasciicircum{}\{q u\_0\} is integral over J\textasciicircum{}r, using the equation 
Z\textasciicircum{}\{D\_0\}-chi\textasciicircum{}\{D\_0 q u\_0\}=0. For any semivaluation v in X, J has finite value because it is primary. 
Integral dependence implies
\[
 qv(\chi^{u_0})\ge r v(J).                                 \tag{4}
\]
If the left side is infinite this is automatic. Otherwise a hypothetical strict inequality makes the leading monic term in the integral 
equation have uniquely smallest finite value, contradicting the ultrametric inequality. Taking the minimum over the finite monomial 
generators of M(I), then using I subset M(I), proves v(I)/r>=v(J)/q on EVERY support. This proves (2) for rational profiles without assuming
 that monomialization preserves an arbitrary obstacle.

For g in C satisfying the contact inequalities, approximate g uniformly by a rational primary profile within epsilon. Subtract a rational 
primary-gauge constant between epsilon and 2epsilon. This subtraction is again a single rational profile after clearing denominators and 
taking an ideal product. It satisfies the exact contact inequalities, hence is at most H everywhere by the preceding proof. Let epsilon tend
 to zero to obtain g<=H. For u=inf\_i g\_i in D, the finite contact set and directedness select one term with g\_i(x\_j)<H(x\_j)+epsilon for
 every j, even if u has poles at some contacts. Then g\_i-epsilon is in C and satisfies the contact inequalities. Hence u<=H+epsilon, and 
epsilon tends to zero. This proves (2) for the ACTUAL decreasing completion, including bottom and partial poles; no flattening or increasing
 closure is used.

Now let f be ANY finite continuous obstacle on X, with no weight-dependence assumption, such that
\[
 f\ge H\text{ on }X,\qquad f(x_j)=H(x_j)\text{ for every }j.             \tag{5}
\]
H is a geometric competitor. Every geometric D competitor below f satisfies (2), so is below H. Consequently
\[
 \sup\{u\in D:u\le f\}=H\in C.
\]
This is an actually positive continuous greatest geometric envelope among ALL competitors. The same proof works for ANY bounded-above 
extended upper semicontinuous f satisfying (5); its envelope is still the continuous function H. Here (5) forces f to be finite below, 
although its upper size may vary. The unit case J=R has H=0 and no contacts; every obstacle f>=0 has envelope zero by nonpositivity.

There is a quantitative version with no presumed continuity of the raw envelope. If f>=H-epsilon everywhere and f(x\_j)<=H(x\_j)+delta at 
the finite contacts, for epsilon,delta>=0, then
\[
 H-\epsilon\le p(f)\le H+\delta.                           \tag{6}
\]
The lower inequality uses the actual C competitor H-epsilon. The upper inequality applies (2) to each competitor shifted by -delta. Thus 
increasingly accurate lower barriers and contact bounds give uniform approximation of raw envelopes to H, even when CE is not established 
for each perturbed obstacle. Conditions (5) are sufficient; no necessity or density among all obstacles is claimed.

This advances beyond weight-dependent obstacles: arbitrary cancellation-sensitive functions satisfying the finite contacts are allowed. The 
general theorem above removes the toric hypothesis for the finite-contact obstacle sector. Neither theorem supplies arbitrary-obstacle CE or
 an envelope counterexample. Finite geometry controls the competitors; the obstacle is never averaged or monomialized. G331 remains the sole
 correctness grant. The proof's conventional backgrounds are finite rational polyhedral geometry, Gordan's finite-generation lemma, normal 
excellent completion, and finite-module adic separation, at exactly the stated hypotheses.

Artifacts: n1.md, proof-companion.md and P12.3-contact-envelopes.tex. The explicit finite certificate used in n2 is implemented by the 
independently written contact\_certificate.py, with contact-input.json and contact-output.json. Rerun: python contact\_certificate.py. 
Program success is only finite arithmetic evidence, not a proof of (2) or of general CE.


\section{n2. Explicit nonmonomial primary obstacles on normal nonisolated fourfolds, including mixed characteristic}

Support: G331 and earlier own n1. We use n1's finite-contact theorem, not the current401 toric-envelope theorem or a finite-cover theorem.

For ANY field k let
\[
 R=k[[a,b,c,d,z]]/(ad-bc),\quad \mathfrak m=(a,b,c,d,z),\quad
 J=(a^2,b^3,c^3,d^2,z^4),\quad
 K=(a+b,c+d,z)+\mathfrak m^2.                               \tag{7}
\]
Both J and K are genuine primary ideals. J contains powers of every maximal generator, and K contains m\textasciicircum{}2. Write the 
saturated monoid cone in Z\textasciicircum{}4 with generators
\[
 g_a=(1,0,0,0),\ g_b=(1,1,0,0),\ g_c=(1,0,1,0),\
 g_d=(1,1,1,0),\ g_z=(0,0,0,1).
\]
The cone consists of x\_2,x\_3,x\_4>=0, x\_1>=x\_2,x\_3. Every integer point is generated by these vectors: choose the coefficient of g\_d 
between max(0,x\_2+x\_3-x\_1) and min(x\_2,x\_3), then use g\_b,g\_c,g\_a for the remainder and g\_z for x\_4. The only lattice relation 
among the first four generators is g\_a+g\_d=g\_b+g\_c. Reducing monomials by ad=bc gives the monoid algebra presentation. Thus (7) is the 
normal excellent complete germ of n1. Its dimension is four. It is regular where any of a,b,c,d is invertible, by solving its equation for 
the opposite variable. At P=(a,b,c,d), the equation has no linear term in the four normal variables, so that localization has embedding 
dimension four and dimension three. Its singular locus is exactly the positive-dimensional line P, over every k, including characteristic 
two. This is a normal nonisolated germ.

The Newton polyhedron of J has the following COMPLETE presentation: the cone inequalities and
\[
 \langle x,w_+\rangle\ge1,\quad \langle x,w_-\rangle\ge1,\qquad
 w_\pm=(1/2,\ \pm1/6,\ \mp1/6,\ 1/4).                  \tag{8}
\]
Both normals are interior to the dual cone: their values on the five generators are respectively (1/2,2/3,1/3,1/2,1/4) and 
(1/2,1/3,2/3,1/2,1/4). To check completeness without assuming a program's answer, the section at x\_4=0 is the cone over the unit square 
x\_1=1, cut by (3x\_1+x\_2-x\_3)/6>=1 and (3x\_1-x\_2+x\_3)/6>=1. Its four vertices are (2,0,0),(3,3,0),(3,0,3),(2,2,2). This follows by 
considering the four square-edge equalities x\_2=0, x\_3=0, x\_1=x\_2, x\_1=x\_3; intersections of both cutting planes force x\_2=x\_3 and 
x\_1=2, whose endpoints are (2,0,0) and (2,2,2). Each individual cutting plane's remaining endpoint is the corresponding opposite square 
corner at x\_1=3. There are no other vertex intersections. For 0<=x\_4<=4, the right sides for this three-dimensional section are 1-x\_4/4. 
For x\_4>4 the section is the whole recession cone. Consequently the full polyhedron has precisely those four vertices with fourth 
coordinate zero and (0,0,0,4), and recession cone T. These are exactly the five generating exponents in (7), proving (8).

Normalize by the monomial primary gauge m. The two contacts v\_+,v\_- in n1 have generator values
\[
 (a,b,c,d,z)=(2,8/3,4/3,2,1),\quad (2,4/3,8/3,2,1),
\]
respectively. Both have v(m)=1 and v(J)=4. At EVERY interior monomial valuation, a+b and c+d have their least term values without 
cancellation, so v(K)=v(m). This also follows at the two contacts directly from the displayed numbers. For an arbitrary semivaluation in 
V\_m, containment m\textasciicircum{}2 subset K subset m gives 1<=v(K)<=2. Define for any real delta>=0
\[
 f_\delta=-v(J)+\delta\big(v(K)-v(\mathfrak m)\big).
                                                                    \tag{9}
\]
This is a finite continuous obstacle on the entire compact boundary. It is at least H=-v(J), and agrees with H at both contacts. By n1 its 
greatest geometric D envelope is exactly
\[
 P(f_\delta)=-v(J).
                                                                    \tag{10}
\]
For delta=1/2 this is a rational signed PRIMARY model obstacle:
\[
 f_{1/2}=\big(v(K)-v(J^2\mathfrak m)\big)/2.
\]
The primary product blowup principalizes J,K,m, so it is the evaluation of an actual signed exceptional rational Cartier divisor there. Its 
obstacle need not be nef. Its envelope is the actual negative effective nef Cartier profile on Bl\_J(R), not positivity conferred by upper 
regularization. Since J subset m\textasciicircum{}2, f\_\{1/2\}<=-3/2 throughout V\_m; it is a genuinely negative example.

To prove the obstacle is genuinely nonmonomial, consider the quotient map to k[[r,h,z]] given by
\[
 a=c=r,\qquad b=d=r(h-1),\qquad z=z,
\]
followed by the monomial valuation with r,h,z weights 1,1,3. The relation ad=bc is identically satisfied. The kernel on R is (c-a,d-b): the 
quotient is k[[a,b,z]], and substitution a=r,b=r(h-1) is injective because replacing b by a+b sends its two coordinates to r,rh, whose 
distinct monomials r\textasciicircum{}\{i+j\}h\textasciicircum{}j have distinct exponent pairs. This is a prime support strictly below m. It
 is an allowed centred semivaluation, normalized already by v(m)=1, and
\[
 v(a,b,c,d,z)=(1,1,1,1,3),\quad v(K)=2,\quad v(J)=2.
\]
The equalities a+b=c+d=rh hold over every field, including characteristic two. At the monomial valuation w\_0=(1,0,0,3) on R, the monomial 
weights of all five generators are identical, but w\_0(K)=1 and w\_0(J)=2. Therefore
\[
 f_{1/2}(v)=-3/2,\qquad f_{1/2}(w_0)=-2.
\]
They have the same values on EVERY monomial by additivity. Hence (9) cannot be a function only of monomial weights. This is an actual 
nonmonomial continuous signed primary/model obstacle, not a coordinate re-description of a weight-only obstacle.

The retained singular-supported valuation killing P and giving z value one has v(m)=v(K)=1, v(J)=4, and f\_delta=-4. Its Jacobian value 
v((a,b,c,d)) is infinite. Formula (10) includes this point and all other supports. No nonprimary correction is divided by an index, and no 
support is discarded. The proof uses finite contact inequalities and genuine primary profiles. It is independent of the Frobenius/test-ideal
 route and works over imperfect fields and all characteristics. It proves an obstacle sector, not CE for arbitrary obstacles on this ring. 
It does not prove that this ring lacks a finite regular cover, and no such premise is needed.

Evidence: the own program contact\_certificate.py enumerates the five choose four candidate positive facets and the seven choose four 
candidate vertices by exact rational row reduction. Its observed output is two positive facet normals, five vertices, and PASS on 23 
explicitly enumerated positive rational monomial-weight cases. It records the normalized contacts and the exact cancellation and 
singular-support values above in contact-output.json. The polyhedral and semivaluation arguments above are mathematical proofs; the program 
checks only this finite certificate. Rerun: python contact\_certificate.py. Inputs, source and full output are in contact-input.json, 
contact\_certificate.py and contact-output.json; no supplied program is executed or imported.

\subsection{A mixed-characteristic normal nonisolated example}

The general theorem in n1 also yields an explicit sector outside equicharacteristic field germs. Fix any prime p, take V=Z\_p with 
uniformizer pi=p, and put
\[
 R_V=V[[a,b,c,d]]/(ad-bc),\quad \mathfrak n=(\pi,a,b,c,d),\quad
 K_V=(a+b,c+d,\pi)+\mathfrak n^2.                         \tag{11}
\]
This is a complete excellent normal domain of dimension four with a singular line (a,b,c,d). Here are explicit checks, so no general 
mixed-characteristic positivity theorem is assumed. The standard monomials after replacing ad by bc form a V-basis, also after completion 
degree by degree. The parametrization a=xy,b=xw,c=ty,d=tw in V[[x,y,t,w]] identifies distinct standard monomials with distinct exponent 
vectors. Thus the quotient is a domain. It is a hypersurface in a regular local ring, so is S2. At a prime not containing all four a,b,c,d, 
a partial derivative d,-c,-b or a is a unit. In the regular ambient localization the defining equation is outside the square of the maximal 
ideal (apply that derivation), so the quotient localization is regular. The ideal (a,b,c,d) has height three, by the catenary hypersurface 
dimension formula and quotient V. Every height-one localization is regular, and Serre's R1+S2 criterion proves normality. At the generic 
point of that line the quadric has embedding dimension four and dimension three, hence is singular. These CM/S2 facts check this SPECIFIC 
hypersurface; they are not imposed on the general theorem or formal audit.

The n-adic graded ring is exactly
\[
 \operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak n}(R_V)
   =\mathbf F_p[\Pi,A,B,C,D]/(AD-BC),                       \tag{12}
\]
a domain. The regular ambient ring has polynomial associated graded ring. For any h there, ord(h(ad-bc))=ord(h)+2, because its associated 
graded ring is a domain. Its initial form is in(h)(AD-BC). Thus the initial ideal of the principal relation is precisely (AD-BC), with no 
extra initial relation. The quotient polynomial ring is a domain by the same monomial parametrization. Consequently nu=ord\_n is a 
valuation, not merely a subadditive order, and nu(n)=1.

For EVERY centred semivaluation v with v(n)=1, membership f in n\textasciicircum{}r gives v(f)>=r, so v(f)>=nu(f). Selecting an element of 
least finite v-value in a primary ideal I gives v(I)>=nu(I). Every negative rational or real primary profile g therefore satisfies 
g(v)<=g(nu). Uniform limits and the ACTUAL infima defining D preserve this inequality. This is a one-point contact certificate at nu, proved
 directly; no count of normalized-blowup components is needed.

K\_V is proper primary and n\textasciicircum{}2 subset K\_V subset n. Since a+b has order one, nu(K\_V)=1. For any delta>=0 the finite 
continuous obstacle
\[
 F_\delta=-v(\mathfrak n)+\delta\big(v(K_V)-v(\mathfrak n)\big)           \tag{13}
\]
is at least -1 and equals -1 at nu. Every D competitor below it is at most -1 at nu, hence everywhere. The primary profile -v(n) is itself a
 geometric competitor, proving
\[
 P(F_\delta)=-v(\mathfrak n)=-1
\]
on the entire normalized boundary. For delta=1/2, (13) is (v(K\_V)-v(n\textasciicircum{}3))/2, an actual rational signed primary/model 
obstacle on the product primary blowup. Its greatest geometric envelope is actual nef Cartier. Since v(K\_V)<=2, this obstacle lies in 
[-1,-1/2].

It is cancellation-sensitive even with the uniformizer weight retained. Map a=c=r,b=d=r(h-1) into V[[r,h]] and use the weighted valuation 
with pi,r,h weights 3,1,1. For a formal series sum c\_ij r\textasciicircum{}i h\textasciicircum{}j its value is min(3 ord\_pi(c\_ij)+i+j); 
its associated graded coefficient/monomial ring over F\_p is a domain, proving multiplicativity. Pullback is centred, with prime support 
(c-a,d-b) strictly below n, and
\[
 v(\pi,a,b,c,d)=(3,1,1,1,1),\qquad v(K_V)=2.
\]
The matching monomial valuation on R\_V has the same generator and uniformizer weights but K\_V value one. It exists by the standard 
monomial expansion over V, with value 3 ord\_pi(coefficient)+total monomial degree. Its associated graded ring is the domain monoid algebra 
over F\_p with a uniformizer variable, so distinct monomials cannot cancel. Thus F\_(1/2) has values -1/2 and -1 at these equal-weight 
semivaluations. The supported valuation killing (a,b,c,d) and giving pi value one has K\_V value one and envelope -1, even though the ideal 
(a,b,c,d) has infinite value. Every support is retained.

This is an unconditional mixed-characteristic excellent normal nonisolated obstacle sector relative to G331. It is not arbitrary-obstacle 
mixed-characteristic CE. The proofs above establish its universal statements. The own finite program checks only the equicharacteristic 
Newton instance and is not a p-adic ring computation.


\section{n3. Exact gauges, compatible normalization contacts, and geometric curve clipping}

Support: incoming qualified G331 and earlier own n1,n2. No B341/E350 product or energy result is used.

The contact theorem of n1 applies to every excellent germ and is homogeneous on rays. If b is another primary gauge, write d(v)=v(b) on 
V\_a, T(v)=v/d(v), and transport obstacle, barrier and contacts by
\[
 f_b(Tv)=f_a(v)/d(v),\quad H_b(Tv)=H_a(v)/d(v),\quad x_{j,b}=T(x_{j,a}).
\]
The positive bounded continuous denominator preserves inequalities, contact equalities, uniform convergence and actual decreasing 
representations. G331 gives precisely this bijection of C,D competitors. Taking their suprema proves the exact envelope rule
\[
 P_b(f_b)(Tv)=P_a(f_a)(v)/d(v).
\]
Substitution supplies the exact three-primary-gauge cocycle. The contact normals remain centred under every primary section; the barrier 
remains -v(J)/q in the new section. Completion transport is the already granted all-support homeomorphism and exact primary contraction, not
 a new algebraization or equivalence of geometric model categories.

Here is a full-fibre normalization extension of the new contact sector, which does not assume general CE upstairs. Let R be any excellent 
reduced germ with finite normalization S, and suppose each positive-dimensional normal local centre S\_i is of the saturated monoid type of 
n1. Take barriers H\_i=-v(J\_i)/q\_i as in n1, or the zero barrier. Require their tuple H to be constant on EVERY restriction fibre of 
rho:X\_S->X\_R. Qualified G331 positively descends the continuous tuple to h in C\_R. Let f be any finite continuous obstacle on X\_R such 
that f>=h, and for every nonzero barrier's finite contact x\_\{ij\} require
\[
 f(\rho(x_{ij}))=H_i(x_{ij}).
\]
For a D\_R competitor u<=f, its pullback on each nonzero branch is at most H\_i by n1. On a zero-barrier branch its nonpositivity gives the 
same inequality. Thus u<=h by surjectivity of rho, while h is itself a competitor. Its greatest D\_R envelope is h. The same statement holds
 for a bounded-above extended upper semicontinuous obstacle satisfying these bounds and contacts. A contact condition at one source point 
never replaces the imposed FULL-fibre compatibility of H.

Specifically, if c is the conductor, G331 identifies a fibre as a singleton when v(c)<infinity. When v(c)=infinity, lifts kill c and 
equality of their restrictions through S/c -> R/c is exactly the identification rule. The finite-value locus is open, the infinite-value 
locus closed. Both are retained in the contact argument. No value v(c)/m is used as a uniform error. Compatibility includes all branches, 
nonminimal supports, mixed-zero and partial-bottom patterns. This theorem does not assert that an incompatible tuple of source envelopes 
descends positively or that an arbitrary fibre maximum is psh.

On EVERY excellent reduced curve, normalization has the finite collection of DVR local centres over the closed point, including multiple 
branches on one irreducible component. A regular conductor element has finite order on every branch, so normalized boundary fibres are 
singleton. On each DVR the marked point is an actual effective Cartier divisor and there are no contracted integral curves to test. All 
finite nonpositive coordinates are independently geometric there; G331's positive full-fibre continuous descent gives all finite nonpositive
 branch vectors downstairs. For an extended nonpositive vector u, max(u,-j) is an actual decreasing sequence of these C vectors with infimum
 u. Thus D is exactly every extended nonpositive branch vector. For any branch obstacle phi its greatest geometric D minorant is min(phi,0).
 This is the exact complete ideal-envelope comparison by G331's independently proved cone comparison. The branch coordinate for two primary 
gauges rescales by ord\_i(a)/ord\_i(b), with the exact cocycle above.

Nilpotents remain invisible and are removed by reduction; if the local reduction has dimension zero the centred boundary is empty and 
statements concern its unique empty function. Literal classical or CLD logarithmic radial extension classes are not changed: their stated 
multibranch mixed-zero obstruction remains. The boundary class may contain (-1,0) without such a literal radial extension. At a smooth 
affine CLOSED germ over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, G331 identifies this exact C,D class with the full published BFJ 
all-semivaluation class, with bottom adjoined. Wherever our contact theorem applies at that specialization, its greatest minorant is 
therefore the BFJ envelope in the SAME class. This does not extend BFJ's published hypotheses to arbitrary smooth excellent, imperfect or 
mixed-characteristic germs. Dimension-one and empty cases above are direct.

Artifacts: n3.md, proof-companion.md and P12.3-contact-envelopes.tex, retaining the full incoming G331 proof/annotation/ledger. Rerun 
delivery and data checks: python prepare\_delivery.py. This scope leaves P12.4 products, P12.5 energy and P12.6 full operator theory 
separate.


\section{n4. Current401 audit, formal reconstruction boundary, and unchanged original residual}

The following is my independent reconstruction of the active formal chain and the limits of the present audit. It concerns complete normal

Completed algebra: for a finite complete local k-module V, continuous duality gives V=(V\textasciicircum{}o)\textasciicircum{}*, with

completed-tensor\_k W=(V\textasciicircum{}o tensor\_k W\textasciicircum{}o)\textasciicircum{}* proves exactness in both slots. Applying

\[
 \operatorname{Hom}_{R\widehat\otimes_k R}(M\widehat\otimes_k N,R\widehat\otimes_k R)
 =\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)\widehat\otimes_k\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,R).

Paired generators generate every map; individual maps need not be decomposable. Perfect coefficients and exponent grouping identify the root

Different/lift: for a fixed k-parameter normalization A, the adjugate of a square matrix of differences of the presentation equations

 dw=\sum_i r_i\operatorname{Tr}(s_iw)

base changes through the linearly disjoint purely inseparable K\textasciicircum{}(1/q)/K. For w in R\textasciicircum{}(1/q), trace

because its generic multiplication is injective and A\textasciicircum{}(1/q) tensor\_A R is an R-free torsion-free module. It does not make

For T=R\textasciicircum{}(1/q), lift multiplication from the B-free module P\_q completed-tensor T through B=R completed-tensor T -> T. 
Compose with ROOT multiplication d on the first T and 1 completed-tensor phi on the target. After multiplication into R its value is

 The latter is the historical immutable false paragraph, not the corrected401 formula. A concrete check in k[[x]], q=3, phi selecting

The fixed-common-field sum of relative Jacobian ideals is exactly Wang's formal Jacobian, not an unrestricted choice of normalization 
fields. At finite residue field one can preserve each generator's cotangent coset by adding elements of m\textasciicircum{}2 avoiding a

Wang's immediate statement/proof and Liu's exact reduced-equidimensional perfect-residue criterion were read. The common-field sum supplies

BIG minimum: for a reduced excellent F-finite B, a Cartier algebra C that becomes full on regular B\_c, and pair ideals that become unit 
there, every stable ideal H containing a regular element has H\_c=B\_c. Locally on B\_c, finite free Frobenius and Krull intersection make

 n\le B_0+a+\lceil n/q\rceil\le B_0+a+1+n/q.

Hence a single c\textasciicircum{}L lies in EVERY such H. Their intersection is an actual generically nonzero stable minimum, not a

 \operatorname{Jac}(R)\tau_R(a^t b^s)
 \subset\tau_D(a^t b^s)

Iteration has Jacobian power ell-1 on the left. Only isolatedness replaces it by a PRIMARY correction uniformly on the whole link.

Isolated model chain: perfect exponent grouping makes ORDINARY Omega\_(R/k) finite. Finite-type model rings are F-finite with finite

Blowing up Fitt\_1(omega), discarding actual chart torsion, and using Fitt\_1=unit, Fitt\_0=0 produces a rank-one strict-transform line

compatibility rule throughout the stated disc-normalized curve range. The ordinary multinode
theorem Book Theorem 70.1.10 records the explicit coordinate-ring instance. At the oppo-

trace comparison exists, or treat a singular germ outside this normalization-and-conductor
range.
    There is a genuine, but diﬀerent, global boundary case. Over an algebraically closed
ﬁeld of characteristic zero, the global trivially-valued framework used in [BJ23, §2] treats an
integral projective variety without initially assuming normality: it supplies a global psh class,

records in the smooth case. This global construction neither selects a normalized link for an
excellent local germ nor supplies the curve-local conductor realization above, local bounded
products, or the required local ﬁnite-map formula. It therefore does not discharge any part
of Problem 6.1.

ties, and purely inseparable universal homeomorphisms. Any claim of independence of psh
or intersection constructions from boundary choices must respect the established radial com-
parison and conductor quotient. Relative b-divisors can be deﬁned on suitable model sys-

and intersection-theoretic package is presently open.
    Two older local-volume questions should not be carried forward as open. For the
Boucksom–de Fernex–Favre local volume, Yuchen Zhang proves a positive dimension-
dependent lower bound for every nonzero volume of an isolated Gorenstein singularity and

For finite continuous f on the compact primary section X, define p(f)=sup\{u in D:u<=f\}. A sufficiently negative primary constant is a 
competitor. If g\_i decreases in C to u<=f, the open sets \{g\_i<f+epsilon\} cover X. Compactness and directedness select one term 
satisfying the inequality everywhere. Its negative constant shift g\_i-epsilon is in C and below f, and is at least u-epsilon. Therefore C 
and D give the same raw supremum. It is finite, bounded, lower semicontinuous and nonexpansive in the uniform norm. Negative shifts in both 
directions prove the latter; no positive-translation invariance is used.

If p(f) is continuous, finitely many continuous competitors and their maximum approximate it uniformly from below, so p(f) belongs to C. If 
p(f) belongs to D, upper semicontinuity plus the preceding lower semicontinuity makes it continuous. Any maximal D minorant is greatest,

\section{n2. Corrected completed free lift and full root kernel}

All statements here are reconstructed; neither corrected396 nor ROOT392 is a grant. Let R be a complete normal local domain of

Here is the exactness argument needed for these completed tensors. A finite module V over R is the inverse limit of its finite-dimensional k
 quotients; its continuous dual V\textasciicircum{}o is their direct-limit dual. Artin--Rees makes a finite submodule's induced topology 
cofinal with its adic topology. A continuous functional on a submodule extends through a sufficiently deep finite quotient. Thus continuous 
duality is exact on the relevant finite-module sequences. Algebraic vector-space tensor and duality are exact, and
\[
 V\widehat\otimes_k W=(V^o\otimes_k W^o)^*.
\]
This proves completed exactness in either slot. It does not appeal to completion over an uncompleted non-Noetherian tensor ring. Applied 
twice to R->R\textasciicircum{}(1/p), it makes S->S\textasciicircum{}(1/p) injective. This is the Frobenius map under the root presentation,
 so S is reduced.

Present finite R modules M,N by finite free modules. In S\textasciicircum{}(ab), impose the M-relation matrix, then the N-relation matrix. 
Completed exactness identifies the first kernel with Hom\_R(M,R) completed-tensor R\textasciicircum{}b and the second with the corresponding
 completed tensor of Hom modules. Therefore
\[
\operatorname{Hom}_S(M\widehat\otimes_k N,S)
=\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)\widehat\otimes_k\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,R).
\]
This is the full Hom factorization, including finite ideals/twists and every S Cartier map. Finite paired generators generate the right-hand

If a regular Noetherian subring A makes R module finite, integral locality makes A local. Its maximal-adic and R maximal-adic topologies on 
R are cofinal. Exact completion embeds A-hat in R, so A-hat/A is a finite A module, with zero residue quotient. Nakayama gives A=A-hat. The 
residue field F has finite extension k; perfection of k and [k:F]=[k\textasciicircum{}p:F\textasciicircum{}p] force F perfect. Cohen 
structure then gives A=F[[x]], whose roots are finite free. This broader ROOT392 claim is valid, but the Jacobian sum below uses only the 
fixed common field k.

Fix A=k[[x\_1,...,x\_d]] inside R, finite over A. Let K\_A=Fitt\_0 Omega\_(R/A) and N\_A=mu\_A(Ann ker(mu\_A)) in R tensor\_A R. A finite

For K\_A nonzero the fraction field extension L/K is separable. If d in N\_A, choose z=sum r\_i tensor s\_i annihilating the diagonal with 
product d. Over L tensor\_K L, z is d times the separability idempotent. The trace in the second slot gives
\[
d w=\sum_i r_i\operatorname{Tr}(s_i w).
\]
The purely inseparable extension K\textasciicircum{}(1/q)/K is linearly disjoint from L/K, and L 
K\textasciicircum{}(1/q)=L\textasciicircum{}(1/q). The same identity holds there. Elements of R\textasciicircum{}(1/q) are integral over 
A\textasciicircum{}(1/q), so their trace coefficients are integral and in its fraction field. Normality of the regular 
A\textasciicircum{}(1/q) puts them in A\textasciicircum{}(1/q). Consequently dT subset A\textasciicircum{}(1/q)[R]. The multiplication of

 is torsion-free over A. Thus P is the indicated submodule of T and is finite free over R. Freeness of R over A is not asserted.

Set B=R completed-tensor\_k T. The multiplication B->T is surjective and B-linear. The module P completed-tensor\_k T is free over B, so its
 multiplication into T lifts to a B-linear map Psi into B, by lifting its finite free basis. Compose
\[
T\widehat\otimes_k T\xrightarrow{,d\otimes1,}
P\widehat\otimes_k T\xrightarrow{\Psi}

\]
for any R-linear phi:T->R. This is S-linear with the Frobenius root source action. On pure tensors, applying mu gives phi(dxy)=d phi(xy). 
Finite-module continuity extends this equality to the completed tensor. Its reduction therefore factors through the surjective root

Multiplication by d\textasciicircum{}q in T would instead induce d\textasciicircum{}q phi, the immutable error demonstrated in n1. No claim

\section{n3. BIG minima, late tails, and the actual completed diagonal}

Use the completed module and lift theorem of n2, not a grant from396. Let B be reduced excellent Noetherian F-finite. Let C be a Cartier 
subalgebra with finite degree modules and C\_0=B. Assume c in B\textasciicircum{}o has B\_c regular, all C\_e become the full Hom modules 
there, and finitely many regular-element pair ideals a\_i become units there. These explicit regular-open hypotheses will be verified for 
the product and diagonal; no graded finite generation is presumed. Put r\_i(e)=ceil(t\_i(p\textasciicircum{}e-1)). Stability means that all 
maps in C\_e take F\_*\textasciicircum{}e((product a\_i\textasciicircum{}r\_i(e))H) into H. The twisted maps compose because 
r\_i(e)+p\textasciicircum{}e r\_i(f)>=r\_i(e+f).

Every stable H meeting B\textasciicircum{}o has H\_c=B\_c. At a regular maximal localization of B\_c, F-finiteness and Kunz give a finite 
free Frobenius module. A regular h in H is outside n\textasciicircum{}[q] for large q, since n\textasciicircum{}[q] subset 
n\textasciicircum{}q and Krull intersection. Thus F\_*h is primitive in that free module and a linear map sends it to1. Hom localization 
holds by finite presentation; localized stability gives the unit ideal. This holds at every maximal localization. Kunz is the named ordinary
 theorem at exactly regular Noetherian characteristic-p rings; its full statement in Smolkinv3 2.3 was read, not its entire original 
historical proof.

There is one universal power of c in EVERY such H. Choose a positive degree q. Evaluation at1 splits on B\_c; clear denominators to obtain 
theta in C\_e with theta(F\_*1)=c\textasciicircum{}a. Choose B\_0 so c\textasciicircum{}(q B\_0) belongs to that degree's pair coefficient 
ideal. For the least n with c\textasciicircum{}n in H, stability and the Frobenius scalar rule give c\textasciicircum{}(B\_0+ceil(n/q)+a) in
 H. Therefore
\[
n\le B_0+a+\lceil n/q\rceil\le B_0+a+n/q+1,
\qquad n\le\frac{q(B_0+a+1)}{q-1}.
\]
Fix an integer L at least this bound. The intersection of all stable ideals meeting B\textasciicircum{}o is stable and contains 
c\textasciicircum{}L in B\textasciicircum{}o, so it is the actual smallest such ideal tau. This is BIG, not finitistic. The ideal generated 
by all twisted maps of an arbitrary regular d, with degree zero included, is stable and generically nonzero, and therefore contains 
c\textasciicircum{}L. Thus the construction supplies the required universal BIG test element, rather than assuming arbitrary-Cartier-algebra
 existence.

If d belongs to tau intersect B\textasciicircum{}o, every late tail generated by twisted images of dB lies in tau. Composition shows the 
tail is stable. On B\_c the pair ideals are units; for each maximal localization a sufficiently large degree sends the regular d to1 by the 
preceding primitive-vector argument. Hence the tail is generically nonzero and minimality makes it equal tau. This holds for EVERY cutoff E,
 not merely for all degrees starting at0.

Both exponent conventions ceil(t\_i q) and ceil(t\_i(q-1)) give the same ideal and all their late tails. Their gaps are bounded by 
ceil(t\_i)+1 independently of e. Construct the minima for both conventions by the same argument and choose a common regular seed in their 
intersection. Multiplication by a fixed regular element of product a\_i\textasciicircum{}(ceil(t\_i)+1) is enough to bridge the bounded 
gaps. Since a seed in tau can be multiplied by a regular element and remains a seed, the two tail sums sandwich each other. The same 
argument proves power invariance tau((a\textasciicircum{}r)\textasciicircum{}(t/r))=tau(a\textasciicircum{}t): the exponents ceil(qt) and r 
ceil(qt/r) differ by at most r-1. No finite-tail approximation or Q-Gorenstein index enters.

Localization of these ideals follows from finite Hom localization and shared nonzero seeds. Full-algebra completion is also exact for 
excellent F-finite normal local A: the m-adic and Frobenius filtrations are cofinal, so F\_*A completes to F\_*(A-hat), and finite Hom 
commutes with faithful flat completion. Extending tau\_A is stable, giving tau\_hat subset tau\_A A-hat. Choose c in A with A\_c regular and
 pair ideals unit. Regular formal fibres make A-hat\_c regular; the same cleared splitting supplies a common c\textasciicircum{}L in 
tau\_hat. Its contraction is nonzero and stable, giving the reverse inclusion. An arbitrary nonzero formal ideal is never assumed to have 
nonzero contraction. This proves the completion rule for full algebras only.

If J C\_e subset D\_e, the correct comparison is J tau\_C subset tau\_D. Choose a regular seed in both minima. The C late-tail formula 
expresses tau\_C; multiplying each output by J turns the map into a D map, whose image of the common seed lies in tau\_D. This proves the 
comparison without claiming J tau\_C is itself D-stable.

Return to n2's S. It is reduced F-finite and equidimensional of dimension2d. Indeed a parameter ring A\_0=k[[x\_1,...,x\_d]] makes R finite 
torsion-free. Clear denominators of a generic basis to embed R in a finite free A\_0 module. Completed exactness embeds S in a free module 
over k[[x,y]]. Every minimal prime of this finite torsion-free algebra contracts to0, so all minimal quotients have dimension2d. A nonzero 
d-codimensional Jacobian minor j of R yields the block minor j(u)j(v) in Jac(S). At the diagonal prime I its image is j\textasciicircum{}2, 
nonzero in R. The exact reduced-equidimensional perfect-residue singular-locus criterion of n2 makes S\_I regular. No S normality or 
product-domain assertion is needed.

Choose regular a\_0 in a and b\_0 in b and set c\_S=j(u)j(v)(a\_0 tensor b\_0). Completed exactness makes multiplication by a\_0 and b\_0 
injective in their slots, and similarly for j; thus c\_S is regular. Its diagonal image j\textasciicircum{}2 a\_0 b\_0 is nonzero. On S\_cS 
the ring is regular and both pair ideals A=aS, B=bS are units. For R's diagonal algebra D, n2 gives j C\_e subset D\_e, so localization at j

Let T\_S=tau\_S(A\textasciicircum{}t B\textasciicircum{}s). Its image mu(T\_S) is D-stable: compatible lifts carry its coefficient-twisted 
roots into T\_S, and passage to the quotient gives the required maps. Its image is nonzero because it contains mu(c\_S\textasciicircum{}L). 
Minimality therefore gives tau\_D(a\textasciicircum{}t b\textasciicircum{}s) subset mu(T\_S).

The completed product of tau\_R(a\textasciicircum{}t) and tau\_R(b\textasciicircum{}s), extended into S, is stable for EVERY full S Cartier 
map by n2's full Hom factorization and stability in each factor. It contains a regular pure tensor, again by completed exactness, so T\_S 
lies in this product ideal. Multiplication sends it to tau\_R(a\textasciicircum{}t) tau\_R(b\textasciicircum{}s). Combining the common-seed 
comparison with these two inclusions gives
\[
\operatorname{Jac}(R)\tau_R(a^t b^s)
\subset\tau_D(a^t b^s)
\subset\mu(T_S)
\subset\tau_R(a^t)\tau_R(b^s).
\]
Iteration yields Jac\textasciicircum{}(ell-1) tau(a\textasciicircum{}(ell t)) subset tau(a\textasciicircum{}t)\textasciicircum{}ell. This is
 the corrected direction. A primary multiplier is obtained only under isolatedness; no finite value of a nonprimary Jacobian on every 
support is inferred.

Verdict: the complete formal BIG/subadditivity gate is discharged for complete normal characteristic-p perfect-residue R, with no

\section{n4. Entire isolated formal envelope chain and scoped verdict}

Use n1--n3 and the full qualified G331. Let R be complete normal local, characteristic p>0, perfect residue, isolated singularity, dimension
 d>=2. This note reconstructs the entire model/trace/primary approximation chain. In dimension1 R is a DVR; dimension0 has empty boundary. 
No algebraizability, CM, Q-Gorenstein or resolution is assumed.

First justify model transfer. Exponent grouping in R over R\textasciicircum{}p makes ordinary Omega\_(R/k) finite: every element is a finite
 sum b\_i\textasciicircum{}p u\textasciicircum{}i and every k-derivation kills the pth powers and the perfect field. This agrees with

\section{n5. New positive sector: all monomial-weight obstacles on complete normal toric germs}

Use G331 and the raw-envelope/nonexpansivity/decreasing-closure results proved in n1. This is new scoped progress on the original envelope 
target, valid over ANY field, including imperfect fields and every characteristic. It concerns actual geometric positivity and all geometric
 competitors, not a new order definition or a restriction to radial functions on a finite link.

Let M be a lattice of rank d, C\_0 a pointed full-dimensional rational polyhedral cone in M\_R, and S=C\_0 intersect M its saturated 
positive monoid. Let R be the completion at the monomial maximal ideal of k[S]. For precision, k[S] is the intersection, in its fraction 
field, of the normal Laurent polynomial ring k[M] with the valuation rings given by the finitely many primitive facet weights. On a Laurent 
polynomial the least facet weight is the least term weight, so these inequalities mean that every exponent belongs to C\_0 intersect M. This
 proves the asserted intersection and hence normality. Finite generation is the elementary rational-cone lattice-point theorem. The 
finite-type ring is excellent, and excellent normal completion is normal; thus R is an excellent normal local domain. Its elements are 
formal sums of monomials chi\textasciicircum{}u, with the maximal-adic completion topology. Fix a monomial primary gauge a. G331 supplies 
its full all-support compact boundary X and independently geometric C,D. These conventional algebraic foundations are used at this exact 
saturated positive affine-monoid setup; no perfect-field base change or torus averaging is used.

The monomial weight of v is w\_v(u)=v(chi\textasciicircum{}u). It is additive, may take infinity, and is strictly positive on nonzero monoid
 elements when finite. The finite-valued elements form a face of S. For finite weights w in the interior of the dual cone 
sigma=C\_0\textasciicircum{}vee, taking the least weight of the terms defines a monomial valuation v\_w on the completed ring. Positivity 
makes the least value well-defined and makes the operation compatible with the completion. Distinct monomials in its associated graded 
cannot cancel. Divide by w(a) to obtain its primary-section point.

Every extended monomial weight arising from v is a limit of these finite interior weights, after normalization. Indeed its finite face is 
cut out by a rational exposing functional lambda>=0, zero on that face and strictly positive on its complement. Extend its finite additive 
weight linearly from the face span to M\_R. Add N lambda, and if necessary a vanishing small positive interior functional. For large N the 
finitely many monoid generators outside the face become positive, and the generators inside the face have their given positive values. The 
outside values tend to infinity. Some primary-gauge generator has finite value; hence normalized primary values converge as well. Monomial 
primary profiles are continuous on all X by G331. Thus inequalities between such profiles and signed monomial obstacles, checked on finite 
interior weights, hold on every extended monomial weight and hence on EVERY semivaluation having that weight.

For any ideal I of R, let M(I) be the monomial ideal generated by all monomials appearing with nonzero coefficient in a finite set of formal
 generators. Noetherianity makes this ideal finitely generated. A monomial ideal is maximal-adically closed, since its finite-module 
quotient is separated; therefore each series whose terms lie in it belongs to it. Hence I subset M(I). If I contains a primary power then so
 does M(I). At a finite interior monomial valuation, v\_w(I)=v\_w(M(I)): the least appearing monomial realizes the value and cannot cancel. 
At a general semivaluation, -v(M(I))>=-v(I). This is a domination of arbitrary ideal profiles, proved by term membership, not by an 
averaging operation over k-rational torus points.

Consider a rational signed monomial primary obstacle on rays,
\[
F(w)=\frac{w(A)-w(B)}r,
\]
where A,B are monomial unit-or-primary ideals and r is a positive integer. Finite lattice combinations are of this form by synchronized 
products and sums. On X its restriction f is finite continuous. Write phi=-F, a homogeneous rational piecewise-linear function on sigma. 
Common normal fans of the finite exponent sets of A and B make phi linear on finitely many rational cones. Define
\[
P=\{x\in C_0:\langle x,w\rangle\ge\phi(w)\text{ for all }w\in\sigma\}.
\]
These conditions reduce to the finitely many rays of that fan, together with the cone inequalities. Thus P is a rational polyhedron. Because
 |f| is bounded on the a-section, phi(w)<=T w(a) for a finite T. Therefore P contains T times the Newton polyhedron of a and is nonempty. 
Its recession cone is exactly C\_0. The finite polyhedral vertex/recession decomposition, obtained by successively moving a nonvertex to 
bounding faces, gives P=conv(x\_1,...,x\_h)+C\_0, with rational vertices. Pointedness rules out a lineality factor.

Clear denominators with q so q x\_i belong to M and hence S. Add sufficiently large powers of EACH monoid generator to the ideal generated 
by chi\textasciicircum{}(q x\_i). These added exponents can be chosen inside qP: for a fan ray w with w(u)=0 on a nonzero monoid generator 
u, primaryness implies w(a)=0 and hence phi(w)=0. All remaining finite inequalities are met by a sufficiently large multiple of u. Call the 
resulting monomial ideal J. Its radical is the maximal ideal, unless P contains0, in which case include1 and use the unit ideal. Adding 
these points does not change its Newton polyhedron, which is qP. Thus
\[
h(w):=\min_{x\in P}\langle x,w\rangle=w(J)/q,
\qquad -h\le F
\]
for finite weights, and the preceding extended-weight continuity proves -v(J)/q<=f on ALL supports. This is an actual primary ideal profile 
and hence an actual negative effective curve-nef Cartier presentation on Bl\_J R by G331's independently proved geometric comparison/core 
inclusion.

It is the raw envelope among ALL geometric competitors. For any rational arbitrary-ideal profile -v(I)/l<=f, equality at monomial valuations
 shows -v(M(I))/l<=f there and hence everywhere, while this monomialized profile dominates the original. Each generating exponent u of M(I) 
satisfies u/l in P, so w(M(I))/l>=h(w); the same domination holds at extended weights by continuity. Consequently -v(I)/l<=-v(J)/q at every 
semivaluation. To handle C competitors, approximate by rational primary profiles, then make a negative rational gauge shift to keep them 
below f. Their errors vanish. N1 identifies the C and D raw suprema. Therefore
\[
p(f)=-v(J)/q\in C_{\rm geom}
\]
and this is the greatest D minorant. This controls arbitrary nonmonomial ideal profiles, their real uniform limits, and completed D 
competitors; it is not merely a toric-restricted supremum. The formula gives a finite rational polyhedral construction for every rational 
signed monomial model obstacle.

Let W be the compact image of X under all monomial evaluations. Primary monomial profile differences contain rational constants, form a 
lattice by products and ideal sums, and separate W using (chi\textasciicircum{}u)+a\textasciicircum{}N, whose value is min(w(u),N). The 
compact lattice approximation proof therefore makes their rational span uniformly dense in C(W). For every finite continuous obstacle f=F\_0
 composed with the weight map, choose such rational signed obstacles tending uniformly to it. N1 nonexpansivity makes their raw envelopes 
uniformly Cauchy. Their limit is p(f), belongs to C\_geom, and is weight-dependent. Thus EVERY finite continuous monomial-weight obstacle 
has an actually positive continuous envelope, not just the rational ones.

For a bounded-above extended upper semicontinuous obstacle on W, take all finite continuous nonpositive majorants of its clipping to0, 
directed by minima. Their envelopes are in C\_geom by the preceding theorem and form one decreasing net. N1 decreasing closure shows its 
infimum is in D\_geom; it is below the obstacle and dominates every D competitor. This gives its greatest D envelope, with the appropriate 
upper semicontinuity, poles/bottom, and decreasing-obstacle-net stability for specified upper semicontinuous limits. The ray formulation and
 n1 give the exact gauge cocycle for ANY primary section; changing a monomial gauge is the immediate weight-coordinate formula. At these 
normal germs normalization is the identity and conductor fibres are singletons. No nonnormal monomial descent theorem is asserted.

This includes normal nonisolated toric germs of arbitrary dimension and monomial-weight obstacles over imperfect residue fields. For example
 k[[s\textasciicircum{}2,st,t\textasciicircum{}2,z]] has a nonisolated singular line in dimension3. The nonsimplicial rank3 saturated cone 
generated by (1,0,0),(1,1,0),(1,0,1),(1,1,1) gives k[[a,b,c,d]]/(ad-bc); adding formal monomial variables gives nonisolated examples. The 
theorem does NOT prove CE for arbitrary obstacles that distinguish valuations with the same monomial values, or for arbitrary excellent 
germs. Its smooth specialization uses the same G331 cone; in the published smooth affine closed/algebraically closed/characteristic-zero 
range it is the restriction of the BFJ envelope, because both are greatest minorants of that identical class. This does not extend BFJ's 
published hypotheses or identify literal analytic/CLD radial extensions.

computations, not a proof of the universal theorem. Rerun: python toric\_envelope.py. No supplied code, solver, compiler, field extension,

\section{n6. New normal nonisolated obstruction to a universal primary correction}

Use the explicit BIG convention in n3 and the toric setup of n5 only at its stated scope. The calculation below proves its all-map 
test-ideal formula independently; no toric test-ideal formula or finite-map operator is imported. Let k be perfect of odd characteristic p, 
and
\[
R=k[[U,V,W,z]]/(UW-V^2)=k[[s^2,st,t^2,z]],
\quad B=k[[s,t,z]],\quad P=(U,V,W).
\]
R is an excellent normal three-dimensional domain, and its singular locus is the formal line P. This follows from the saturated monoid or 
the hypersurface and its codimension-two Jacobian locus. Write monomials as chi\textasciicircum{}m=s\textasciicircum{}a t\textasciicircum{}b
 z\textasciicircum{}c, with m in M=\{(a,b,c) in Z\textasciicircum{}3:a+b even\}, all coordinates nonnegative. For N>=1 set 
A\_N=(U,W\textasciicircum{}N,z\textasciicircum{}N), a genuine primary ideal, and
\[
w_N(a,b,c)=a/2+b/(2N)+c/N,\qquad
H_{N,t}=\langle\chi^m:w_N(m+(1,1,1))>t\rangle.
\]
We claim tau\_R(A\_N\textasciicircum{}t)=H\_(N,t) for every real t>=0, using stability exponents ceil(t(q-1)).

First every R Cartier map extends to a B Cartier map. The fraction field extension L/K is separable quadratic; purely inseparable root 
extension gives L tensor\_K K\textasciicircum{}(1/q)=L\textasciicircum{}(1/q). Hence an R-linear phi extends uniquely to an L-linear map on 
L\textasciicircum{}(1/q). Outside (s,t) the finite cover is etale: where s is invertible, B is given by S\textasciicircum{}2=U with 
derivative2S a unit, and similarly for t. Frobenius root base change on this chart is explicit, since s\textasciicircum{}(1/q)=s 
(U\textasciicircum{}(1/q))\textasciicircum{}(-(q-1)/2), with t=V/s; the t-chart is analogous. Thus the extended map carries the root module 
into B at every height-one localization. Since B\textasciicircum{}(1/q) is finite free and B is normal, the 
intersection-of-height-one-localizations criterion makes all its coefficients integral globally. The extension is an actual B-linear map 
B\textasciicircum{}(1/q)->B. Codimension-two etaleness and normality, not a general trace theorem, justify this step.

In the regular ring B, the root monomials with residues0,...,q-1 in each coordinate form a free basis. For any monomial 
chi\textasciicircum{}h in a source and any output monomial chi\textasciicircum{}n of any B Cartier map, these basis expansions give
\[
q n_i+(q-1)\ge h_i\quad(i=1,2,3).
\]
The map coefficients are power series with nonnegative exponents. Thus cancellation can only remove possible output monomials. If 
chi\textasciicircum{}h is in A\_N\textasciicircum{}r H\_(N,t), r=ceil(t(q-1)), then w\_N(h)+w\_N(1,1,1)>r+t. The displayed coordinate bound 
gives
\[
q w_N(n+(1,1,1))\ge w_N(h)+w_N(1,1,1)>r+t\ge qt.
\]
H\_(N,t) is therefore stable under every extended B map and hence EVERY R map. Monomial ideals are adically closed, so this calculation 
handles formal series as well as polynomial monomials. It is nonzero, indeed contains sufficiently high primary powers.

To prove minimality, let K be any generically nonzero stable ideal. Invert c=UW. The ring becomes regular and A\_N becomes unit. Finite Hom 
localization and the primitive-vector Frobenius argument of n3 give K\_c=R\_c. Hence d=(UW)\textasciicircum{}L belongs to K for some integer
 L. For a target m=(a,b,c\_0) satisfying w\_N(m+1)>t, choose q=p\textasciicircum{}e large and r=ceil(t(q-1)). The three capacities
\[
\left\lfloor\frac{q(a+1)-2L-1}{2}\right\rfloor,
\quad\left\lfloor\frac{q(b+1)-2L-1}{2N}\right\rfloor,
\quad\left\lfloor\frac{q(c_0+1)-1}{N}\right\rfloor
\]
are nonnegative and their sum exceeds r for all sufficiently large e: dividing by q gives w\_N(m+1)>t. Choose i,j,h within these capacities 
with i+j+h=r. The monomial d U\textasciicircum{}i W\textasciicircum{}(Nj) z\textasciicircum{}(Nh) lies in A\_N\textasciicircum{}r K; its 
exponent A has A\_i<q(m\_i+1). Put alpha=m-A/q, so alpha\_i>-1 and alpha in (1/q)M.

Define the R-linear map pi\_alpha on root monomials chi\textasciicircum{}u by 
pi\_alpha(chi\textasciicircum{}u)=chi\textasciicircum{}(u+alpha) if u+alpha belongs to M, and0 otherwise. Whenever the lattice condition 
holds, its coordinates are integers strictly greater than-1, hence nonnegative. It therefore maps into R, not merely its fraction field. 
Translation by an ordinary monoid exponent preserves the selection condition and proves R-linearity. Its residue-class selection and 
rescaling make it adically continuous; it extends to completed series. Applied to the chosen source root it returns chi\textasciicircum{}m. 
Stability implies chi\textasciicircum{}m belongs to K. This works for each target and every fixed L, with arbitrarily large Frobenius 
exponents. Thus H\_(N,t) is the smallest stable generically nonzero ideal and proves the formula. The strict threshold and the q-versus-q-1 
rounding are checked directly, not inferred from an asymptotic name.

Now let Q be ANY fixed proper primary ideal of R. Choose L>=1 with z\textasciicircum{}L in Q and choose N>6L+9. Set t=2/3. Since
\[
w_N((2,0,0)+(1,1,1))=3/2+3/(2N)>4/3,
\]
U belongs to tau(A\_N\textasciicircum{}(4/3)). For every0<=j<=L,
\[
w_N((0,0,j)+(1,1,1))=1/2+(j+3/2)/N<2/3.
\]
Hence no z\textasciicircum{}j, j<=L, belongs to H=tau(A\_N\textasciicircum{}(2/3)). A factorization of U z\textasciicircum{}L into two 
monomials in R has t-exponent0 and s-exponents summing to2. Each s-exponent is even, so one factor has s=t exponent0 and is 
z\textasciicircum{}j with j<=L. That factor is outside H. Monomial ideal products have ordinary monomial membership, also after completion. 
Therefore
\[
U z^L\in Q\tau(A_N^{4/3}),\qquad
U z^L\notin\tau(A_N^{2/3})^2.
\]
There is NO single primary Q for which Q tau(a\textasciicircum{}(2t)) subset tau(a\textasciicircum{}t)\textasciicircum{}2 holds for all 
genuine primary ideals a, even at the fixed rational t=2/3, on this normal nonisolated germ. Taking Q=m\textasciicircum{}h in particular 
disproves a uniform primary replacement of the Jacobian over all primary pair models. The example is normal and uses actual primary ideals; 
a nonnormal conductor or unsupported radial example is not involved.

This is a proof-route obstruction, NOT an envelope counterexample. Indeed this ring has CE over perfect odd characteristic by the actual 
finite regular cover: the full fibre has the two sign conjugates (or their coincident specialization), as follows from the qualified G331 
normal coefficient trace/full-fibre theorem. Max(g,g composed with sign) stays in C\_B, is full-fibre constant, and descends positively;
