For a Noetherian local ring \\((R,\\mathfrak m)\\), a centred real semivaluation is a map to \\([0,+\\infty]\\) satisfying \\(v(0)=+\\infty\\), \\(v(1)=0\\), multiplicativity, the ultrametric inequality, and \\(0<v(\\mathfrak m)<+\\infty\\). Its support \\(v^{-1}(+\\infty)\\) is a prime strictly below \\(\\mathfrak m\\); no minimal-support restriction is imposed. Ideal values are minima over finite generating sets. Relations between generating sets prove independence and\n\\[\nv(IJ)=v(I)+v(J),\\qquad v(I+J)=\\min\\{v(I),v(J)\\}.\n\\]\nUnits have value zero. A proper primary ideal always means primary for the marked maximal ideal.\n\nFix a proper primary ideal \\(\\mathfrak a\\). The section \\(V_{\\mathfrak a}(R)=\\{v:v(\\mathfrak a)=1\\}\\) is compact Hausdorff. Indeed semivaluation axioms and \\(v(\\mathfrak m)=1\\) are closed conditions in the compact product \\([0,+\\infty]^R\\); addition, minimum and the order relation have the required continuity/closedness. Choose \\(\\mathfrak m^r\\subset\\mathfrak a\\subset\\mathfrak m^s\\), with \\(r\\ge s\\ge1\\). Then \\(s v(\\mathfrak m)\\le v(\\mathfrak a)\\le r v(\\mathfrak m)\\). Rescaling identifies the two sections. Every primary ideal value is finite positive continuous and bounded there. For another primary ideal \\(\\mathfrak b\\),\n\\[\nH_{\\mathfrak a,\\mathfrak b}(v)=v/v(\\mathfrak b),\\qquad\nu_{\\mathfrak b}(H_{\\mathfrak a,\\mathfrak b}v)=u_{\\mathfrak a}(v)/v(\\mathfrak b).\n\\]\nThe denominator and its inverse are bounded. Substitution proves the inverse and the exact three-gauge cocycle. The centred cone is the product of its section and the positive radial coordinate \\(v(\\mathfrak a)\\); hence these sections represent its intrinsic ray quotient. Nonprimary proper ideals give only their open finite-value domain, which can be noncompact. Units and zero ideals have no level-one section.\n\nNilpotents have infinite value. Comparing \\(f+n\\) and \\((f+n)-n\\) proves that reduction preserves every semivaluation and ideal gauge. A zero-dimensional reduced local ring is a field and has empty centred boundary. For a positive-dimensional excellent reduced local ring, a penultimate prime of a saturated chain to the maximal ideal gives a one-dimensional excellent domain quotient. Its finite normalization has a local DVR factor, whose order pulls back and normalizes into the section. This proves nonemptiness. Ordinary background used throughout is lying over, prime avoidance, finite Artinian decompositions, and the quotient/finite-type-localization stability, Nagata finiteness and universal catenarity consequences of excellence. None is used to assert resolution in arbitrary characteristic.\n\nEvery finite integral injection \\(R\\hookrightarrow B\\), with \\(B\\) reduced and nonzero, gives a continuous surjective restriction \\(V_{\\mathfrak aB}(B)\\to V_{\\mathfrak a}(R)\\). Here a finite algebra has the finite union of its closed-centre sections above \\(\\mathfrak m\\). To lift \\(v\\) with support \\(\\mathfrak p\\), choose a prime \\(P\\) of \\(B\\) above \\(\\mathfrak p\\) and form the finite field extension \\(\\operatorname{Frac}(B/P)/\\operatorname{Frac}(R/\\mathfrak p)\\). Extend the valuation ring by taking the integral closure, a prime over its maximal ideal, and a dominating valuation ring. The domination assertion follows from Zorn: in a maximal dominating local subring, either adjoining \\(x\\) or \\(x^{-1}\\) leaves the maximal ideal proper. If \\(1=\\sum a_i x^{-i}\\) with all \\(a_i\\) in that ideal, multiplying by a power and dividing by \\(1-a_0\\) makes \\(x\\) integral, so lying over makes the ideal proper after adjoining \\(x\\). Localizing contradicts maximality unless one of the two elements already belongs. Intersection with the old field is the original valuation ring: an element outside it has inverse in its maximal ideal. An algebraic equation for any new nonzero field element has two least-valued terms; thus an integer multiple of its value is in the old value group. Dividing this old real value by the integer gives a well-defined order-preserving real embedding, using common multiples. Integral elements have nonnegative value by the least-term test for a monic equation. Compose with \\(B\\to B/P\\), assigning \\(P\\) infinite value. This construction first kills the support; it never extends a nonzero-support semivaluation to the original fraction field. Compactness makes restriction a quotient map.\n\nLet \\(S\\) be the finite normalization of an excellent reduced \\(R\\), and \\(\\mathfrak c=(R:S)\\). Clearing denominators of finitely many generators of \\(S\\) gives a regular conductor element. The conductor is an ideal of both rings and\n\\[\nR=S\\times_{S/\\mathfrak c}(R/\\mathfrak c).\n\\]\nAn element of \\(S\\) whose residue comes from \\(R\\) differs from an element of \\(R\\) by an element of \\(\\mathfrak c\\), proving this identity. The normalization boundary is the finite disjoint union of local normal centres above \\(\\mathfrak m\\). Idempotents choose a minimal component; localization at its centre changes no values of denominators. Chinese remainder elements separating the finitely many centres, and their complements, have open positive-value loci selecting these pieces. The pieces are therefore clopen. Branches mean these local centres, not merely minimal primes.\n\nIf \\(v(\\mathfrak c)<+\\infty\\), choose \\(c\\in\\mathfrak c\\) of finite value. Every lift satisfies \\(w(s)=v(cs)-v(c)\\), so it is unique. The subtracted number is finite. If \\(v(\\mathfrak c)=+\\infty\\), all lifts kill the conductor, and equality after restriction \\(S/\\mathfrak c\\to R/\\mathfrak c\\) is exactly their identification. This infinity stratum is closed; its finite complement is open, without a closedness claim. A fibre-constant continuous function descends continuously by the compact quotient. A fibre-constant extended nonpositive upper semicontinuous function descends upper semicontinuously: its closed superlevel sets have compact, hence closed, images. These assertions alone supply no positivity descent.\n\nCompletion preserves the entire boundary for every Noetherian local ring. For \\(F\\in\\widehat R\\), choose representatives \\(F_N\\) modulo \\(\\mathfrak m^N\\), and put \\(d=v(\\mathfrak m)>0\\). Differences have value at least \\(Nd\\). If some \\(v(F_N)<Nd\\), later values stabilize; otherwise they tend to infinity. Define \\(\\widehat v(F)\\) by this limit. It is independent of representatives and satisfies\n\\[\n\\min\\{\\widehat v(F),Nd\\}=\\min\\{v(F_N),Nd\\}.\n\\]\nApplying this to sums and products proves all axioms and uniqueness, including infinite values; completed units have unit representatives. Compose with \\(q(t)=t/(1+t)\\), \\(q(+\\infty)=1\\). The displayed continuous truncations have uniform error at most \\((1+N/r)^{-1}\\), because \\(d\\ge1/r\\). Thus completed evaluation is continuous and completion restriction is a homeomorphism. Every completed primary \\(J\\) contains \\(\\widehat{\\mathfrak m}^N\\). Representatives modulo that power of its generators belong to \\(J\\cap R\\) and, with the boundary power, generate \\(J\\). Hence \\(J=(J\\cap R)\\widehat R\\). The quotient isomorphism also proves contraction of an extended primary ideal recovers it. Unit-or-primary profiles and their uniform and decreasing classes therefore agree under completion. No equivalence of geometric model categories is asserted.\n\nThis is a mathematical argument with the stated ordinary background. def escape(t):
    substitutions = {'\\':r'\textbackslash{}', '{':r'\{', '}':r'\}',
                     '$':r'\$', '&':r'\&', '%':r'\%', '#':r'\#', '_':r'\_',
                     '^':r'\textasciicircum{}', '~':r'\textasciitilde{}',
                     '<':r'\textless{}', '>':r'\textgreater{}'}
    return ''.join(substitutions.get(c,c) for c in t)

===== WHOLE SUPPLIED INERT MATHEMATICAL DATA 18: 018-native-program-diagnostics.py.DATA.txt =====

"""Small exact diagnostics for NEW formulas. No supplied program is imported.

This tests explicit finite monomials and rational coordinates only. It does
not implement the geometric cone, prove comparison, or certify envelopes.
"""
from fractions import Fraction
from itertools import product
from math import inf, ceil
from pathlib import Path
import json

F = Fraction
HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
(HERE / 'reports').mkdir(exist_ok=True)
weights = [F(1), F(3, 2), F(2), F(3), F(7), inf]
cases = []
for branch in [1, 2]:
    for s, t in product(weights, repeat=2):
        if min(s, t) == 1:
            cases.append((branch, s, t))

def value(exp, vals):
    # 0 * infinity means a variable is absent, not an undefined product.
    return sum(e * v for e, v in zip(exp, vals) if e)

def minimum(gens, vals):
    return min(value(e, vals) for e in gens)

def power_m(n):
    return [(i, j, n-i-j) for i in range(n+1)
            for j in range(n-i+1) if not (i and j)]

def contains(gens, exp):
    return any(all(e >= g for e, g in zip(exp, gen)) for gen in gens)

profile_checks = membership_checks = witness_checks = 0
largest_gap = F(0)
for m in range(1, 25):
    a = (m+1)//2
    canonical = [(0, 0, m)] + [(i, 0, a-i) for i in range(1, a+1)]
    canonical += [(0, j, m-j) for j in range(1, m+1)]
    tentative = power_m(2*m) + [(i+2, j, k) for i, j, k in power_m(m) if not j]
    for branch, s, t in cases:
        vals = (s, inf, t) if branch == 1 else (inf, s, t)
        actual_canonical = minimum(canonical, vals)
        expected_canonical = min(m*t, s+a-1) if branch == 1 else m
        assert actual_canonical == expected_canonical
        actual_tentative = -minimum(tentative, vals)/(2*m)
        expected_tentative = max(F(-1), -F(1, 2)-s/m) if branch == 1 else F(-1)
        assert actual_tentative == expected_tentative
        obstacle = -F(1, 2) if branch == 1 else -F(1, 2)- (0 if s == inf else 1/(2*s))
        signed_model = F(-1, 2) if branch == 1 else min(s, 2)/2-F(3, 2)
        assert actual_tentative <= obstacle and actual_tentative <= signed_model
        raw = F(-1, 2) if branch == 1 and s != inf else F(-1)
        gap = raw + actual_canonical/m
        assert 0 <= gap <= F(1, 2)
        largest_gap = max(largest_gap, gap)
        profile_checks += 1
    witness_s = m-a+1
    assert -minimum(canonical, (witness_s, inf, 1))/m == -1
    witness_checks += 1
    for i, j in product(range(2*m+1), repeat=2):
        for branch in [1, 2]:
            exp = (i, 0, j) if branch == 1 else (0, i, j)
            expected = j >= m if i == 0 else i+j >= (a if branch == 1 else m)
            assert contains(canonical, exp) == expected
            membership_checks += 1

truncation_checks = 0
for H, B, n, s in product([F(-1, 2), F(-1), F(-3)],
                         [F(-1), F(-2), F(-4)], [1, 2, 7], weights):
    if B > H:
        continue
    N = max(1, ceil(n*(H-B)))
    lhs = max(B, H-s/n)
    rhs = max(B, H-min(s, N)/n)
    assert lhs == rhs
    truncation_checks += 1

def encode(x):
    return 'infinity' if x == inf else str(x)

inputs = {'m_range': [1, 24], 'weights': list(map(encode, weights)),
          'normalized_cases': [[b, encode(s), encode(t)] for b,s,t in cases],
          'monomial_box': '0<=i,j<=2m on each nonzero component monomial',
          'limitations': 'Finite monomial/value arithmetic only; all-support and geometric proofs are n1--n4.'}
result = {'status': 'PASS', 'profile_cases': len(cases),
          'profile_checks': profile_checks, 'monomial_membership_checks': membership_checks,
          'exact_gap_witness_degrees': witness_checks,
          'largest_sampled_canonical_gap': str(largest_gap),
          'truncation_identity_checks': truncation_checks,
          'mathematical_certification': False}
(HERE/'diagnostics-input.json').write_text(json.dumps(inputs, indent=2)+'\n')
(HERE/'reports/diagnostics.json').write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2)+'\n')
print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))

           'P12.3-ROOT416-normal-surface-resolution-and-primary-model-source']):
        body=Path(rec['path']).read_bytes()

        exclusion_count+=1

        'incoming_source_bytes':len(source),

       for p in HERE.rglob('*') if p.is_file() and p.name!='own-hashes.json'
       and p.relative_to(HERE).parts[0] not in ['.git','.aws','.codex','.agents']}
